Interpretation of the meaning: «Whichever woman asks her husband for the talaaq without any [valid] reason, the fragrance of Paradise is haraam (forbidden) for her.»
Because this is a matter that makes the marriage unstable. And some examples of the reasons for which the woman thinks she can ask for the talaaq:
«My husband does not give me much attention.» What is that «not much attention» according to you, dear sister? «I think my husband is with his friends a lot; he should divide his attention between me and his friends, for example three days with the friends and four days with his wife.»
«I think my husband comes home much too late; he always comes after one o'clock [at night], and therefore I want to be divorced from him.»
These are not reasons. For it is not the intention that the man sits at home all day with the woman, or that the woman determines for the man how much [time] he sits with her. What is the correct proportion in this? That the man gives the woman, in quality and quantity, the right attention she needs according to his means. If he is someone who — in particular — travels very much, then the woman should take that into consideration and be patient. And the astute, vigilant woman makes her husband long for her while he is far from her, by means of her beautiful words and by means of the beautiful things she says to him. So instead of going and getting annoyed, thereby hurting the man and having no patience, she makes sure that the man is with her as much as possible by means of the right communication, the right allurement, and the right adornment. For you allure/adorn yourself for your husband by means of your femininity. That is the 3ibaadah that should be there at that moment. [But] when you go demanding this attention with screaming and cursing, and «if you do not come home I will change the lock» — [that is wrong]. [There are] sisters who have thrown their husbands out of the house merely because they come home late. So it is important that the woman receives the attention she needs for her cultivation and her attunement to leading the family, for her companionship, for the sexual attention, and for the emotional attention. Not that the woman goes and determines this herself. For the woman should not arrange this in this way.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says (declared authentic and narrated by — among others — Imaam at-Tirmidhie): «المُختلِعاتُ هنّ المنافقات». Interpretation of the meaning: «The women who seek khul3 [without valid reason], they are the hypocrites.» And when the teacher looks back on more than twenty years [spent] in his field, he sees that most of those who asked for the talaaq indeed also [ended up] in misery afterwards. Even more so, that the signs of nifaaq (hypocrisy) are also seen/recognised in them. And they — usually — do not have a correct/good reason for requesting this khul3 (talaaq).
And it belongs to the rights of the man that his wife preserves their marital relationship and does not ask for the talaaq.
Questions
Question: The last-mentioned hadieth, does it apply to the women who ask for khul3 without a valid reason? Or to every woman who asks for khul3?
The answer: To the women [who ask for it] without a valid reason. For 50% [of the reasons] is an invalid reason: «I cannot stand him anymore». They then go to certain people who — for example — have some knowledge but do not have much knowledge of the cases relating to marriage. They then say to her: «not being able to stand him is a valid reason». That is incorrect. Based on a hadieth from the time of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam: one of the women came to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and said: «O Messenger of Allaah, I want to ask for khul3.» He asks: why? She says: «I cannot stand him because of his appearance.» For this man had an ugly appearance. She could not have intercourse with him [i.e. consummate the marriage as the woman consummates it]. At that moment the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said to her: «Will you return to him his dowry [mahr (dower)]?» She said: yes, whereupon the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam separated them. So this concerns appearance. And this woman had tried, but [it] did not work. And usually it happens that the woman refuses to obey the man, after he admonishes her and explains to her that she must stop that. She then refuses to trample on her egoism [her arrogance], and does not go and obey her husband. Some women paint a beautiful story around [the matter] and say: «I cannot fulfil my husband's rights, and therefore I cannot stay with him.» This is a pitfall. If she is granted the khul3, she can show remorse, but she will not be able to fulfil one of the important conditions of tawbah, and thereby risks that her tawbah is not accepted; because she can no longer put [the matter] right. For she refuses to obey her husband, and that is also no longer possible because she has left the marriage. That is exactly the reason why the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam calls the women who ask for khul3 hypocrites. That is [that she is engaged in] embellishing a matter; they then go looking among the people of knowledge for someone who will tell [them] that it is a [valid] reason so that she gets her khul3 after all; therefore she is a hypocrite, while the reason is a completely different reason. That is a danger, and therefore we should beware of it.
What is a valid reason?
That the man does not give her various rights. For example that the man does not give her her sexual right (that he has forsaken her for a very long period).
That the man has left her, does not spend on her, and no longer asks after her. If that has truly been established for a long period (more than four months), then she has the right to ask for khul3.
That she finds him [so] ugly that she cannot share the bed with him, and that she — without [the khul3] — would fall into zina (fornication). Therefore look well at your husband before you marry; because when you marry, [the matter] is serious.
These are reasons for which you can ask for khul3.
And many women [come] to people of knowledge and say: «yes, my husband does not spend on me». Then some persons who do not have much experience with this say: «yes, that is allowed [to ask for khul3]». That is not correct. For first it should be looked at carefully what was agreed between the man and the woman. What does the woman mean by not being provided for? Is [it] that she does not get the four jackets she wanted to get, but two, because he has little money, or is [it] that he does not spend on her at all while [maintenance] was agreed upon? If it was agreed that he would not spend on her the first and second year, then she should accept that, and khul3 cannot be requested. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam called marriage «a solemn covenant». So it is a very serious relationship that should also be taken very seriously.
Question: When your family does not accept a small wedding, especially your parents, how do you deal with this?
The answer: When you accept it, that is enough. When you [stand] behind your husband, that is enough. Then you both go and look together at how you will solve it. The point is that you are behind your husband, not behind your parents with regard to spending a lot on the wedding. Can the two of you solve it together, can the parents solve it, is there another possibility, another form of a big wedding? And one of the brothers solved [the matter] by making a lot of rice, and they slaughtered a sheep. In this way they were also able to invite many brothers and sisters. So [one] dish is enough. And the teacher says this [from] what he has seen around him and from his own experience.
Question: I now have an image that I — as a woman — can enter the Fire very quickly. Because with the angry look at my husband I commit a great sin. How should I deal with this? Can you give me more [explanation] on this?
The answer: That image is good, and it means that you should cultivate yourself well by revering your husband and not giving an angry look. And [there is] also another image: the more you please your husband, the higher your side [in the scale] is, [such that] you can enter Paradise in a high position. That image — that you risk being punished when you hurt your husband — is an important image; because it keeps you away from every form of hurting your husband. And another image: «I will go — precisely — love to do what my husband loves, and do the best that he finds pleasing before he asks for it, in order to enter Paradise». So it is not [enough] to have one image; rather, [have] both images so that you can form a balance between the two matters with them.
Question: Is [there] a hadieth about 3aa-ishah [in which] she was jealous of KHadiedjah?
The answer: 3aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa (may Allaah be pleased with her) says: Haalah bint KHuwaylid, the sister of KHadiedjah, asked permission to enter upon the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. Then the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam recognised the way KHadiedjah used to ask permission. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was comforted by that. He said: «O Allaah, Haalah!» He rejoiced, and so I became jealous — said 3aa-ishah — and I said: «What do you keep mentioning of an old woman among the old women of Quraysh, who has died, while Allaah has given you someone better than her».
And 3aa-ishah says in another hadieth: «I was never as jealous of anyone as I was of KHadiedjah» [while she had already died], before he married me, when I heard him mention her, and I heard from Allaah that he should give her the glad tidings of a house in Paradise.
And among the narrated ahaadieth is that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «Have I been given someone better than her? She believed in me when the people disbelieved me, and she affirmed my truthfulness when the people denied me, and she supported me [accompanied and helped me] with her wealth when the people withheld from me, and Allaah granted me her children and withheld from me the children of others». For all the other children of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam died during the lifetime of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam except [the children] of KHadiedjah. And among her children is Faatimah. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam loved KHadiedjah radiyallaahu 3anhaa very greatly. So that was a form of loyalty to her, and for the sake of what she did for the da3wah. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam once said to 3aa-ishah: «I have truly been granted the love of her».
Question: May the woman ask the man about his salary while they are still in the acquaintance phase (before marriage)? And is this something you advise? Or is it better to «trust» the man that he is able to provide for the woman?
The answer: Of course that is allowed. [However,] that is not what the teacher advises. The teacher makes clear that the woman can ask whether he can estimate [for himself] whether he can provide for her with his salary; because the woman should be content with little.
Question: Can you mention the names of the children of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam (other than the children of KHadiedjah, and other than his son Ibraahiem)?
The answer: Al-Qaasim (the son of KHadiedjah). [He] died. He was born before the prophethood and died when he was two years old. And 3abdullaah. And Ibraahiem (born in al-Madienah). He is the last of his sons, and he died when he was seventeen months old. And his daughters: Zaynab (she is the eldest of the daughters of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and she is from KHadiedjah). And Ruqayyah (she is the wife of 3uthmaan). And Umm Kulthoem (she too was one of the wives of 3uthmaan after Ruqayyah had died, and therefore 3uthmaan was called Dhoe an-Noerayn (the possessor of the two lights)). And Faatimah (she is the youngest of the daughters, and she is the wife of 3alie ibn Abie Taalib). And the offspring of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was limited to the offspring of Faatimah and 3alie, and among them are al-Hasan and al-Husayn. [Note: in the original, the name of the husband of Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthoem appeared corrupted as «Luqmaan»; the unanimously agreed-upon correct [name] is 3uthmaan ibn 3affaan radiyallaahu 3anhu (may Allaah be pleased with him), Dhoe an-Noerayn, so it has been set down correctly.]
Question: So the Prophet had no children from his other wives?
The answer: The sons — in particular — died earlier [prematurely] so that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam would — in any case — have no successors/offspring from his direct line of succession, that is to say, so that the people would not say «he is the one who should come after us», [whereby it] would become a form of kingship in which the inheritance would be «the son of so-and-so and the son of so-and-so». That is not what Islaam came for. [Rather,] whoever has more knowledge is [the one who] rules. That is among the reasons why Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa caused the sons of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam to die. And his offspring came from Faatimah, and she is also the most beloved of his daughters to him sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And all the children are from KHadiedjah except Ibraahiem, for he is from Maariyah al-Qibtiyyah. And all the children died during the lifetime of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam except Faatimah. For she died six months after the death of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
Question: Are the man and the woman in Paradise still married?
The answer: If they die [while] married, then yes.
Question: The sister has a question about the annoyed look from the wife towards the husband. She wondered whether the woman also sins if she gives an annoyed look without the man doing anything?
The answer: If your wife is angry with the man, or has given an annoyed look, then she is sinning. And the fact that men make a joke of it — that is noble behaviour from the man, without responding angrily. That some men joke about it, or deal with it in a good way by dealing with it in a laughing way — is something that is commendable for the man with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. But the woman at that moment is in the process of [committing] a sin, especially if she does it near her children. For the authority of the man and the woman is then undermined by the children, so that the tarbiyah is then not possible.
Questions
Question: Two sisters live in Nijmegen. We are forced to travel without a mahram (male relative whom one is forbidden to marry) to the conference, and we wanted to travel together in [one] car; what do you advise us to do? Travelling together without a mahram, or is it better after all to receive the conference lessons via Skype?
The answer: The advice is that you take your mahram with you; because the mahram will be able to benefit greatly from it. If the men come along with you, that is — precisely — good. And it is something that does not occur often, but twice a year, and unlike previous years. And the advice remains: make sure you convince a mahram to come along after all. If that is not possible, then it is not permissible to travel for this, as long as you can also receive the lessons via Skype.
Question: A sister helps someone a lot, and the reverse does not happen. What should she do then?
The answer: First you should examine your intention with which you help them. When the intention is a correct (sincere) intention, you will not ask this question. For with a sincere intention it does not matter whether you help someone [even] if they do not help you. When you only want to obtain the reward of Allaah, then we do not expect anything in return or any form of help in exchange for the help we offer; because our reward is the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and the hasanaat (good deeds) that we will see with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. So examine your intention first; because the fact that you are asking this question means that your intention was not sincere. The moment you make your intention sincere, it does not matter whether people help you or not.
Question: Do you know the al-Karama mosque in Amsterdam, and do you advise receiving lessons [there] or not?
[The teacher asks:] Which imaam [is there]? She does not know which imaam is there. [He said:] If you ask about the imaam there, or the person who gives the knowledge (for that is what matters most), then the teacher can answer that. The teacher Aboe Mu3aawiyah is on the internet. She sends the link to the teacher.
Question: I have a question about brand clothing. In my environment people say that Nike — for example — is not permissible. What is the correct Islamic ruling on this?
The answer: In general, wearing Nike is permissible as long as it does not contain things that Islaam has not permitted; but if you can avoid such a brand, that is better. But that [it is said] that it is not permissible to wear a shoe from Nike without there being something [in]correct about that specific shoe — that we cannot do.
And with regard to the rights and duties of the man and the woman, it is important that we know that these are the minimum matters [the lowest level] of how the man and the woman should deal with one another. For they comprise the minimum rights of the man and the woman. And that does not mean that this is the most and best way of dealing with one another.
We are going to look: what improves the relationship between the man and the woman? What brings the man and the woman closer to one another? By what are quarrels, gaps and problems avoided? And it is important that we know that everyone who wants the tranquillity, happiness and blessing of marriage, it is important [for him] to fulfil these rights that he has covered in the past lessons. Both the man and the woman. Even more so, that one thereby obtains an eternal happiness all the way to Paradise, and that one fulfils these rights for the sake of Allaah, not in order to obtain the rights from the other. For it is not a trade-off, nor a negotiation, as the teacher has said several times. It is only [seeking] the pleasure of Allaah by means of fulfilling these rights.
And it is important — when one of these rights is violated once on a small level — that one does not jump up and say «my right is being violated». Rather, one should discuss this with the other for the sake of Allaah in a calm manner. And it is best to overlook it; because making an issue of it causes annoyance between the man and the woman. For making an issue out of a small matter opens the door of the shaytaan.
And among the wisdoms in marriage and in the relationship is that when [the matter] is very small and not worth mentioning, it is overlooked, and that one also does not feel the weight of [counting] oneself as noble — for that also causes annoyance. That you say: «I am noble, I will overlook this.» That is not patience, but a form of arrogance. Thereby the annoyance grows much bigger. So do not go presenting yourself [in the guise of] the noble one. Make sure you have patience for the sake of Allaah, and also truly forget it.
Unless [the matter] is worth mentioning, big, recurring, [and] admonishment is given [about it] and after the admonishment there is still no improvement — then we proceed to other steps that we will learn later, in shaa-e Allaah.
And fulfilling these rights causes love and affection towards one another. Thereby the Muslim homes are improved, and thereby the whole society will be improved. And the non-Muslims too will partake of this good; because our children will then be raised in the right way.
And when we speak about these rights and duties, we should know that we are part of this society, which can [make] a positive contribution or a negative contribution.
And besides that, it is very important that the mothers and fathers raise their children in preparation for marriage with these rights. What we are doing now in the lesson — should — in reality — be done by the father and the mother from an early age. From when the child is two, three or four years old. That the child learns how to honour the elders, how to give them their rights, how to keep secrets, how not to expose the 3awrah (parts of the body that must be covered). These are matters the child should be raised with. For when the child is raised with this, many problems will be avoided [in which] many sisters and brothers now [end up]. So our sons and daughters should be raised with these rights and duties so that they are easily made aware of them before they marry. Then when they marry, you only need to remind them of these rights.
And the father and mother who have not raised their children with these rights and duties, [but] do not even remind them [of them], and are occupied [only] with school or private tutoring — when the child is twenty-one they say «go and get a profession» — then you are [at that moment] in the process of destroying your child, not [in the process of] equipping him for marriage so that he can be a cornerstone that completes the rest of the community.
And among the things a righteous mother in the past advised her daughter is that she said to her: «O my little daughter, the wasiyyah (counsel/admonition) is very important, and it is a reminder for the one who forgets, and a help for the sensible one. If any woman could do without a husband — because she also has parents, and because she is in great need of them — then I would be the most able of all people to do without that [i.e. then I should have been able to do without my husband for your sake], but women were created for men, and for them [women] men were also created. O my little daughter, you have left the environment from which you came, and you have left behind the nest in which you grew up, to the place of [a person] you do not know or did not know before, and a companion with whom you are not yet familiar. And this man has — by means of this contract (the marriage contract) — become your master and overseer. Be a servant to him and he will be a servant to you (or like a servant), and observe for him ten qualities and he will raise you high. As for the first: submission to him with contentment and sufficiency, and listening to him well and obedience. And the third and the fourth: paying good attention to the place of his eye and his nose, so that he sees nothing ugly from you, and smells nothing unpleasant from you, and let him smell from you the finest you have. And the fifth and the sixth: paying good attention to his sleeping time and his eating time. For when he is very hungry, [he becomes angry], and when he is disturbed in his sleep, that makes him angry. And the seventh and the eighth: watching over his wealth, and watching over his children. And the comprehensive conduct with regard to his wealth is that you manage well, and with regard to his children that you carry out the right administration (that is — for example — that you prepare the children for the arrival of their father, and that you do not let the children scream, and do not let their father find them in a screaming or hysterical state when he enters the house. Make sure that [the atmosphere] at that moment is calm, that they are occupied, that they are asleep, or [that] they are admonished to calm down; because their father is coming shortly). And the ninth and the tenth: never disobey him, and never spread a secret of his; for if you disobey him, you break his heart, and if you spread one of his secrets, you are not safe from his scheming [betrayal]. And do not show joy [while he is troubled], nor sadness [while he is joyful].»
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍۢ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا ۝٧٤﴾ [Soerat Al-Furqaan, verse 74]. Interpretation of the meaning: «And those who say: our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring a coolness for the eyes, and make us an example for the God-fearing.»
And these words from the mother we should pass on to our daughters, and raise our daughters with them, and remind them of them. And that is possible when we are a good example for our children, and when we think well of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and do not think «that is not possible». For that means that you either do not know how [it] should [be done], or do not want it. Therefore it is important that we work on this [strive in it], and not carelessly cast aside [neglect] the rights as being merely rights of the man and the woman, and leave the matter at that, and only claim your right when you marry. No, for that is not how [it] should [be].
Discuss this with your children, and tell your children what the rights and duties of the man and the woman are, and go and prepare them for it by means of the tarbiyah. Thereby we can reach a better culture, in shaa-e Allaah.
Very many women do not understand this, and otherwise they would live like a queen — said the teacher. And that will be explained later.
If you position yourself humbly towards your husband, and always revere your husband as well, and also treat him as your master — then his heart is in your hand, and you can knead it as you wish, and you can say what you wish, and he will then follow what you love. That is — in reality — a secret recipe that is also difficult for very many women to put together.
Take your husband's heart and he will do what you wish, within the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. Do you want your husband to truly do more than merely be considerate of you, [and] to love what you love? Then say to him: «you are my master, you are my leader, your command is obeyed» — and that should also be carried out literally. When he speaks, open your ears and your heart to what he is speaking about.
Listen to his words, not mere hearing. For [otherwise] the heart at that moment is not with the man. When you open your ears completely, and place your focus on your husband, and humble yourself before your husband — then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has decreed that at that moment you [have] your husband's heart in your hand, and that you can knead it as you wish. And some women have succeeded in this, and others have — unfortunately — failed in it because the shaytaan gained the upper hand. And some women have succeeded and have kept their husbands away from the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. The woman then says to the man: «I will miss you», whereupon the man stays at home because he misses his wife. That is a woman who has failed, because she has abused that power. So that power you can obtain, but you should use it for good.
And something quite important that the teacher will share shortly: these are women whose existence is becoming ever rarer. One of the women says: «If I want to wake my husband from sleep for his prayer, I wash my hand with water so that it becomes cold, then I perfume it with the finest perfume my husband finds pleasing; so when my hand touches him with that coldness (his body), he smells that perfume, and he gets up for the prayer.» That is a woman who has won her husband's heart with that.
And another woman said: «I won my husband's heart with the following: my husband once said to me in a loud voice: I am going to eat/have lunch with my friends. Do you need anything, woman? Then I said: fine, but do not come late; because the electricity will be cut off. He turned around and said: how do you know the electricity will be cut off? I say that [because] the moment you leave the house, [the house] here becomes dark, and when you enter, you light up the house, and everything in me is lit up.»
And a third woman said: «I won my husband's heart by means of the following: I accustomed my husband to the following: when he travelled with his friends, I would put a love letter in his clothes without him knowing, in which I tell him about my feelings for him at the moment he departs from me, and [about the fact] that my children too can sometimes come between me and him so that we cannot be loving together. And on one occasion there came a day when I was not pleased about his travelling; at that moment I did not write him a love letter. He went searching the whole [time], and said when he returned: I left nothing of my clothes, or my bag, without searching in it (that is, I searched everywhere) for your letter you have accustomed me to. I searched the bag three times and saw nothing.» Then this woman said: at that moment I regretted not having given him a love letter, and I promised myself that when I have a good habit, I will not stop this good habit.
So the woman can make of her house a paradise that her husband does not want to leave, and she can also make it a hell that her husband cannot bear, and [whereby] he seeks his way out every time. These are matters from which the married women should draw a lesson, and which the unmarried women should learn, and which the mothers should hand down/pass on to their children.
These women are sisters in our time. So they are astute sisters.
And the teacher advises the sisters to stay at home as much as possible. Go to your relatives, go to your acquaintances. Maintain the ties of kinship, and do that at home. And do not go out much; rather, it is best not [to go out] at all if it is not necessary.
Questions
Question: Is it known who gave this magnificent wasiyyah to her daughter?
The answer: Umaamah bint al-Haarith, the daughter of al-Haarith. When her daughter (Umm Iyaas bint 3awf ash-SHaybaanie) married 3amr ibn Hudjr.
Question: What do you advise the sisters who go on holiday and may encounter many forms of fitnah (temptation/trial)?
The answer: On a sunny day the temptations weigh very heavily, and that is not right. And it is good for [one] to have recreation, there is no harm in that, but try to do it in a halaal way. And try [to pass on] what we have received in lessons, pass it on as well; repeat the lessons for yourself. And do not let [anyone] make you believe that you are [about] to become extreme, or that you take [things] too heavily. And perform the da3wah.
Question: What do you advise the sisters who do not go on holiday but are on a break?
The answer: Go and review the material again, make sure you have something to do, and if you really have time, make sure you devote yourself to the da3wah. And [there is] also a summer school that still needs help.
Question: Has the thinking chart/mind map also been made in Arabic?
The answer: No, that has not yet been accomplished, but they want to do that, in shaa-e Allaah. And in English too they still want to do it. If anyone can translate it into English...
We will receive educational teachings from this soerah (Soerat Al-Kahf) during the conference.
Homework
We will discuss the homework in two weeks in the application.
Organise your notes.
Once again the same for the married women: discussing these rights that we have covered with their husbands, and checking whether they carry them out well and what they should also do for that. And for the unmarried sisters it is important that they already start preparing themselves for this.
That one discusses these ten counsels (from the mother to the daughter) — for the married woman, [she discusses them] with their husbands and also puts them into practice. And if they are not yet doing so, then they should check how to improve them. And for the unmarried woman, [that she discusses them] with her parents; for perhaps [things] will go better with her parents, and the parents will also be delighted by what we are learning, and they too will start training themselves in realising this by also practising it with the parents. First discuss with the father and the mother how things stand with these matters/counsels. Say to them: we have learned such-and-such, and try to emphasise the positive things in this, and practise these counsels with your parents.
Lesson thirty — Sunday 9 September 2018
Summary of the last lessons before the summer break
The rights of the woman
That the man treats the woman in/with goodness. And all the other rights are a branch of this good treatment.
That the man has patience with the woman, and that he pardons her for the (general/daily) mistakes she commits towards him. Step 1: teaching (teach her that what she did is not correct, even if you thought she knows that). Step 2: reminding (by means of a wink of the eye, or a joke, or biting the upper/lower lip, or frowning, or staring). Step 3: admonishing. Step 4: rebuking. Step 5: punishing.
That the man protects the woman in all aspects of what causes her harm: in her honour, or in her cultivation, in her way of thinking, in her feelings, in her behaviour, in her physical health, in her reputation, in her chastity, and also in what influences her (because that watches over her cultivation and her way of thinking).
That he gives her the knowledge she needs and that is obligatory for her (Islamic and general knowledge).
That he commands her to practise the religion of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
That he gives her permission to go to the mosque (without her neglecting her duties, and without her travelling without a mahram).
That he does not expose her secrets, and does not mention her bad qualities in the presence of another.
That he consults her in the matters that fall within the boundaries of the rights and duties of both, and in which she also has a right of decision, for example having children.
That he does not stay outside the house and come home late at night without need, [whereby] she worries about him, and without letting her know that he is fine.
That the man gives the woman the right attention (and the sexual attention as well).
That the man is just between all his wives (if he is married to multiple women), and that he treats her justly [in comparison] to his other wives.
The rights of the man
The woman should acknowledge the high position of the man, realise it and fulfil it. And «qawwaamoen» means two things: the correcting and the evaluating. So men are the ones who correct, the educators, and the leaders over women.
The woman should guard and protect the honour of her husband. And she should also guard and protect her own honour, her chastity, her property and her children.
The woman should beautify herself for her husband, and also smile at him and not frown, and be spontaneous, and not appear to him in a way he detests.
The woman should stay in his house, and not leave the house except with his permission.
The woman should not let anyone into his house except those for whom he gives permission and whom he likes.
The woman should guard his property, and not spend anything from it except with his permission (a general or specific permission), and not spend from her own property unless the man has given permission for it.
That she does not perform a voluntary fast without his permission while he is present.
When she spends on her husband, that she does not talk about it afterwards, and that she does not humiliate him by saying «I did this for you».
That the woman accepts the little that her husband has if her husband is poor, and that she accepts what is available, and that she does not burden him/ask him to spend more than he can bear.
That the woman raises his children (and her children) in the right way, and that she has patience with that, and that she does not go humiliating them in his presence, or insulting them, or screaming at them, or invoking [curses] against them; because that hurts him.
That the woman treats well the people whom he loves and who are close to him, for example his parents and his acquaintances.
When her husband calls her, she hastens to him.
That she conceals his secrets, and does not spread anything of them.
That she preserves the relationship with him as long as there is no reason to leave him or ask for the talaaq.
Counsels of a mother to her daughter
«O my little daughter, the wasiyyah is very important, and it is a reminder for the one who forgets, and a help for the sensible one. If any woman could do without a husband — because she also has parents, and because she is in great need of him — then I would be the most able of all people to do without that, but women were created for men, and for them [women] men were also created. O my little daughter, you have left the environment from which you came, and you have left behind the nest in which you grew up, to the place of [a person] you do not know or did not know before, and a companion with whom you are not yet familiar. And this man has — by means of this contract (the marriage contract) — become your master and overseer. Be a servant to him and he will be a servant to you (or like a servant), and observe for him ten qualities and he will raise you high. As for the first: submission to him with contentment and sufficiency (1), and listening to him well and obedience (2). And the third and the fourth: paying good attention to the place of his eye and his nose, so that he sees nothing ugly from you (3), and smells nothing unpleasant from you (4), and let him smell from you the finest you have. And the fifth and the sixth: paying good attention to his sleeping time (5), and his eating time (6). For when he is very hungry, [he becomes angry], and when he is disturbed in his sleep, that makes him angry. And the seventh and the eighth: watching over his wealth (7), and watching over his children (8). And the comprehensive conduct with regard to his wealth is that you manage well, and with regard to his children that you carry out the right administration (that is — for example — that you prepare the children for the arrival of their father, and that you do not let the children scream, and do not let their father find them in a screaming or hysterical state when he enters the house; make sure that [the atmosphere] at that moment is calm, that they are occupied, that they are asleep, or [that] they are admonished to calm down; because their father is coming shortly). And the ninth and the tenth: never disobey him (9), and never spread a secret of his (10); for if you disobey him, you break his heart, and if you spread one of his secrets, you are not safe from his scheming. And do not show joy [while he is troubled], nor sadness [while he is joyful].»
The beginning of lesson thirty
All [five sisters present] have a microphone except sister Sumayyah.
What was the connection with these lessons during the break? Apart from the morning and evening adhkaar (remembrances of Allaah). Was the mindset/feeling/message [conveyed] in a [different] way [i.e. was what we learned applied]?
The reaction of sister 1
A sister made clear that during the break she went through all the lessons once more and tried to arrange them once more. For during the break she had more time to look at that extra. And she is not yet completely finished with it, but she can — in shaa-e Allaah — still find time for it. And on a personal level there was an incident that was related to the lessons discussed in the lesson material. So the sister went and looked up that material related to it, and applied it in practice in the situation she was in. That was extremely helpful.
The teacher: With regard to free time and self-management, how did you manage yourself with that, with regard to what you received? The sister makes clear that during the break — because there were no lessons — she found [it] difficult, and she longed intensely for the lessons. She noticed that she had a need to receive lessons again. So she started a small group with some converts [new Muslims] to look together once a week at the lessons of basic 3aqiedah (creed) (which were [available] on «Islam Planning Online»). To stay occupied with cultivating herself, and to discuss with one another how someone saw something. That is, by repeating the lessons of the knowledge of family affairs by herself, and thinking about them again because time has passed over them. And she now looks at them more clearly than she did at the time.
The reaction of sister 2
With regard to the lessons, how she applied them during the break: she was in Morocco for a long period, and with regard to marriage she held many conversations about it there in Morocco. She noticed that the view of very many sisters there — especially the relatives — on marriage has changed. They have started thinking differently about the role of the man, and that shocked her. She reminded them of the role of the man. They have started thinking about the man in a more Western way. She did not have that image of Morocco, but that has changed very much over the years among the sisters she spoke with.
The teacher: That is a widespread phenomenon occurring in many Islamic countries. For in the media, in the magazines and among the families, the non-Islamic way of thinking is being transmitted. When the shaytaan comes to them [directly], they will not accept it, but by means of «participation», «the freedom of the woman» and «the value of the woman» — [a person] is also influenced in his thinking, so that one — in the end — goes and thinks in that way and behaves in that way.
The sister: With regard to spending free time on the holiday, she tried to give [it] an Islamic touch. When she goes to the city [town], she still tries to visit a mosque. In the year 1920 a battle took place in the north of Morocco. And she thought it was beautiful to see that [things] could also have gone differently. And she tries to do that in Morocco as well and in other places. They went to a mosque in Fes.
The teacher: With regard to the sisters who [came] from the Netherlands, did you also perform da3wah with that? [The answer:] Mostly towards the relatives. And she did not specifically invite them to also receive the lessons of the knowledge of family affairs.
The teacher: It is important that attention be paid to encouraging people to receive more lessons (basic 3aqiedah, the knowledge of family affairs) so that they develop themselves and grow in this religion. Then you will notice that many messages you have said often do not get through, but through the lessons they do — yes — improve, change, and go and convey themselves the message that you convey. So it is important that people be motivated towards these lessons/advised about them. [There are] brothers/sisters who for more than 14 years have been informing other brothers/sisters to register every year. So you see that after 14 years there are still people registering. Some need [one] week, some [one] year, and others need years. So in the da3wah we should not become discouraged when people do not want to respond.
The sister: A number of sisters around me took off the hidjaab during the break. I advised them not to do that. And this was truly something I found hard. How can I deal with their remorse?
The teacher: [By making clear to them] that they should show remorse, and that they should let themselves be cultivated, and that they should gather knowledge; because knowledge is the only thing by which one remains firm. For when someone changes his attitude or his country and goes and behaves differently, it means that the iemaan is not rooted in his heart. For knowledge leads to firmness. They will then also practise sincerity towards gathering knowledge, and thus remain firm. That is, [that] people be advised/motivated to register for gathering knowledge, and that all thresholds be explained and removed immediately, and that they devote themselves to gathering this knowledge. For every word/sentence of knowledge they receive, you receive a reward for it. And every sentence or word they say, and every deed they perform, and every deed towards others, and the advice, and the tarbiyah they give their children — you receive a reward for all of that. An incalculable reward that countless earths could accommodate, with regard to gathering knowledge. So the more aware you are of the reward, the more driven you are to lead someone to this tremendous matter.
The reaction of sister 3
The sister — in the end — also went on holiday for three weeks to Morocco. And the connection with the knowledge of family affairs was the relationship with her family. The dealings with them, and what everyone's rights are, and how you deal with that.
The teacher: Can you give a number of examples to give more attention to this material?
The sister: She would suggest something and her father would decide what would be done. And she always kept this in her mind. The teacher: How about the division of time, and [about the fact] that we [learned] that when we say something, we think [first]? [The sister:] The division of time — when she was in Morocco at the beginning she wanted to do Qur'aan, but the further they went into the holiday, the more she had let that slip. She had taken Islamic books with her, and at the beginning she did that more than at the end of the holiday. She found [it] difficult to find a form of balance. She did not feel obliged to gather knowledge continuously. And a [short] break would also be good — she thought.
And with regard to thinking in advance about what you say: she finds it difficult to get into that. The teacher: We have learned that before we do something, we think: will Allaah be pleased with this or not? The sister: The sister did — yes — take that into consideration. She noticed that when she wants to go and drink something in the evening with her family, she notices that [there are] certain places they go to where there are many distractions where she prefers not to end up. For example: they sit somewhere drinking, [and at a distance of] three shops music is being played or [there are] women in revealing clothing. On the holiday they would quickly end up in a situation she does not want to end up in, where she prefers not to be.
The teacher: The teacher also went abroad to perform da3wah. He [would enter] restaurants and it would be requested [there] to turn off the music. Then it is said: «no, sorry, we will not do that; because the restaurant's system is set up like that». Which system is given precedence? The system of Allaah or the system of the restaurant? «No, we are not that strict» — they make clear, and they prefer to keep the customers satisfied. They did not want to turn off the music. [Then it is said:] «Fine, may Allaah reward you, we are leaving.» So it is important — after you have advised — that you avoid the place. They were the only customers; there was no [other] customer. Then you go to another place and you see that another place is much better/calmer, and one is not disturbed by music. So if you are in a place where there is music, you should not surrender yourself to that. And you should — in any case — admonish in your place — for example — the family. [There are] very many temptations, and [there are] many things. Do you [all] think that Allaah loves this, will Allaah bless us with this? Or is it better that we go to another, calmer and better place? That is the minimum. And the danger of such a place is — without you noticing — that you go and find it normal. For you see many supposedly practising people [who say]: «everyone sits [here], so why would I make [things] difficult?» Therefore it is important that we do not surrender ourselves to such situations. And in any case, also when planning to go there, you can ask: will we encounter music there, will we encounter women there? So this is also something for the next time we all have dealings with this.
Sister 4
Patience in trial, and also inviting people to patience. And in Morocco [there was] a wedding; she advised and decided not to go.
Sister 5
A sister had a question. The teacher made clear that the places of fitnah are still to be avoided (the music and other things). Imagine you go as a family on an outing to the city. How far should you go, and how should you find a balance in that?
The teacher: Thinking well, and firmly establishing the priorities well. Will Allaah be pleased with me if I go towards my destination that I am going to? If you can determine a clear «no» for yourself, then it is also a «no» to going there. And if [the answer] is «yes», then you refrain from going there and ask people of knowledge [i.e. if there is a clear sin in it, you stop]. Is it healthy for me to go outside [where there are] many women in revealing clothing at whom even the woman is not allowed to look, let alone the man? So we should weigh things carefully. For the matter is not a question of «how far do we go in this?». The only question: will we please Allaah with this or not? Should you weigh every outing? If you know with certainty that you will end up in sins, then you should certainly weigh. Not that you say to yourself: «yes, but we see those women everywhere». For if you are going to a specific place, then you should also plan for it in advance in an Islamic way. For it is different [when you are] walking down the street because you have to walk there; then you can lower your gaze. But when you go to a specific place of which you know 100% that you will see and hear those sins — even if you are not going specifically for them — then you should ask yourself: will Allaah be pleased with this or not? If the answer is «no», then is there a necessity to go there? No, then we do not go there.
The sister: Should you then distinguish between necessity and relaxation [recreation]?
The teacher: Can you relax in a halaal way? That means we should seek those possibilities and make an effort to seek those possibilities. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «لقد خلقنا الإنسانَ في أحسن تقويم، ثم رَدَدناه أَسفَلَ سافِلين». Interpretation of the meaning: «Verily, We created man in the best stature; then We reduced him to the lowest of the low.» That means that the human being who does not please Allaah belongs to the lowest of people. For the disbelievers are [lower] than the believers with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. We should make an effort to go towards the good. That means that when I go to a country that I know is filled with corruption (that they do not follow Islaam), and evil, and nudity, then you should not love to come there even if it is a relaxing holiday. For then you go and seek out exactly where you will be influenced [badly]. And as a Muslim you should also look at the situation. When you gather less knowledge, you have less iemaan. And when you are less among the practising sisters, you have less iemaan. And when you are reminded of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa less by means of the lectures and other things, you have less iemaan. That means that you are somewhat vulnerable to the shaytaan, and that you go and make yourself more vulnerable by exposing your eyes, your ears and your whole body to the temptations. Then these temptations will enter more easily. And thereby your iemaan decreases. So your iemaan drops, and that is also the state of very many people who go on holiday. For they do not plan their holiday in the right way with regard to the health of the iemaan. So when you are vulnerable to the shaytaan, do not go and expose yourself to more temptation; because the iemaan drops because of it. For very many brothers/sisters stop gathering knowledge after the holiday; because their iemaan has dropped [to such an extent] that they have fallen into that vulnerability [such that] they think: «oh, I will do it sometime». And it is good to relax, but for that we have also set down those adhkaar. So that there is [at least] a minimal reminder of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa alongside the obligatory prayers and the like.
When you see yourself like this, then you should not expose yourself to more temptations. [Rather,] make more effort to perform da3wah yourself. For who is then the first to hear the da3wah? You yourself. That means you are then also in the process of admonishing yourself. For da3wah is among the matters we should not let go of in any situation of our lives. Even when we sit in the waiting room, we can also perform da3wah. We can write a beautiful message (a few sentences) that people will think about. And perform much dhikr (remembrance of Allaah) so that we too resist the temptations of the shaytaan.
The sister: With regard to the da3wah — we also received lessons on this — but some people feel that they are too bad [in state] to perform da3wah. At that moment the shaytaan is a competitor. He will use everything he has to prevent you from performing da3wah.
The sister: [People say:] «yes, but you do this and you do that». Then you say to them: «may Allaah reward you well, I have gained much more love for you [because] you point out my mistakes to me». For when you perform da3wah, your most important goal is the pleasure of Allaah. And as a secondary goal you want the improvement of these people. You want Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa to open the hearts of these brothers/sisters whom you admonish, to the admonition. [But] first your own heart should open itself to the admonition. First you should be glad and [sincerely] mean that that [person] has done a good deed by pointing out your mistakes to you.
Everyone who comes to you and advises you to pay attention — [beware] of responding in an arrogant way. Throw that under your foot and trample on it: say «may Allaah reward you well for the reminder». What is the effect of that on that [person] when you are truly sincere? Then you are in the process of performing da3wah. The sister makes clear that she will not feel arrogant; because it seems as if the other person is doing it to spite you [to hurt you], but she feels precisely even more lowly.
Did that [person] say he is spiting you? No, but the tone [the intonation] seems that way — according to the sister. She perceives it that way. That means the sister should work on herself, not on the other person.
And among the things we should work on is that we never think badly of the one who advises us. Never! Even if at that moment he wants to spite you, and you say «may Allaah reward you well for pointing this out to me, I have shown remorse for it and will show more remorse». At that moment the one between whom and you there is enmity [becomes] as though he were a devoted [bosom] friend. That is what Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says. He subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «ولا تَستوي الحسنةُ ولا السيّئة. ادفَع بالتي هي أحسنُ، فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوةٌ كأنه وَلِيٌّ حميم». Interpretation of the meaning: «And the good deed and the evil deed are not equal. Repel [evil] with that which is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.» And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «وما يُلَقّاها إلا الذين صَبَروا». Interpretation of the meaning: «And none is granted this except those who are patient.» Therefore we should train ourselves to reach this level. For our patience begins with not thinking that they are spiting us. And besides that, you can transform your negative feeling into a positive feeling. Then you can also know that you are being tested as to whether you will accept the da3wah, and that you gain more drive to perform da3wah.
So you do — yes — continue advising other people; because that means you first give the advice to your own heart. For when the teacher is in the process of giving the lesson, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is witness that it also has an effect on his heart, his thinking; because at that moment he is also speaking first with himself. And everyone will notice that too. So it is important that we are upright in this.
And it is also permissible to perform da3wah while you yourself do not do anything [of what you call to]. [However, there is] a difference between the steps you should take and being the most exemplary. For what is less ideal is that you also go and advise about matters you yourself do not do. Therefore the scholars say: «follow what I say, and do not follow what I do». For even the scholars can have weak points, or may have forgotten something, or make mistakes. For the statements are much more precise than what they do. And apart from that, you should — yes — show the good example yourself. And that does not mean that when you are not the good example, you are not allowed to perform da3wah.
Questions
Question: A message that was shared in the WhatsApp group. It begins — it was about the upbringing of children. It was about a certain speaker of whom scholars have said that he should not be followed. And that is Nu3maan 3alie KHaan (Nouman Ali Khan) (an English-speaking speaker).
The answer: [The teacher] will research this; because he has no knowledge of this. He should research it well, and cannot issue [a judgement] on it. They send the lecture privately to the teacher — the lecture of the brother who responded to the other brother.
The teacher says that it is important that a path be followed that also corresponds to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. For the path in this — so as not to end up on the path of misguidance — is a very important matter. The teacher will explain the extreme paths, and the middle path in this according to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
The lax path is the path of «it does not matter who [the speaker is], we take from everywhere; because everyone is free to say what he wants, and everyone is free to take what he wants». This path is not permissible; because Allaah and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam have made clear that we should filter our ears and eyes, and that we should distinguish between pure knowledge and impure knowledge. For the matter [depends] on what is said, not on who says it. For many people it does not matter what [the speaker] studied, what ideology, what methodology he has, as long as that [person] — according to us (they then think, instead of «according to the Sunnah») — speaks in a normal way, there is no problem. That is a path of misguidance. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam has also warned us against this path. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «The Jews split into seventy-one sects, and the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and the Muslims (my ummah (community)) will split into seventy-three sects. All of them [in the Fire] except one. Then the sahaabah asked: who is this sect? [He said:] It is the djamaa3ah (community) upon which the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam is today, and his companions». So the djamaa3ah are the sahaabah, and the Sunnah [is] the way of the sahaabah. By this it becomes clear to us that we should — in any case — filter.
And another [extreme] path is «we may not take from anyone, and we go digging into every preacher to find his mistakes, and then we go and declare him unfit because he committed these mistakes, and because he does not follow our shaykh». This is a very dangerous and destructive path that is being followed. For if we follow this path, we ourselves will no longer know what we should follow, [and] we turn away from the rest of the scholars except for one or two scholars, and we sow much doubt among the people, and we make people turn away from knowledge. For they have established certain incorrect guidelines that do not belong to the Sunnah. For the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam never said: follow only one or two shaykhs. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also did not say that when someone makes mistakes, we may not follow him. For the only one who does not err in the religion [is] the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. From Aboe Bakr to the last human being on earth, they will make mistakes, but Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam have taught us how we should deal with that, and that there are people who have a different position in Islaam from others. And [there is] a specific narration relating to this. Mu3aadh ibn DJabal has a saying relating to the scholars. He says: «Beware (that is: be alert) of the slip of the wise man (the scholar), and do not let this slip lead you to turn away from him. How can we distinguish the mistake from the good matter? He said: the good has a light by which you recognise it, and the mistake is that which contains darkness».
And Mu3aadh ibn DJabal has the most knowledge of halaal and haraam of this ummah. This is said by the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
The more knowledge we take, the more light we receive. The better we can distinguish between a threshold, a tree and a pit in the road — [that is] the more knowledge there is, the further the light shines. So that means that we can distinguish between the good and the false by means of knowledge. How do we know whether the one giving the lessons really has the knowledge or not? You know that [by the fact that] the scholars have advised that he give those lessons. You know that [by the fact that] he only uses the sources of Allaah, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, or the sahaabah. No [sources] from Western sources, ahaadieth that are not authentic, dreams, and the like. No, he bases himself in all his statements and deeds on these three authentic sources (Allaah, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and the sahaabah).
[There is] a sect that arose around the year 1992, which tried to dig into every active preacher for his mistakes, and to display his mistakes, and these mistakes could also be differences [of opinion] (that they have an opinion with evidences, and these have an opinion with evidences, and they call that bid3ah (innovation) while it is not bid3ah but merely a difference [of opinion]). They would declare them weak. They would cut and paste from the audio files and video clips, and present that to the scholars. And from this fitnah some were alert to the fitnah, but many scholars were not alert, and went along with these things. And around the year 2000 very many scholars [dissociated themselves] from these sects and warned [against them] (Ibn Baaz, al-Albaanie and others). So thousands of scholars warned against this sect. And this sect also exists in the Netherlands. And the principle of this sect: has someone made a mistake? Then he should be razed to the ground, and also [because] their shaykh is not visited in Makkah or al-Madienah. And this sect has disintegrated. And the middle path is that we hold on to the people of knowledge, cling to them, listen to their advice, learn from them, and be alert not to enter into any form of these two extremes (laxity or exaggeration). For one says: «follow a madhhab (school of law), because you are a Moroccan you should follow the [such-and-such] madhhab». And another says to you: «if you do not agree with my shaykh, then you do not follow the Sunnah». [And that is wrong, for] this Sunnah does not depend on one shaykh or one scholar.
You should distinguish between judging an act and judging a person. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «إنما الأعمالُ بالنيات». Interpretation of the meaning: «Verily, deeds are only by intentions.» And: «إنما لكل امرئٍ ما نوى». Interpretation of the meaning: «And verily, every person shall have only what he intended.» The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam distinguishes here between judging deeds and judging a person; because when someone utters kufr (disbelief) (which takes him out of Islaam) — then for judging him you need other conditions than [the conditions of] judging the statement. For the statement can be kufr, but the one who uttered it need not thereby have become a kaafir (disbeliever). [There was] a man who uttered kufr while he was being tortured. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said to him: «Be patient, O family of [so-and-so]» [i.e. O household of so-and-so]. So he had not become a kaafir. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam relates about a person who says: «O Allaah, You are my servant and I am Your Lord». The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «He erred out of the intensity of joy.» For he meant the opposite: «You are my Lord and I am Your servant». Because he was so overjoyed, he does not thereby become a kaafir; because he made a mistake. And if someone throws the Qur'aan, that is kufr. [And] Moesaa also threw the words of Allaah out of anger (the tablets). He did not pay attention to it. He was [so] angry with his people that he threw them. So is Moesaa a kaafir? No. So the way of the Sunnah and the sahaabah is that they distinguish between judging an act and judging a person.
And judging a person [means] that it is a judicial verdict, or a judgement [issued] just like that without verification, without checking whether he meant it or not, whether he understood what you said or not, [and] that he perhaps made a mistake he can retract later, [and] that he is forgetful. So it is a judicial verdict. That means that many more conditions are attached to it than for [a judgement] to be issued on it just like that. So the great scholars are the ones who should issue judgements on this, not some students of knowledge. Therefore it is important that we are not dragged onto a path in which we warn others against those who make mistakes, [by] advising them not to learn from him/gather knowledge from him [on the pretext] that his 3aqiedah is correct and his manhadj (methodology) is not correct. And we should also not accept from just anyone what that [person] says. And we should also not go and sit and listen to just anyone. Everyone who calls himself a guest speaker, [and whose name] appears in a flyer, [and] because he belongs to an institute — [it is said:] it will be fine. No, that should be filtered by people of knowledge.
What is the difference between 3aqiedah and manhadj? The 3aqiedah is what one believes. And under that fall Tawhied (the Oneness of Allaah), belief in the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and distinguishing between halaal and haraam. And the manhadj [is] the way of gathering knowledge and calling to knowledge. For there are people who go astray in knowledge, like the shie3ah (Shiites). And there are also people who go astray in the manhadj, like the IKHwaan [al-Muslimoen (Muslim Brotherhood)]. And from this methodology other sects have also arisen.
What if a scholar permits men and women to sit mixed in a lecture? Should you beware of taking knowledge from him, or is it only that you should not go to the lesson?
In the time of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam there was no partition between the men and the women, but there was no mixing between the men and the women. For the men were [at] the front, and the women were [at] the back. So if [the matter] is truly mixing — [such that] the men are on one side and men and women sit next to one another — then that is not correct. And that does not yet mean that this person accepts it. For it may be that this arrangement was imposed [on him], in that it was requested [of him]. But if [the matter] is under his management [in his hand], then that means he is making a great mistake in that, and that does not mean that everything he says is incorrect, no. [But] yes, [there is] a mistake in the manhadj; because he mixes the men and the women. So such a person has a form of [undisciplined] leniency. And we should not judge matters ourselves; rather, we let people of knowledge judge in that.
And not everyone who gives lectures [or] gives lessons can we simply ask such things. For [there are] levels among the people of knowledge and the scholars. Imagine that such a teacher agrees to people being mixed. Knowledge may not be gathered and transmitted in that way. Then that [person] should be advised.
And it is different when the men and the women sit in [one] group on Skype. That is a different matter.
Imaam Ibn Hadjar [al-3asqalaanie]: it is said about him that he had the 3aqiedah of al-Ash3arie. For he took some ideas from al-Ash3arie. And the source [with the Ashaa3irah is] philosophy, the intellect. And that is not [the case] with Imaam Ibn Hadjar [i.e. he was not a pure Ash3arie].
Question: If we want to receive lessons somewhere at an institute, how should we proceed to see whether the 3aqiedah and the manhadj are correct?
The answer: Why do you want to go to another place if you have a safe environment? If someone says «Allaah said, the Messenger said, the sahaabah said», and he is authorised [licensed] by the scholars, then you can receive lessons from him. But the moment someone says «that scholar said, that manhadj is such-and-such. That [person] agreed with it» — then they find that «wow», and they see it as knowledge. [Whereas] that [is not] knowledge. The matter is simple. Whoever says to you «yes, but the theory is such-and-such» — from that person no knowledge should be taken. If you want to gather knowledge somewhere, then ask the person of knowledge who also taught you that Allaah, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and the sahaabah said [such-and-such].
Question: And how about the Arabic/Qur'aan lessons? May you receive them from people who are known to have an incorrect 3aqiedah?
The answer: It is a matter [that lies] in the fitrah that the student is influenced by his teacher. Whoever teaches you the Qur'aan can also influence you with other things. So if you see that someone has a good 3aqiedah, then go and learn there. For that has a greater priority than learning from someone who has no [sound] 3aqiedah. And you listen to the Qur'aan in the best way as it was sent down. For the muqri-e [the reciter of the Qur'aan] will not influence you in any way whatsoever. So it is permissible to listen to a muqri-e.
Should we turn away from the people who constantly start on this [topic, i.e. discrediting the preachers]? Yes, certainly! Turn away from the people who are always occupied with this. For that deadens the heart, so that you are no longer occupied with yourself. Occupy yourself with what is more important, including the dhikr.
