The fiqh (jurisprudence): the salaah, the fasting, the Hadj and the zakaah.
[There is] knowledge that is obligatory upon everyone [and] absolutely obligatory, but [there is also] knowledge that only becomes obligatory [when] you have dealings with it, such as the zakaah and the Hadj, and buying and selling (the permissible and impermissible contracts).
If you are in the marriage, [or] are preparing yourself for the marriage, then what we receive in 3ilm shu-oon al-usrah is also obligatory knowledge with which one educates oneself and can order one's marriage relationship and perform the tarbiyah of the children in the correct way. So when one refuses to gather this knowledge or postpones this matter, then according to the measure of his refusal he will also commit injustice.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «طَلَبُ العلم فريضةٌ على كل مسلم» — «Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim».
[There are] two important things that keep one from gathering knowledge:
Shyness [embarrassment]. «I know that I do not know that, but if the people know that I do not know that, the people will look down on me, and the people will think that I know nothing.»
Arrogance. «I already know it, I already know it» — while he does not know it at all. And among the forms of arrogance is also «I can look it up myself». These people will be kept from knowledge until they show remorse, behave humbly, and gather knowledge.
And it is also important that we know that the more knowledge we have, the more our iemaan increases.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟﴾ [Soerat Faatir: 28]. Interpretation of the meaning: «It is only the people of knowledge among His servants who fear Allaah.»
What does that mean? It means that the more your knowledge increases, the more your khashyah (awe-filled fear) and your iemaan towards Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also increase. So the matter here is not specifically [about] the scholars; the matter here [is] that the more knowledge you have, the more reverence and fear you have. And the khashyah [awe] is fear with veneration. So as your knowledge grows, your iemaan grows as well.
And another matter that decreases the iemaan and causes instability [is] the imbalance in the religious experience between the two partners. For they are not at [the same] distance in their practising. One has begun to practise and the other refuses to practise, or says that he does not want to start yet, or [says] that the other is going much too fast. The matter [is] that there is an imbalance between the two partners with regard to the dien.
And [there is] also another imbalance, namely that the woman follows/holds an opinion and the man follows/holds another opinion. And this form of imbalance is easier to solve than the balance in the practising of both partners. For the balance in practising requires the will of the one who practises least to practise more, to be taken towards the good path. For that, one ought to make an effort. And when this imbalance is from the man towards the woman (that is, [that] the woman practises less than the man), it is important that the man takes his responsibility as leader, educator and the one responsible for the family, to take his wife towards the good by motivating her, by making the path beloved in the correct way, by letting her choose the correct friends, [and by] taking her to lectures and lessons that increase her iemaan. These are all possibilities that the man can use and ought [to use]. And it is an obligation upon him towards his wife. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will question him about this on the Day of Judgement, because he is the one responsible for his family. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «والرجلُ في بيته راعٍ، وهو مسؤولٌ عن رعيّته» — «And the man is a shepherd in his house, and he is responsible for his flock» (in al-Bukhaarie and Muslim). And the hadieth: «أَلا كلُّكم راعٍ، وكلُّكم مسؤولٌ عن رعيّته. فالرجلُ راعٍ على أهل بيته، وهو مسؤولٌ عنهم. والمرأةُ راعيةٌ في بيت زوجها وولده، وهي مسؤولةٌ عنهم» — «Verily, every one of you is a shepherd, and every one of you is responsible for his flock. The man is a shepherd over the members of his household, and he is responsible for them. And the woman is a shepherdess in the house of her husband and over his children, and she is responsible for them».
That means that everyone who is in his house falls under his responsibility. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also commands that in the Qur'aan: Soerat At-Tahriem: 6 «يا أيها الذين آمنوا، قُوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارًا» — «O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire.»
It is narrated from Ma3qil ibn Yasaar (in al-Bukhaarie and Muslim) that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam say: «ما من عبدٍ يَستَرعيه اللهُ رعيّةً، يموت يومَ يموت وهو غاشٌّ لرعيّته، إلا حَرّم اللهُ عليه الجنّةَ» — «There is no servant to whom Allaah entrusts a flock, who dies on the day he dies while he is deceiving his flock, except that Allaah has forbidden Djannah to him».
So [it is] not [the case] that the man can say «it is her business», or [that] the woman says «it is his business». That cannot be; for everyone will be questioned [held to account] about his will regarding the advice, his will in the authority, and his will in the responsibility.
And when [it is] the reverse, when the woman practises more than the man — and often both practise [little] to an equal degree. And sometimes the woman begins earlier than the man. Then it is important that she takes the responsibility to get him to practise, by saying: «You are the leader of the family, and all the decisions you make have consequences for the family. And also your sins that you commit have an effect on the family, and your iemaan that you have also has an effect on the family; therefore it is important that you please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa more, and obey Him more, so that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa helps you and blesses you and is pleased with you, whereby He also helps you to lead us in the correct way.» In this way the woman guards her position and the position of her husband, but she — nevertheless — fulfils her responsibility. And what usually happens is that the woman goes and behaves angrily and irritably towards the man, [whereby] the man turns away from the woman, and a gap arises between the man and the woman, an even greater gap in the practising. Thereby neither of them gains anything. Therefore it is important that both partners each fulfil their own responsibility to admonish the other, advise him, and help him fulfil his responsibility. For when the woman goes and becomes rebellious and irritated [because] the man does not pray, [or because] he smokes — then she thereby also commits a sin; when she becomes rebellious, gets angry, then she too is engaged in committing sins. This [is] the way in which you help your husband. And the guideline [is]: guard the position of the man. Then the man will respond to that more. And if that does not work for the woman, then at that moment she ought to engage a person of knowledge. Why is it not right at that moment to engage his father or her father? Because it usually happens that [things] go wrong, and the parents — unfortunately — do not have the correct wisdom and knowledge to set such matters right; therefore it is important that this be done by a person of knowledge and experience with marriage matters, [who knows] how to reconcile between the partners, and [that] both sides be heard. If you cannot do that yourself, then it is important that the sister engage a person of knowledge who will also go and advise her husband, admonish him, or perhaps give him a form of programme. So this imbalance ought to be solved.
And if this imbalance is not solved with patience [and] much trying, then it is important that a person of knowledge look at the situation very carefully and study it. Is it better that such a woman stay with this man, or does she — nevertheless — request the talaaq? So [the one looking] ought to be a person who has much knowledge of this, so that everything is taken into account in it.
The ustaadh experienced [a case] of a convert [new to Islaam]. She was in a very difficult situation. The house is not her house but her husband's house. And she has children from this man. And he smokes, does not pray, and sometimes smokes hashish. And this sister — yes indeed — practises, prays, wears her hidjaab. But if she were divorced now, she would end up in a completely different situation, in a situation in which she no longer has maintenance, no longer a house, and no longer other possibilities — while the man does not keep her from realising her practising. And then the children would also experience even more drama [tragedy], be inflicted with even more psychological damage than they [already have], [and] more fitnah would arise [because] the partner might want to take revenge. So the ustaadh said to this sister: «Be patient and keep advising. And when you are kept from wearing the hidjaab or from the salaah, then it is better that you leave him.»
And [there is] another matter relating to the imbalance. And the guideline in this: when the woman regards a matter as obligatory (and trustworthy scholars regard it as an obligatory matter), then the man ought to permit her that. For example the niqaab (face veil). If she follows the opinion that says it is obligatory, then he may not keep her from wearing the niqaab. For with her it is a sin, and with him it is not, because he follows another opinion. And if the woman says «I follow the opinion [that says] it is recommended» and the man follows the opinion that it is obligatory, then the woman ought to obey the man even though she follows the opinion [that says] it is recommended. Then she ought to obey the man.
These, then, are guidelines regarding the imbalance in opinions.
And the woman ought — in the end — to obey the man, except in disobedience to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
And another matter relating to the iemaan is that both partners or one of them enters the zawaadj with an incorrect intention: for example for the money of the other, [or] wanting maintenance from the other, [or] for a little adventure, [or] wanting sex from the other. For there is only one intention [that makes] the zawaadj lead towards the correct path, and that is the ikhlaas. In such a case it is important that one awaken the intention by uttering it: why do I want to marry you, and how do I want to realise the marriage. And when one has not done that, one does it once one is married: «Let us awaken anew our intention of why we married. To please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.» And when we are in the marriage, it is important that we talk with each other about this intention and the practical realisation of this intention: for example that we advise each other more and more often, that the woman obeys the man more, that the man takes the woman into consideration more, by — for example — reminding each other of the question of whether, with the deed we perform or the statement we have uttered, we want the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and letting each other get used to this question. Do I want to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa? Yes, I want to. No, I do not want to. I do not know, I will not do it, but I will ask people of knowledge. So this is a matter that ought constantly to be a reminder and a principle in the home. For when you do not have such an intention, the iemaan will also be less; for your decisions will be according to your intention, [and] your love will be [likewise]. And so will also be the drawing closer to one another; for your love for the other will not depend only on whether that other gives you what you want or not, but will depend on whether that [person] pleases Allaah or not. That is a far more lasting relationship and love than mere love that depends on «are you nice to me or not». So that has a direct effect on the iemaan.
And another matter that also decreases the iemaan is that money receives a higher priority with both the man and the woman. For when money receives a higher priority, that also has an effect on the iemaan. Not only on the iemaan of the man or the woman, but also on the children and the way of raising the children. «You must study well so that you make a career, so that you are not behind in money.» That is a destructive tarbiyah, instead of the children having the pleasure of Allaah as the highest priority. Prestige, beautiful clothing and beautiful shoes — that is what the children then receive.
And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also took this matter [into account] in the education of the wives of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ قُل لِّأَزْوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحْكُنَّ سَرَاحًۭا جَمِيلًۭا ۝٢٨ وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْمُحْسِنَٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًۭا ۝٢٩﴾ [Soerat Al-Ahzaab: 28-29]. Interpretation of the meaning: «O Prophet, say to your wives: if you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come; I will give you an enjoyment and release you in a beautiful manner. (28) But if you desire Allaah and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter, then verily Allaah has prepared for the doers of good among you an immense reward. (29)»
With this Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa commands His Messenger sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam to have [them] choose between two choices: the dunyaa or the aakhirah. The dunyaa: no problem, [they are released]. The aakhirah: then [there is] a great reward.
And in a hadieth narrated by 3aa-ishah, she says: when Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa commanded His Messenger to present these two choices, he began with me, and said to me: «I will mention a matter to you; do not hasten until you have consulted your parents.» [She said:] he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam knew that her parents would never let her separate from him. That 3aa-ishah mentioned, that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam knew that.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says through the tongue of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam: «I will give you a good, beautiful enjoyment.» And the good enjoyment here [is] that you are divorced, receive money, and can separate. Or the aakhirah, and you have patience. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «Verily, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has said» — and then he mentioned the aayaat. Then [3aa-ishah] said: «O Messenger of Allaah, about you should I consult my parents?! Rather, I choose Allaah and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter.» Then he put the same question to the rest of his wives.
And [there were] at that moment nine wives under the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. Why were these aayaat sent down? These aayaat were sent down after some of his wives had asked for nafaqah (maintenance) (and the nafaqah is money for them that they could spend on themselves — while their basic needs were present with them. They had water and sufficient dates and one garment they could wear. Rights had been given [to them]. And the nafaqah [here] is expenses [allowance]). So either you choose the money, or you choose the aakhirah.
And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also said in another aayah (Soerat At-Tahriem: 5): «عسى ربُّه إن طَلّقكنّ أن يُبدِله أزواجًا خيرًا منكنّ، مسلماتٍ، مؤمناتٍ، قانِتاتٍ، تائباتٍ، عابداتٍ، سائحاتٍ، ثَيِّباتٍ وأبكارًا» — «Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you: Muslim women, believing women, obedient women, repentant women, worshipping women, fasting women, previously married women and virgins.»
That means that the women — and also the men — give money a high priority. And money has only come to be used as a test [so that] Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [be pleased with it]. For when it becomes much, we will be tempted by it. So the less money, the better. Money ought therefore not to be our priority.
And one of the cases the ustaadh has handled, and which stands out above all cases with regard to money — and it need not — apart from that — be the woman [alone] who is the one greedy for money. The woman called the ustaadh. «My husband does not practise. He prays, but he does not grow a beard» — she wants — in reality — to be divorced from him. When the ustaadh spoke with the man, he found out that they had quarrelled, not about the practising of Islaam, but merely because the woman says: «I want you to put half of your property in my name; for the contract of community of goods [marriage in community of property] is constructed that way. I want you to put that in my name» — and one of her complaints was that he does not provide for her, that he gives her very little allowance, and that she has to make a great effort to extract that little bit of money. When the ustaadh found that out, the ustaadh asked her about it, and she said: «That is correct, because it is my right.» Then the ustaadh advised and admonished her: the man never said: «When I enter the marriage with you, I will give half of the money.» And she had already received in the Netherlands half of the house, and she also received the child benefit, which she had saved up in her account for ten years. The ustaadh asked: why do you do that? [She said:] they are my children. [He said:] the money is the money of your children, and the man has the right to decide where these expenses go. [She said:] no, she raised them. And he also found out that her husband regularly gave her 250 euros per week.
She says: «Everything is expensive in our time, so that is impossible. With that I cannot even get a beautiful dress.» [He said:] give me an example of how you have to make a great effort to extract money from him. [She said:] last month I reminded him several times that he should buy a bicycle for his child. The ustaadh [needed] to step outside for a moment to cool down, to compose himself. And in the end this woman refused to cooperate. She destroyed her marriage and the marriage of her husband in order to bring in that money.
And [the matter] can also apply to the man, in that he is only greedy for the woman's money, or is only busy with work, work, work, and forgets his responsibility for his wife and children.
And the solution for this is that one — before entering the zawaadj — communicates clearly, and knows with whom one is entering the marriage. That one knows what his intentions and goals are. And that one asks Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa to give him the best partner. For whoever is greedy only for money, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will not guide him to the correct decision. For when the money becomes less, the problems grow. And especially with the non-Muslims: when suddenly the man or the woman is left without work, then divorce immediately follows. And that [is because] most of their marriages are built on money. They then have nothing more to offer each other except love for the sake of money. They live to work, [and] do not work to live. And with some Muslims you find that too. And that [is because] the money — once again — is the only thing keeping them together. That is a sign. So it is important that one perform tawbah, correct oneself, and give money no priority whatsoever, but use money only to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And this disease requires a long breath in the healing. And for that, people of knowledge ought to come who admonish both persons. And [the matter] can end in a talaaq. For the talaaq is not always wrong.
And another matter [is] deceiving each other and lying to each other. And this matter leads to distrust. For the more open the relationship is, the more you can trust each other, and the more you can lead each other to the pleasure of Allaah. For if one of them lies, and the other knows that one of them is lying, how can one lead the other to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa? [One] cannot; for there [is] no trust. For trust is the foundation of admonition and tarbiyah. If the woman knows that her husband lies — someone calls, and the man gives the woman the telephone [and says]: «Say that I am not [here], that I forgot my phone» — even if the woman were to cooperate [with] the act, the man ought not to think [that] there is trust between us. For the woman is not permitted to cooperate. For he has broken the trust. For when one helps the other in lying, there is no longer trust between them, however much you want to deceive yourself with it. And the woman will also use this matter when she deems it necessary towards the man. Then she says to the children: «This you must not tell your father. This must stay between us.» That is deception. And thereby this disease passes on to the children. «Ah, if your father finds out about this, he will get angry, so you must not tell it.» You are — in reality — saying to the children: do that too when we raise you. And the ustaadh does not understand these parents. May Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa guide us to the best.
What Is the Solution for This?
The solution for this is that one perform tawbah, and never lie. That one not think [there is] trust when they lie to others. That is a pitfall of the shaytaan. That one not follow the pitfalls of the shaytaan, and be open and truthful towards one another. And that the woman also tell everything to her husband, and the man also tell everything insofar as he deems it necessary and wise. And when [the man] is asked about something, he does not go and lie. So the tawbah is very important in this, and that one also keep away from this matter. And one ought also to be truthful with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and that is the foundation [by which one is] also truthful with one another. For whoever has more iemaan, you can trust more. That is the foundation.
And the incorrect fixing of the conditions in the marriage contract [is] the next matter that is connected to the iemaan. Incorrect and unrealistic conditions. And that can come for all sorts of reasons. One of them is that they want to marry each other quickly, but — nevertheless — want to follow each other's desires. The woman wants to finish her studies, so they put in the marriage contract: «The woman ought to finish her studies» — without thinking about [the fact] that the woman is then also outside the house every day, and gathers with non-Muslims and men, whereby she loses her shyness [sense of modesty] and loses many things she needs in the marriage, whereby the irritations multiply, the iemaan decreases, and — in the end — a talaaq comes.
And the ustaadh does not know, until now, a [single] marriage in which the woman had to finish the studies and which has succeeded, unless [the woman] is in the final year [such that] only the graduation remains for her. That is not what the ustaadh means. When ought you to have children? When ought you to set up your home? If you are at school every day, if you have homework, if you have to do assignments with fellow students, if you have to do an internship, and the like. Such a marriage will not succeed, however great the dream of both of them [is]. It is impossible for such a marriage to succeed, and if one keeps going on [in it], he has committed sins; for the proportions [relations] are not correct.
And another example is that the woman stipulates a condition that the man may not marry a second wife. And this is a condition that — in the opinion of many scholars — is not permissible. For something that is permissible may not be made forbidden. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa reproached, from above the seven heavens, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam when he forbade himself to eat honey in order to please some of his wives.
Soerat At-Tahriem: 1: «يا أيها النبيُّ، لِمَ تُحرِّم ما أحلّ اللهُ لك، تَبتغي مَرضاةَ أزواجك؟ واللهُ غفورٌ رحيم» — «O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allaah has made permissible for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allaah is Forgiving, Merciful.» That means, then, that this condition too is not correct.
And it may be that for the man one wife is not sufficient to guard his chastity. So [it is] not [the case] that he is driven by desire; rather, [he is] driven by pleasing Allaah in the correct way. For it is part of the man's fitrah that he marries multiple women. That is simply something normal.
That means, then, that at that moment such a contract/condition has forbidden what is obligatory for him to perform, and then [the matter] collides. Therefore it is not correct that such a contract/condition be set, even though some scholars/preachers say it is permissible. And the ustaadh has explained a number of proofs [that] it is not permissible, and even that many scholars have not allowed it.
How Do We Deal with This?
Before we make contracts, before we set conditions, it is important that we ask people of knowledge whether these conditions are good or not, and whether we can set these conditions or not. And also, if you already have conditions in your marriage and they are still in force, have them examined [reviewed].
And such conditions often lead to sins, and thereby to less iemaan. For they lead to irritations, to unrealistic proportions [relations] between the man and the woman.
And another matter connected to the iemaan is that the drive of both partners is so low [that] one does not want to practise. Then the partners talk with each other — either in words or in an indirect way —: «We think it is fine like this, we do not need to do more, we do not need to hold on to the man growing his beard, praying al-fadjr, wearing his trousers above his ankles, the woman wearing a djilbaab; [no] a small headscarf suffices. We do not need to make [things] difficult for each other.» That brings about less iemaan, an incorrect proportion [relation], an incorrect relationship, which — in the end — ends in one separating, or continuing in the sins.
Therefore it is important that one be a strong example towards the other. For the sins do not have an effect on ourselves alone — when we also have a responsibility for the others around us, the sins will not only have an effect on ourselves, but will have an effect on the partner, and later also on the children, on the behaviour of the children.
And the ustaadh [is] often in dispute with parents about [the claim] that in our time it is difficult with the upbringing. When you sit somewhere where there is a meal, it is easy to fill [the time] with talk and complaining, a form of complaining culture. For example: «In the Netherlands we cannot raise children; the youth of our time, the children of our time» — while we do not realise that we [ourselves] are the cause. Everyone who has responsibility for another is the cause. When you say to that [person]: what do you want? [he says]: I want them to have good work and to practise. [You say]: do you consider yourself to be practising well? [He says]: yes, we do our best. [You say]: then why do you not go and do what pleases Allaah? [He says]: may Allaah guide us. So it is we [who] ought to change first. We — nevertheless — want them to become better? [But the matter] stops there. Thereby we deceive ourselves by wasting time, holding empty conversations, and complaining about others without looking at our own behaviour, while we are the cause. We raised these young people this way, we brought them up this way. Therefore it is important that we push ourselves even more towards the practising by advising one another, and that we make the social control even greater, by using the admonition and the social advice. Everyone in your circle, advise him according to where he has reached in his practising. Whoever prays but does not raise his children in the correct way, advise him 3ilm shu-oon al-usrah. And whoever ought to gather knowledge, advise him the basic 3aqiedah. That we ought to make our habit. That we — [the people of] gathering knowledge — be the strong ones, the leaders, so that we attain the pleasure of Allaah, and so that we practise first ourselves, and so that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also helps us [so that there is] a better environment around us. For in the better environment we ourselves can also help.
Questions
Question: Is it correct that you may not set conditions in the marriage contract that are self-evident, such as seeing your parents?
Answer: Yes, seeing your parents is something self-evident. For if you are in the marriage, you will not end up in a prison. In the end it is obligatory that you see your parents every now and then, [but] not that you appear before your parents every week. And [the matter] differs if your parents live nearby. If your parents live far away, then it is an exaggerated culture that she would have to appear at her parents' every week. The woman ought to know that she falls under the authority of her husband. If she wants to see her parents every week, that can collide with the authority of her husband, unless she has a sick mother and the like. Then the man ought also to know whether he can fulfil that condition.
Question: Is [it] bad if you do not set conditions during your marriage contract?
Answer: No. That is precisely better. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: whoever was easy, simple, gentle and approachable — Allaah has forbidden the Fire to him on the Day of Judgement. For the marriage requires flexibility, and especially more from the woman; for [it is] — in the end — [about] the man's plan. When there is no flexibility in the marriage, then — usually — there are the conditions that stand in the way of the marriage. Thereby quarrels come, [because] they cannot be fulfilled. And if there are conditions, then they ought to be described well.
So the fewer the conditions, the more blessed [the marriage] is.
A new point: not fulfilling each other's rights.
That brings about more frustration towards each other, and that brings about less iemaan. Thus [the matter] continues until the gap between the partners grows larger. And this circle ought to be broken by no longer acting in a reciprocal manner. For when one of them is wronged, the other ought not also to take a right from the other. That brings about a greater gap and more problems in the marriage. For when the dien has no foundation in the marriage, the marriage breaks and the marriage relationship breaks. Therefore it is important that one always return and refer to the three pillars: 1. one goal; 2. one path; 3. one leader.
And in order not to end up in such a situation, — at the very least — the rights of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa ought to be fulfilled and the rights of the other partner fulfilled. The man fulfils the rights of the woman, and the woman fulfils the rights of the man. And both fulfil the rights of the children, and then the children also fulfil the rights of their parents when they grow up. That [is] the positive circle that ought to be in the correct way.
Do not take another's right when he has taken your right, and engage the help of a person of knowledge to know what your rights actually are, and how you can realise them. What are the rights of your partner actually, and how can you help him realise them?
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «المؤمنون [المسلمون] عند شروطهم» — «The believers [the Muslims] abide by their conditions». Narrated by Imaam at-Tirmidhie and declared authentic by Imaam al-Albaanie.
«The believers [the Muslims]» means that when you enter the marriage, one of the most important conditions is that you fulfil the rights.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says in another hadieth: «إنّ أحقَّ الشروط أن تُوفُوا به ما استَحلَلتُم به الفُروج» — «Verily, the conditions most deserving to be fulfilled are those by which you have made the private parts permissible». That, then, [is] the mahr; but some scholars say that that [includes] all the conditions as well, indeed including the rights of both partners. For that [is] what you enter the marriage with. That you also know: he/she fulfils my rights.
Another point: that the partners each live their own life.
The partners ought — as we have clearly covered before — to live one life. For when [it is] not so, and when each goes his own way and has his own dream world, his own vision of this world, of the future, and of how things ought to go — then that will not succeed, and they will only stand in each other's way, and will not help each other in attaining more iemaan, and will be more occupied with competing with each other and obstructing each other than [with] loving each other and supporting each other towards the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Therefore it is important that the partners have only one world, one vision, one perspective. And when the partners differ in opinion, they ought — once again — to follow the three pillars: one goal, one path, one leader. And what also plays an important role here is that they be very quick in repairing the relationship, and that they not dwell far too long on things, and not let their feeling take the upper hand so as to dwell on things. For the things that have been dealt with, spoken out, forgiven — we ought to forget them and move on with our life. Thereby we will not create two worlds.
And another thing with which there is no gap [read: which precisely creates one] is that each goes and seeks his own advice. The woman with her friends, and the man with his friends. Then the friends go and play the role of the heroine: «How can you accept that?» That only makes the gap even bigger. So if you want to make the gap smaller, make sure that you seek advice only from one person of knowledge. [There are] teachers, students of knowledge — for every question you ask them, they need to ask someone who has more knowledge; because there [is] noise in the information they ask about. Ask the shaykh himself, not an intermediary. Ask one person who [understands] matters in a comprehensive way. For your vision too will enter into chaos if you ask more than one person. And you yourself will not be on one path, because you receive one answer from one and another answer from another. And the matter also depends on the way in which you tell something. Therefore it is important that you tell this matter to only one person [who is] trustworthy, who has substantive and practical knowledge, so that that [person] can give you a correct answer.
And another matter that also has an influence on the iemaan and in which people go and live a private life [is] that the partners neglect each other in the sexual attention and the educational [pedagogical] attention. That attention you ought to give each other as a 3ibaadah (worship) for Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
And the educational attention [is] the attention in which you both discuss how you can deal with each other in a better way, how you can improve the relationship, how the man can educate/improve/guide the woman. For that, conversations ought also to take place. And these conversations need not necessarily be dry [conversations]. For some people think that [matters] ought to be discussed in a serious way. For example during the love play [the foreplay] (during the sexual attention), during the meal, before sleep. For when a conversation occurs time and again, it will also acquire its gradual build-up. Also in the topic, and also in the way in which it is discussed.
In this way we can ensure that not everyone has his own life.
And another matter is that one leaves a weak iemaan without treatment. Thereby you also get less iemaan. For when the iemaan is weak with both partners or with one of them, they ought to seek how they can increase their iemaan, how they can draw closer to Allaah, and how they can get an iemaan boost. For when you have less iemaan, you are weaker and more vulnerable [more susceptible] to the shaytaan. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has even called us to attend gatherings with which we can increase our iemaan. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا، استَجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دَعاكم لما يُحييكم» — «O you who believe, respond to Allaah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life» (Al-Anfaal: 24). Those are the gatherings of the Qur'aan and the Sunnah, with which you enlarge your knowledge in this dunyaa.
Questions
Question: With regard to the educational attention: is it [something] to which the man ought to take the initiative, and can the woman also perform it if she sees that the man forgets it or the like?
Answer: Yes, certainly. If your husband — because of work, or [because] he does not see it, or does not want to give it attention — then she ought to anticipate that [take it upon herself]. And if he does not deem it necessary, then she ought to look at how she can convince him that it is necessary. And depending on his attitude, it is necessary that she alert him [motivate him] to the fact that it is necessary that he be present.
Question: [There are] also sometimes partners [with whom] the sexual attention collapses completely, [because there is] such a gap [between them]. And those are intimate matters that are only between the man and the woman. Imagine [that] a sister does not know well how she can improve that — [are there] certain pieces of advice? How can you give people — without them showing it outwardly — general advice for those who have problems with that?
Answer: We will give attention to this at the fifth core of the zawaadj relationship. [There is] a difference between someone who advises you from [the position of] professional assistance [counselling] and someone who advises you from [the position of] a friend; for such a thing you may not discuss with your friend. That is not permissible. And from [the position of] professional assistance you can advise a sister in this in a covered way. And that we will discuss extensively later. Then it is important that she seek — literally — closeness to her husband, not in a sexual way, but how she says it, what she says, what he likes, what you do not like. And vice versa likewise, that [the man] be taught how he ought to deal with a woman. For apart from the act itself, the matter [concerns] more the closeness. The closeness of the way of the man and the woman. It ought to be built upon the iemaan, the ikhlaas, upon a higher goal than mere sexual intercourse. For example, [there are] women who, when they seek closeness and their husband does not respond to it or does not show that he responds to it, quickly become frustrated and irritated, and then immediately change the atmosphere. This way — they ought to be taught [that] she ought to have patience and perseverance, and how the man and the woman deal with each other in this.
Question: A good point that was raised.
Answer: Almost all the sisters and brothers receive no sexual education with which they are prepared for their marriage. Usually [these] brothers and sisters have received sexual education at school, but they have also seen and heard much, and have perhaps — unfortunately — also done [it] much, as experience. And that is not experience; rather, [it is] experience built upon incorrectness, badness and falsehood. Such experience is at that moment taken into the marriage by the newly-weds. And the elders are different from us, and we are different. And that also goes back to the parents. For they regard this as a forbidden matter [taboo] to discuss, and say to themselves: «They have enough experience, they have seen and heard enough» — whereby they refer to the media and the like. Thus the parents and their children base — to some extent — this topic on the bad experience they have gone through. Whether [that] was by hearsay or they experienced it themselves. So that is a gap with the partners in an Islamic marriage. One of the gaps between the man and the woman is that there is no preparation for the marriage in this respect, neither from the parents nor from the young people either, and that both form themselves in secret and make themselves dependent on the experience they saw or heard before the marriage.
[There are] two kinds of sexual education: 1. from [the age of] zero until the buloegh; 2. the sexual education in preparation for the marriage. And for the sexual education from zero until the buloegh, 12 lessons [were prepared] that have been/will be given at various schools and [at] al-Istiqaamah for the girls, and this year also for the boys, and that especially for the children who are about to become mature [baaligh]. And perhaps it is also a good idea that a programme [course] be set up for the sexual education in preparation for the marriage. For many marriages break [because] they do not know how the fitrah of the man and the woman is constructed, and how the position ought to be in the sexual intercourse, the approach of the man and the approach of the woman.
