Nevertheless the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam asked [and requested her] to explain to him why she was panting, and whether it was she who was following him. At that moment he said to her: «لَتُخبِريني أو لَيُخبِرني اللطيفُ الخبيرُ» — «Either you tell me, or al-Latief (the Most Subtle), al-KHabier (the All-Aware) will tell me.» And in order to avoid provocation she also asked: «Does Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also know what we think?» She is in the process of learning. And after she had explained to him and the confrontation [took place], she changed the subject in order to turn away from incorrect communication and provocation. That is, to remove herself from provocation. So this is how you see that here both 3aa-ishah and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam [should] take each other into consideration in the best way, despite her mistake, which she herself also corrects afterwards.
Another incident:
When 3aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa was accused of indecency, and 3aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa was very sad but knew with certainty that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa would help her — she avoided every form of provocation so that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam would not become angry or irritated. And likewise the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam did not blame her and did not accuse her. It was a severe trial for both the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and 3aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa. And we will one day tell the whole story about that. For it is a wonderful story from which we can learn a great deal, especially with regard to patience, how you deal with news and rumours, and how you make sure that you do not wrong another. And also in that incident, 3aa-ishah and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam tried to avoid every form of provocation.
And also when 3aa-ishah became jealous when Umm Salamah brought a dish [bowl] with food for the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and 3aa-ishah made it fall to the ground. Despite 3aa-ishah's mistake, he avoided provocation. He smiled and said to Aboe Bakr and the others present: «غارت أمُّكم» — «Your mother became jealous.»
Everything you can do to help the other against his shaytaan you should do in the zawaadj. That means, then, that you are engaged in practising the hadieth (narration) of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam: «انصُر أخاك ظالمًا أو مظلومًا» — «Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.» The sahaabah (companions) said: «We know how to help him when he is oppressed.» [They said:] But how do we help the oppressor? The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «You seize his hands [you prevent him from his oppression].» Narrated by the Imaam al-Bukhaarie, who declared it authentic, and narrated by Anas ibn Maalik.
«I should not stand up for myself [take my own side].» [Rather,] standing up for yourself [is] that you help the other against his shaytaan, not that you help the other for his shaytaan. And you do that with gentle words, even if the other has made a mistake, and you do it with a fixed step-by-step plan:
Teaching. 2. Reminding. 3. Admonishing. 4. When someone keeps going [in the mistake], you keep admonishing him as a woman; but if the woman keeps going [in the mistake], then she should be rebuked by the man, and he should do that only as a fourth step. 5. Punishment.
In this way you are not engaged in provoking. So when the woman says «I do not want you to talk to me in this way» or «I am not the type [type] who wants to be rebuked by anyone» — then she should — nevertheless — become such a type. So if you do not want to be addressed in a rebuking way, or do not want to be punished, then make sure that you correct yourself at the first steps (teaching, reminding, admonishing). If you do not correct yourself — because of your stubbornness — after all the steps, and also do not accept the rebuke, then that is a form of kibr (arrogance).
So this point [revolves] around every form of provocation in communication. You should look at the communication that calms the other, or with which you can reach the heart of that other, so that the other can also be directed [led]. For when the heart is engaged, the limbs will get to work. And when the heart is not engaged, the limbs will not get to work.
3) Make sure — as a man — that you do not say «no» to everything in order to thereby show your manliness or your leadership.
Some men think that when they say «no» to everything, their manliness and leadership are shown. That is absolutely not correct; [it is] rather the complete opposite. For this matter ensures that both the woman and the children go and do things behind the man's back, or [that] the father/the man is no longer obeyed. And in addition, the woman will also, little by little, step by step, come to dislike her husband. Such a man should examine his sincere intention. And we have covered that the sincere intention also has a direct effect on the decision. Why do I decide in a certain matter by saying «no»? Have I obtained the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa by it, or do I only want to show my presence?
Do I want to bring up my wife and children for the sake of Allaah, or do I only want to supposedly cover my weakness with it? So it is important, when one is in leadership, that one takes one's decision on the basis of the sincere intention and knows that one is engaged in tarbiyah and that at that moment one wants to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. When that is [so], then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will also bless such a decision. And when that is not [so], then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will not bless such a decision, and it will have a counterproductive effect towards both the woman and the children.
And the man should also not forget that the woman and the children also want to have fun [amusement], and that this fun should also be used for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. So instead of the man saying «no» every time, he says «no» when he wants to reach an educational goal for the sake of Allaah with it, or when he sees that it is something that is not right with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa or can lead to that. And sometimes the woman or the children cannot see that. For example that the father forbids his wife a wedding. He knows — for example — that his wife talks a lot, or backbites a lot. He knows that the shaytaan will tempt her to — nevertheless — backbite about this sister and that brother and that family. At that moment he does not have to say to her: «No, do not go to that wedding.» If he sees that there will be certain sisters who enlarge/fuel her need for ghiebah (backbiting)... [She says:] Why do you not want that? No music is played, and there [is] no 3awrah (what should be covered) [visible]. Then he says «no» because he has an educational goal, namely that she does not gather with certain sisters who fuel her need for ghiebah. That is an educational goal that the man should see coming. Avoiding letting the one you are bringing up fall into the trap of the shaytaan. And it would be good to tell what the consequence is if she goes there. If the woman does not see that and goes on arguing even further, then he should say: «I do not want you to go there, but do you need something else that Allaah is very pleased with?» — purely because he spares her from committing the sin. So he should teach her little by little to avoid those sins. If she falls into them again, then he should remind her and admonish her. That is a way the man can use. And the man does not always have to justify himself. So you should not say to your husband that when he says «no» he wants to cover his manliness. We learn this in order to know how we can bring up and how we can be brought up. So the man can — without justifying himself — say «no».
And the woman should — in the end — weigh up: what do I want more, the hasanaat or an evening of fun that can lead me to sins? For the shaytaan can come to you [and say]: «Your husband does not want you to have fun [amuse yourself], your husband is not skilled in communication. He has no communication skills, or he loves isolation [withdrawal].» Then the women sometimes also go and press on about that. And some women go and look things up on the internet. And on the internet is everything that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is not pleased with. So they go and look up psychological websites and say: «My husband is a narcissist.» You will have filled in the symptoms with kuffaar (disbelievers), and out of that came a form of analysis. Those are incorrect ways of dealing with one another.
So make sure — if you are a man — that you do not say «no» to everything. That was also not the way of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, [that he] says «no» to everything. When [something] was possible [and] had no educational harms, he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam would say «yes». Even more, he himself had fun [played] with 3aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa. He carried her on his shoulders and showed her men who were throwing spears. And every time he asked her: «Have you had enough?» Then she would say: «No.» So he left her until she said «yes», and then he lifted her down from his shoulder.
Make sure — as a man — that you also push your wife towards good, and when she does good, that you also praise her with a du3aa-e: «May Allaah watch over you, may Allaah love you.» Make sure that your praise really has value: «May Allaah reward you with good (djazaaki-llaahu khayran)», «may Allaah make our love increase for His sake.» That is important for the love and closeness of the bond. For when you only say «no», that can destroy her self-confidence, and it will have an effect on the children and on her and on the way in which she treats you as a man. This will only have a bad, counterproductive effect.
4) The man should not misuse his leadership by demeaning the woman.
By misuse we mean only [the evil]. Not that he exercises his authority over her. [There is] a difference between exercising authority over your wife and misusing leadership. Exercising authority over your wife [is] that you treat her according to the pleasure of Allaah. And in that it can sometimes be necessary that «no» is said. When the woman asks for incorrect things, or [things] she knows are not permissible [for her], and then receives a «no» — that is not misuse of leadership. And the man goes and misuses his leadership when the woman is demeaned from the Islamic point of view. For the matter is not [about] how the woman feels demeaned, but [about] an important guideline, which is the Islamic guideline. The matter [concerns] the guideline that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has established. And the guideline [is]: that he does not insult, does not disfigure [revile], and that he fulfils the rights. That is what we also covered under the rights of the woman, where the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam forbade insulting, reviling, or striking/insulting the face. That [is] demeaning the woman.
And when the woman is advised or rebuked [because] she has performed a bad deed, then there is a problem with the woman [in the fact] that she behaves in an arrogant, haughty way when she says that her husband misuses leadership. She should be brought up by the man, and she should accept that her husband brings her up. When that is not accepted, it means that the woman is here engaged in committing a dangerous sin, and that is already kibr. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam has explained this [as]: «بَطَرُ الحقّ وغَمطُ الناس» — «Rejecting the truth [not accepting the truth] and looking down on people [demeaning them].»
And looking down on people means that you treat them below the position that Allaah has given them, not [according to] the position that you would like to give them. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given the man a very high position in the zawaadj compared to the woman. And this is in this world — as we have explained — for organising the division of tasks in the zawaadj. That means that the woman should deal with this position and accept this position. And the man should not misuse his leadership by demeaning the woman, by insulting her, reviling her, hitting her on her face, by — for example — not listening to her. And not listening means — literally — not listening: that he has no listening ear for her, which she needs for her tarbiyah. That is the meaning of not listening to her; not that «not listening» [is] that he does not do what she says. And especially in the presence of the children, then it is an even greater sin. For when the man demeans the mother in the presence of the children, the children will look down on her, and that also works [back] on him. His authority brings [the contempt] via the mother of the children to the children. And this also falls under the responsibility of the man, for the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «والرجلُ راعٍ في بيته، ومسؤولٌ عن رعيّته» — «And the man is a shepherd in his house, and responsible for his flock.» So it does not belong to leadership that the man demeans the woman, and most especially not in the presence of the children.
A strange story:
The teacher often encounters cases in which he had a suppressed laugh. A woman said to the teacher: «I want to be divorced from my husband; because he demeans me, does not appreciate me, does not give me attention.» The teacher said to her: How does he demean you? Give me an example with which he demeans you. She said: «Once he came home tired, sat down on the sofa and stretched out his leg, and while he was sitting there I went to clean the house. I was vacuuming with the vacuum cleaner. He put his legs on the sofa, and when I reached his legs, I said to him: ‹Move your legs away.› He said to me: ‹I am tired.› I said to him: ‹I am also tired, but I want you to move your legs away.› Then he said to me: ‹Fine, I will move my legs away› — and he put his legs on the sofa [again]. By that I felt demeaned.»
When you hear this story: who [is] the one demeaning the other? The way in which she speaks towards her husband is a demeaning way, and the fact that she cleans in his presence after he comes home — that is already a form of demeaning. You know that your husband comes home at such a moment, so you should allow him rest. That you then use the vacuum cleaner while he wants to rest, and then address him in this way — that is a form of kibr.
The teacher said to her: How does he insult you? Then the man said: I will tell it, and let her say whether I am telling the truth or not. «I often told her that the walls needed to be painted. Every time she says that she does not want to do that. So I took the bucket and started painting the walls. When she saw me, she snatched the paint roller from me and said: ‹Have you gone completely mad? What are you doing?› I said to her: ‹Sit down calmly, I am painting to make the house beautiful.› The man took the roller with the paint on it and said: ‹I will paint, and if you do not want me to paint, that is your business, then you should leave here; go to another room.› Then she said: ‹Yes, that is what happened: he goes and paints without me wanting it and without me having given permission for it.›»
Some scholars say: «شَرُّ البَلِيّةِ ما يُضحِك» — «The worst calamity is that which makes one laugh.»
The teacher said to her: How did he insult you? She said: «He said to me: go to another room.» [While] she said to him: «Have you gone completely mad?»
[There is] something going on here — what is happening here? [There is] a reversed perception. It appears here as if the woman takes on the role of the man, and she goes — on top of that — and also demeans him, insults him, and then finds that he has demeaned her. That [is] the world turned upside down. And after calming down, the teacher explained to her how she should deal with her husband, and she acknowledged that. So when someone thinks that he is the victim while he is the perpetrator, that is a problem. And sometimes [that] is also with the man, [that he] pretends to be the victim while he is the perpetrator. So the man should not misuse his leadership by demeaning the woman. And demeaning does not depend on how the woman feels, but depends on the guidelines of the legislation of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And sometimes the feeling of both the man and the woman is the problem.
5) Search in a positive way for the qualities of the partner.
Even though your husband or wife has indicated «this is what I love and this is what I detest», it is important that you also know: are [there] more things my husband/wife loves? Do that in a positive way. That means that you should not go and look for mistakes, instances of forgetfulness, and incorrect things. Do not go looking for that by saying: «See, you did that. See, you should not advise me; because you also do bad things yourself.» That is incorrect. For every person has the right to advise the other, however bad the other may be. So it is not right to run after the mistakes. [There is] a difference between bringing out the most beautiful in someone and running after the mistakes. How can I calm my partner? It is important that you examine how you can influence him in a positive way. How can I calm my husband in a positive way when he is angry? The woman should seek that more [than the man]. For the man often gets angry more than the woman. What things can I do at that moment, say, give, show him or let him hear [such that] he calms down? You can ask [your husband] about that, but you should also seek it out. And you do that with feeling, and sometimes by trying, but do not go provoking. So that you can also lead your partner to something else.
3aa-ishah did that too. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was very angry with her [because] she had gone out, followed him, and thought that he was going to another wife. Then she said: «O Messenger of Allaah, tell me what I should say when I visit the graves [the djanaazah]». For one of the important qualities of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam is that he came as a teacher, an educator. So if you know from your husband that when I ask him to teach me something connected to the context, he will also do that — whereby he focuses on something else and does not focus only on the negative. So the man should also do likewise.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam could also have said: «You were wasteful with the food, you did something incorrect.» [But] he smiled and turned [it] into positivity. He picked up the food from the ground and placed it before them. Turning the negative into the positive you do by trying, and before the zawaadj you do it with your little brothers, your little sisters, and your father and mother.
And in your zawaadj you should do that by first communicating about this. What do you find pleasant? What do you love? What calms you? When you utter beautiful words that come from your heart, not with an insincere heart and angry eyes. Do it with a sincere heart and smiling eyes, then [the matter] arrives. Be — as a woman — compliant, and be — as a man — merciful. And this is something that should — in reality — be done during the second phase of the zawaadj. That [is] the phase in which you go and test [probe] each other. After the rosy phase has passed, there the communication begins, and then you go and try to approach each other in a positive way in order to move from the negative towards the positive.
6) Make sure that you approach your partner in a beautiful/wonderful way.
Do that sometimes also when you are angry. How did the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam know that 3aa-ishah was angry? He would see or hear that from her, [in that] she says: «By the Lord of Ibraahiem.» And when she was pleased [happy], she would say: «By the Lord of Muhammad.» She said afterwards: «True, O Messenger of Allaah, I only leave out your name.» That means that she could not bear to leave him and leave his love, even though she had an anger within herself to which she had no right. That is a mistake that she herself also corrected afterwards. He sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said that he knows when she is angry and knows when she is pleased with him.
So even when 3aa-ishah made a mistake and was angry with the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, the only thing she left out [was] the name when she swore an oath. And even when she was angry, she approached the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam in a beautiful way. Why? So that the matter would not escalate more terribly, escalate even further.
7) Make sure that you never compare your partner with another.
And that you also never compare yourself with another. Both the man and the woman. And that you never go and compare your relationship with another. For that is one of the greatest sources of irritation, evil, unnecessary jealousy, and talaaq (divorce). [That] they say: «My friend received something from her friend, but I receive nothing at all», or [that] the man says: «She does that for him, and this for him, and you do nothing at all. What do you do for me?» That is a bad approach in communication, and also a bad approach in your head. Never go and do that in your head; because that can appear in speech.
And comparing with another ensures that you awaken in yourself unnecessary jealousy and envy (hasad), and that you create in yourself an unnecessary dislike towards your partner, and that you forget the blessings that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has bestowed on you in your partner. Those are all sins. And that you deny the good that you receive from your partner — and that is also a sin. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also rebuked the women for this. He sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said to them: «أَلَيس أنكنّ تَكفُرنَ العَشيرَ؟» — «Is it not [the case] that you are ungrateful to the husband?» And today very many men also do that. After some 20 years the man says: «I have never seen any good from you.» That is a major sin. And that is [something] because of which many women — and also men — are thrown into the Fire. And such behaviour occurs mostly among women. And unfortunately this behaviour also occurs often among men.
And when you also do that, it means that you have no self-confidence — whether you are a man or a woman — and that you have no appreciation for yourself. And comparing your partner with another or [comparing] your relationship with another relationship will also lead to depression. For you will not be able to reach exactly the same as the other. So that ensures that you become depressed, while you can draw a great deal of positivity out of your own relationship. Every person [has] his own situation, his own life, his own growth, his own rizq (provision). Do not go comparing yourself with another. That will lead to you destroying your relationship.
And when you want something from your partner, it is important that you entice [attract] your partner to it in a way that is permissible within Islaam. And that is possible by means of your gentleness as a man, and your femininity as a woman, or by means of a form of persuasive power that you have been granted — and if you have not been granted it, then you should learn it. And we will learn how we can convince each other, in shaa-a Allaah.
Questions
Question: A question about the phase [that comes] before the zawaadj, [that comes] even before the first introductory conversation. In the sister's environment [there is] a convert sister who is in contact — via another sister and her husband — with a brother who is interested in entering the zawaadj with her, via the man. They have not yet had an introductory conversation, but quite a lot of questions are being asked which the sister thinks would better be asked during the first introductory conversation. Many questions are asked back and forth directed towards entering the zawaadj, and the sister thinks they should be asked during the introductory conversation. She can no longer find the lesson, and wants to ask the teacher what advice he gives in this.
Answer: The shaykh's advice in this is that the questions asked via e-mail or the app, those questions asked [should] be limited only to the questions with which one weighs up: do I want to enter a first conversation or not. Questions such as, for example, the general personal data: how old someone is, what the preference of that [person] — if it is a man — is for the woman, and if it is a woman, [her preference] for the man, what background he/she has. If [the matter] is limited to those questions and both come to the conclusion that they want to know more about each other and want to have a conversation, then the follow-up questions will be in the first conversation. And the important questions for the first conversation: do you perform the salaah, do you wear the correct hidjaab. This [is] the advice the teacher gives from experience, and that does not mean that no other questions may be asked.
Question: Rebuking the woman.
Answer: Rebuking the woman [comes] after the three steps. The man should take into consideration the way in which he rebukes her. And she may not say that she is not a type [type]. And the way in which the man rebukes the woman should be within the pleasure of Allaah. That means that he does not rebuke her in the presence of the children, does not demean his wife, humiliate her, revile her, or be utterly unjust in the way he speaks with her. And that is not for the woman to assess, rather [the matter] is for a person of knowledge to assess. And the man can and should judge whether he is being just or not. If he fulfils this condition, then the woman may be rebuked. And rebuking means that the man shows that he is angry. That means that the woman has already gone much too far and is already in the phase of the major sins. And the rebuke can also be [that] the man sometimes addresses the woman as if he is bringing up a child. And there is no harm in that, and the woman should also accept it. And the woman who does not accept that [is] someone who does not have the correct humility. And the man may do this because he is responsible for the deeds of his wife, and responsible for the treatment of his wife and the tarbiyah of his wife. If she does not accept that, then it means that no tarbiyah is possible in the zawaadj, and — in reality — no zawaadj is possible either.
Question: The woman [has] towards the man only the following steps that she can follow: teaching, reminding, admonishing, and once again/continuing the admonishing. Is that correct?
Answer: That is correct.
Question: May the man shout when rebuking?
Answer: The man may shout, but shouting is not a good, fitting way; but it is not impermissible, unless one is fasting. Then he may not shout. And outside of fasting he may shout, but it is not something Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa loves. And when the children also hear that, it comes close to the limit of what is not permissible. For the children may not hear the mother being approached in this way. That will only be to the detriment of the tarbiyah of the children.
Question: The sister had a question about taking lessons with a man. May she let a man test [examine] her in the recitation of the Qur'aan?
Answer: The scholars have multiple opinions on that. When [the woman] is engaged in reciting the Qur'aan, she should beautify her voice. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «ليس مِنّا من لم يَتَغَنَّ بالقرآن» — «He is not of us who does not recite the Qur'aan melodiously.» And the beautifying of the voice the man should not hear. That [is] the 3awrah part of the voice. So when the woman beautifies her voice, that is a form of 3awrah that the man may not hear, and that is why some scholars have said that it is not permissible — when the man is young and can be tempted by these beautiful voices — for this woman to go and teach him. And [there are] in our time enough women who teach women the Qur'aan. So if the woman sees that and has knowledge of it, then she should also do that. To read the Qur'aan, to receive its correction through a woman. For in our time [there are] also WhatsApp groups, via the internet, via al-Madienah [the illuminated city], and also in the Netherlands [there are] female teachers who teach women how they can pronounce the Qur'aan in the correct way.
[Follow-up question:] So should you do everything you can to find a female teacher?
[Answer:] If [the matter concerns] the recitation of the Qur'aan, then you should give everything to find a certified (mudjaazah) female teacher. And if the [teaching] woman comes from another city, [then you do that] via Skype, or via the telephone, or in another way.
[Follow-up question:] And if you want to obtain your idjaazah (certificate of authorisation) so that you yourself can teach others?
[Answer:] The idjaazah is a form of certificate with which you are recognised as a teacher of the Qur'aan. It is a form of certificate with a sanad [chain] going back to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And the idjaazah does not mean [only] a chain, but means a certificate, a form of accreditation [recognition]. And [there are] also women who do this via the telephone, and with that you can obtain a certificate.
8) Make sure that you continually praise each other instead of only complaining about each other.
In principle the culture of complaining should be banished. For every form of complaining brings with it only negativity. And by complaining the teacher means: enumerating/mentioning and repeating everything that goes wrong. That ensures a very negative atmosphere [in which] we are influenced by what is heard. If we keep complaining every time only about what does not go well, then we go and influence each other in a negative way, whereby the heart goes and focuses only on negativity. And the culture of complaining is a culture that has been implanted in us/that we have absorbed from the kuffaar; because the kuffaar do not believe in Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, nor in the Hereafter, nor in the mercy of Allaah, nor in the fact that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will hold us all to account on the Day of Judgement. [They do not believe] that if we have patience — instead of going and complaining — [we are rewarded], [nor] in the raising of ranks in Paradise when we have patience. The kaafir (disbeliever) does not believe in that. So when we are among them in the workplace, in the schools, and take a lot from them, then we will take that on as a habit as if all of that were fine, and we will forget how Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam taught us to deal with these matters.
And what is very important: when something goes wrong, that we do not go and mention it, that we do not say «that went wrong». [Rather] we say then: «قَدَّر اللهُ وما شاء فَعَل» — «Allaah has decreed, and what He wills, He does.» Thereby we will no longer return to the past, but we will learn from the past. Make sure that you do not blame each other; because blaming is complaining. If someone has made a mistake, then say to that [person]: make sure that you show remorse. Do not remain hanging in the negative. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوْبَةًۭ نَّصُوحًا﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «O you who believe, repent to Allaah with a sincere repentance.» (Soerat At-Tahriem, verse 8) Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa addresses — from the beginning, when He addresses the believers — [in a positive way]; because in the preceding verse He addresses the disbelievers. So Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa addresses the believers directly in a positive way.
And also [in] another verse, directly when Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa warns against the mistakes committed by the people of Loet, Noeh and Saalih, He says afterwards: ﴿وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «And ask forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him.» (Soerat Hoed, verse 90) And thus in all the verses in which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa addresses the believers and warns them against bad matters, He subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says directly: «And repent, perform the istighfaar (asking for forgiveness).» Try to always speak towards the positive, and do not keep complaining about each other or yourself.
Try to teach your tongue the habit of the following dhikr (remembrance), namely «al-hamdu-li-llaah». And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has described the sahaabah in the earlier Books as the grateful ones, because they say «al-hamdu-li-llaah» often. So when you have — for example — pain in your back, your leg, wherever: «I will take medicine, al-hamdu-li-llaah. Allaah has cured me of that pain, al-hamdu-li-llaah.» With that you have praised Allaah, not complained, and performed a du3aa-e for yourself. But when you say: «I have a lot of headaches, I have to toil every day, I have very much work», then you only go and make yourself depressed, and you place yourself and others in a negative atmosphere [in which] they are prompted [stirred] to also go along with that negative atmosphere. Say «al-hamdu-li-llaah», and also remind others of «al-hamdu-li-llaah».
And it is also very important that we try more to appreciate each other's good deeds and to perform a du3aa-e for them: «Tabaaraka-llaah (blessed is Allaah), may Allaah raise you in Paradise, I see that you are performing dhikr, maa shaa-a Allaah, may Allaah keep you constant in that deed.» And when you yourself perform a good deed, say to yourself: «Al-hamdu-li-llaah, that Allaah has guided us to this wonderful deed.» How many [people] has Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa not guided to the salaah! Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has guided us to the siyaam (fasting). It is self-evident because it is obligatory, but it is a guidance from Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And the fact that you remind each other — gives you more iemaan and also gives the other more iemaan. Attribute everything to Allaah when you see something good. And attribute everything bad to yourself, and say: «We should improve ourselves.» This is — once again — a positive approach.
When someone does something for you, thank him. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «من لا يَشكُر الناسَ لا يَشكُر اللهَ» — «Whoever does not thank the people does not thank Allaah.» Why? Thanking the people is also a form of thanking Allaah; because with that you also acknowledge the good that others have given you.
Try to thank your wife or your husband. Try to awaken the positive atmosphere, and especially for the men. That is a very important matter for the men — that they praise their wives a lot; because that is one of the matters that also cause a big gap between the man and the woman. The woman should do everything she does for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and not wait for the appreciation of her husband. But the appreciation of the man is an obligation from the man towards the woman, as we just covered in the hadieth.
When your wife has cooked for you but used less salt or sugar than usual, thank her; because she has made an effort. And also try to remind her of her ikhlaas. For the more you thank, the more your wife will be of service to you. And likewise the man. The more often the man hears thanks from the woman with a du3aa-e, the more closely [connected] he becomes with his wife, and the better the relationship becomes. And the woman should also make sure to give the man the best welcome and allow him his rest when he comes from his work, [or] comes from a journey. Do not make complaining a fixed routine. Do not make it so that when he enters the house [you say]: «The children, I had to do so much» etc. It is fine to unburden your heart, but you do not do that by means of complaining.
Thank Allaah that He has given you this occupation; because [there are] many women who have no occupation for themselves, and so they become depressed and go on antidepressants. Instead of that, you have received these opportunities when you use them for the sake of Allaah. They are doors to reward. The pain you feel, the effort you make, and the things you do — [are] doors for you to raise your ranks in Paradise. And these doors shield you from evil (from all the waswaas). [For example] that a woman has a very severe pathological obsession [with cleanliness], or goes and grinds away a lot within herself, gets many doubts, gets many bad whisperings because she has nothing to do — or rather, has no goals that she has established for herself. Make sure that you see these doors as positive. That you can get rid of the illness, and that you count it with Allaah so that you are rewarded for it.
When we count [reckon] our thinking [with Allaah], we see that the world looks completely different from before. Then we see the world from another perspective. Make sure that you welcome your husband when he comes home by beautifying yourself, calming your children, giving each [one] his task, smiling, taking things [from him] when he comes home, and having prepared his place of rest, so that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa rewards you. If you treat him like this, then he will also treat you like this.
Do not show your displeasure except when it has value, that is, when you are engaged in improving something. So we should not show our displeasure at the least and smallest of matters. The big mistakes or the mistakes in the religion you should not complain about, rather you should improve them. And the small mistakes, when they occur often, it is important that they are spoken about, but not in a complaining way but in a positive way.
9) Do not go looking for the concealed mistakes.
When you discover a mistake in your partner while he/she has concealed it, he is closer to tawbah than someone who does it openly. Imagine that your husband does something but wants to conceal it from you — that is something positive; because it means that he is ashamed before you and has shame. If it is concealed, then he is closer to tawbah than if he did it openly. And whoever commits his sins openly [is] a mudjaahir (one who makes [his sins] public). The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «كلُّ أُمّتي مُعافًى إلا المُجاهِرين» — «All of my ummah (community) will be pardoned/spared except the mudjaahiroen (those who make their sins public).» Who [are] the mudjaahiroen? They are those whom Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has concealed and who then uncover [it] the next morning by speaking about it. This the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said. And it is a hadieth narrated by the Imaam al-Bukhaarie and the Imaam Muslim.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also indicates that those who make their sins public, speak about them or commit them in public, are further from the cure of these sins than those who conceal themselves. When someone conceals himself, try to advise him in general terms.
For example: the man hides himself from his wife when he looks at bad films or incorrect images. Then it is important that the woman makes clear to him that everything we see and hear — Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will hold us to account for it. And she should beautify herself more for him; because the fact that he looks at other women means that he is missing something in her. And it can also be that the woman is missing something in the man. And when this sin is not a major sin, then he should approach her in general terms, admonish her; but when he sees that it occurs often, then he should say something about it.
And the repetition of a minor sin is a major sin. Then the woman and the man should say something about it to the partner. When you discover a mistake in your partner and he wants to conceal it, it is important that you conceal that and do not make him confess it openly; but if you see it often, that you then admonish him concretely [specifically].
You should — in any case — conceal each other. And a sin between you and Allaah you do not have to share [with your partner] if it has no effect on the family. Make sure that you show remorse quickly; because every sin — nevertheless — has a direct or indirect effect on the family. And when you do not reach [a solution] by yourself, it is important that you ask a person of knowledge so that you know how you should deal with such a sin.
10) Make sure that you make your partner happy.
«I want to make my partner happy.» Even more, [there is] a wonderful hadieth. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam indicates in a hadieth what the value of this is. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says in a hadieth declared authentic by the Imaam al-Albaanie and narrated by 3abdullaah ibn 3umar: he said: a man came to the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. He said: «O Messenger of Allaah, which people are most beloved to Allaah, and which deeds are most beloved to Allaah?» The Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «أَحَبُّ الناس إلى الله أَنفَعُهم للناس» — «The most beloved people to Allaah are those most beneficial to the people.» That is, those who give the most benefit to the people. «And the most beloved deeds to Allaah are: a joy that you bring into a Muslim, or that you remove a distress from him, or drive away a hunger from him, or pay off a debt for him.»
Then the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said (and the hadieth still continues): «And that I walk with a brother of mine for a need [of his] is more beloved to me than performing i3tikaaf (retreat for worship) in this mosque of mine — in al-Madienah — for a month.» Then the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «And whoever restrains his anger, Allaah will cover his shortcoming; and whoever suppresses his rage — while if he wished to carry it out he could have carried it out — Allaah will fill his heart with contentment [on the Day of Judgement]; and whoever walks with his brother for a need until he has completed it for him, Allaah will make his feet firm on the Day when feet slip [the Day of Judgement].» This [is] the whole hadieth.
And what concerned us [here is]: «The most beloved deeds are a joy that you bring into a Muslim.» This [is] with a Muslim in general, so how about your husband? Your wife? So one of the most beloved deeds to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is that you make your partner happy. And some are difficult about that: «He does not do that with me, so why should I do it?» [Do it] for yourself. So that you perform the most beloved deeds to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
11) Make sure that you trust each other by sharing everything with each other.
Share everything with each other. As partners you should share everything with each other. And especially the woman with the man. There may not be a private matter — from [the moment of] your entering the zawaadj there is no private world, your private affair, your private matter. You should share everything with each other. That also ensures a close bond.
12) Make sure that you give your purity and cleanliness a high priority.
When you are not clean, and you almost always have dirty/filthy hands, or hands always smeared with car oil, painting work, the smell of onion, the smell of garlic, the smell of «ras el-hanout», and the smell of everything and anything — then your partner does not want to come close to you, and if he wants to, he is hindered by these things. Make sure that you do not open doors that the shaytaan misuses. So your tahaarah (purity) should have a high priority in your life. And some men/women find great hardship in that, because they have to make a lot of effort for it.
13) Make sure that you give everything you have to keep psychological worries and their causes outside the house.
That negativity we spoke about — that the woman has nothing to do in the house, that the man loiters around the house all day, that one urinates in the bathroom [without cleaning], that no dhikr is performed. From both the man and the woman. One should have fun [enjoyment] when one is at home, feel safe when one is at home. From the man['s side, that he] does not hear complaining or grumbling every day [«nothing goes well»], and also from the man['s side, that he] is not only occupied with searching for or seeking out people's mistakes, whereby the atmosphere of the house becomes a hell — and that is not right. Make sure that you have at home a safe home for everyone.
These worries you can combat by performing the adhkaar (remembrances), and by not isolating yourself, and by having the right people [around you], by seeking out the right company. And the man can — when he is outside — also communicate with his wife in the best way so that his wife does not become isolated, especially in the first years when she does not yet have an occupation with her children. Make sure that you have a programme at home: cleaning, adhkaar, teaching, hygiene — all these matters should be in a programme in the house so that the shaytaan gains no influence. Fill your time with the obligatory deeds, the recommended deeds and the permissible deeds so that you also have no time to think about the disliked matters, let alone the forbidden matters.
Set up your programme as a woman or a man. For it is sensible for the woman — especially in her first years — to have a programme when she is at home, and to fill her day with that with which she can invest for the coming years. And one of the positive consequences of such a programme is that it also helps you to forget the pains, forget the injustice, or forget the longing for your parents.
Step 1: Forget it. Step 2: Do not let yourself be reminded of it. Step 3: Conceal the feeling (do not speak about it). Step 4: Focus on the positive matters so that you no longer have time to bring out the negative matters.
14) Draw lessons from negative events.
From every negative event in your life you can draw many lessons, but you can also draw lessons from the mistakes of others. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam — when he wanted to advise someone — said: «Do not be like so-and-so: he used to stand [in prayer] at night and then left the night prayer.» And that was 3abdullaah ibn 3umar. When 3abdullaah ibn 3umar heard that, he never again left the night prayer. So you learn from the mistakes of others, and you also learn from your own mistakes. And all of that is positive. And sometimes you ask people: «What are you thinking about?» [They say:] «I do not know, I was not thinking about anything. I saw a cloud, and I thought I was on that cloud, then I was at the market buying something, then at the South Pole.» So your thoughts have no order and no structure. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given you the faculty of thought to invest it well, by thinking about how you can improve yourself, learning from the mistakes of others, how you can plan your day, how you can reflect on the creation — not to dream about all sorts of things while you yourself do not even know where you are. Those people the teacher does not understand and does not want to understand. How can you not use your faculty of thought to invest it in the right way? Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa addresses us in the Qur'aan with «oeloe-l-albaab», and those are the people of understanding. You too, use your intellect, and do not grow tired [weary] when you go and think.
15) And another important matter [is] «do not dig up old cases» [literally in the original: do not pull old cows out of the ditch], [also] at escalation.
The matters that passed long ago, were dealt with, were talked about many times. When there are problems, the man, like the woman, goes and digs up the old cases again. They are old bodies that passed away long ago and you pull them out of the grave again. These matters ensure problems that are impossible to solve when you bring back the old matters every time.
When Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa accepts the tawbah of a servant, it is not for us to let this sin come up for mention again. Every time something goes wrong, remind each other of tawbah. «Have you shown remorse? Saafie [good], then we erase it. We talked about that long ago and it has passed.» In this way it is easy to forgive matters and forget them. What are the problems now? Not what the problems were 15 years ago. For when you store up the pains and also do not remove them, the bond between you and your partner will not be close, will not be good, and cannot be made close. And the trust will also be removed.
The teacher wants to stop here. And next week we will continue with more advices. We stopped at «do not pull old cows out of the ditch».
Questions
Question: How about a sin — when you know that he is not addressed [held to account] for the sin when he does it — should you then address him about it?
Answer: When he conceals himself and you find out, then you should leave him concealed and admonish in general terms. And when you find out — without spying; because spying (tadjassus) is in itself a major sin — that he repeats [the sin] again, then you should — indeed — address him about it.
Question: At the point «make sure that you praise each other instead of complaining about each other» — about welcoming the man when he comes home. How can the unmarried sisters train for that?
Answer: You should prepare yourself for meeting your parents when you are outside the house or when they are outside the house. When they are outside the house, that you go and prepare their place of rest and that with which they find it pleasant to be welcomed, and in any case with a sincere smile from the heart. Even if they have only been away a few minutes or hours, [it is] the same. You welcome them with a du3aa-e, with gratitude, with beautiful words. Do not go saying to yourself: «They will find that exaggerated.» Every beautiful word they find pleasant, even if they say the opposite; keep saying it. And when you are outside and come in, also meet your parents with beautiful words. Choose the most beautiful words that they would love to hear. And do that also with your older brothers and older sisters; because in this way you go and accustom yourself to it, whereby it also becomes automatic for your husband. Do it with ikhlaas; with that you can also keep it up.
Question: The zakaah (obligatory charity) on wealth. May you also give it to a relative who has no income or [has] a low income? The relative [is] the brother or sister.
Answer: No, that is not permissible. The zakaah — as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam calls it — is the surplus [the filth] of wealth, with which you purify the wealth. That you do not give to your brother or your sisters. To your brother or your sisters you give from your money as sadaqah or as a gift. And the people who are in debt you may give zakaah, but not [if they are] from your family.
[Follow-up question:] Does it apply to first-degree family that it is not permissible?
[Answer:] To other countries [the zakaah] may not go. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «فإن هم أَطاعوا لذلك، فأَعلِمهم أن الله افترض عليهم صدقةً تُؤخَذ من أَغنيائهم وتُرَدّ على فُقَرائهم» — «If they obey in that, then inform them that Allaah has made obligatory upon them a charity that is taken from their rich and returned to their poor.» So the zakaah of Yemen should go from Yemen to Yemen, and from the Netherlands to the Netherlands, and it may not be sent to other countries. So a general answer cannot be given now.
Question: When you have reached the nisaab (the minimum amount) and [the money] was in your possession for longer than a year. When a year has passed, you should look at that moment and give 2.5% of it.
Answer: You look [after] a year at what you had. If you do not know exactly how much, then you should make a positive estimate, that is, that you estimate more than what you think [the reality] is.
Question: The sister understood that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and the people of his household and his descendants did not accept sadaqah, only as a gift. How about that if someone points to that and says that he does not want to accept sadaqah?
Answer: The descendants of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam may not accept sadaqah. Al-Hasan once took a date and tried to eat it, whereupon the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam took it from him and said: «كِخ كِخ» (that is: that is dirty). He said to him: «This is the surplus of the people's wealth, and Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has forbidden it to us.» That means that he knows with certainty that he is one of the descendants of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And this prohibition applies to the descendants of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And you can change your intention and say that it is a gift.
[Question:] Does it not apply to «ordinary» people?
[Answer:] For the people who do not descend from the Prophet [sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam], sadaqah is not forbidden.
[Follow-up question:] And if someone — nevertheless — wants to follow them in this without being a descendant of the Prophet, is that correct?
[Answer:] You may not do it as an act of 3ibaadah for Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Homework
Organise your notes.
Examine at each advice you have received how you can prepare yourself if you are not yet married, and if you are married, then make sure that you discuss all these advices with your partner, and that together you begin working on at least three of these advices.
The thirty-sixth lesson — Sunday 4 November 2018
Homework (28 October 2018)
Organise your notes.
Examine at each advice you have received how you can prepare yourself if you are not yet married, and if you are married, then make sure that you discuss all these advices with your partner, and that together you begin working on at least three of these advices.
Discussion of the homework (4 November 2018)
Student 1
A sister has begun working on a number of points.
1. Avoiding provocative communication.
Avoiding provocative communication with her family members, avoiding conflicts, avoiding clashing topics. She wants to train on this by applying the points mentioned above. And she has gone and trained on this. At the moment when a conflict is about to occur, for example with a little sister or a little brother, the sister tried to make sure that [the matter] does not escalate by not responding to it [not entering into it]. If that did not help, she left the place where the disagreement occurs. This is how she trained on this point. And with regard to this point [in relation] to the parents: she did not respond [did not enter into the matter] when her mother was angry with her [because] she found that she had helped her too little in the house during that period. And when the sister's mother is angry, she goes and shows that by recounting it time after time in her presence, speaking then in the third person. The sister did not respond to that. If [it] went on too long, she asked in a sighing way [with a sigh] for [her mother] to stop it, [while] she knows that that was not right. If it kept going on for a long time, she left the place and went to her room.
The teacher: Keeping the other quiet [calm], or trying to give everything you have to make that other calm and pleased — when you say nothing about it, did that help anything? No. For usually [it] is seen as you ignoring the message that the other is recounting, not taking it seriously, as if you pretend that there is nothing [going on], as if you are innocent. And in principle that is provocative behaviour. In the advices we have learned — with regard to the one who has authority over you — you should give everything you have to take that [person] seriously, keep him calm, and please him. The fact that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given the mother a high right, especially with regard to good companionship [the good company] — means that you should give everything you have to please your mother at that moment as she would like and in the way she would like, and that you also correct your mistake, improve yourself. For at the moment that your mother is angry with you, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is angry with you. So when you ignore [the matter], you are — in reality — ignoring even the anger of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And then it does not matter to you — so it appears — as if it does not matter to you whether Allaah is angry or not angry with you. When your mother stands before you angry with you and you know that you are guilty — when your mother has ordered something simple and you have not done it — then you should think: Allaah is angry with me. The fact that my mother flares up at me like this means that Allaah is angrier with me to the measure of her anger. That you should care about, and so [it is] with everyone who has authority over you. That is a way in which you can prepare yourself for your marital relationship with your husband. Instead of taking your husband's anger seriously, it appears as if you make him even angrier by ignoring him and not taking him seriously, and then walking off to another room. And what strikes the teacher is that she says: «In the past I used to say to my mother: ‹Stop [it]›, in a sighing voice.» And that is striking; because in our time it is — literally — trained at school to say this to the father or mother: «Stop, quit it, I do not like this.» And the matter [concerns] the pleasure of the mother, on which the pleasure of Allaah depends. Not [what] the child finds pleasant.
You should imagine: «Allaah is angry with me to the measure of my mother's anger. Allaah is angry with me to the measure of my husband's anger.» So the angrier your father, your mother, or your husband is with you, the angrier you have made Allaah. And some people think to themselves: «I did not do anything. You are making yourself angry.» No, the fact that he is angry is already in itself a major sin. The fact that that [person] is not pleased is already in itself a major sin. And your reverence for your mother, your father and your husband does not [mean] that you determine when he may be angry and when not. [Rather it means] that when he is angry, you care about pleasing him and calming him. 3umar ibn al-KHattaab used to stand up for justice in a magnificent way. When he saw that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was angry, he said: «We believe in Allaah and in the Messenger, we believe in Allaah and in the Messenger.» And he also said: «We hear and we obey.» He kept saying that until the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam calmed down in his anger. You can — indeed — think: «There is nothing [going on], I did not do anything.» At that moment you are the assessor of your parents [and] your husband, and then there is no longer a relationship of tarbiyah.
Questions
Question: When your parents are angry with you and you are silent. Imagine that your mother or father — precisely — wants your silence when they get angry — is that then counted as ignoring, or as pleasing your parents when they get angry?
Answer: It is important that the son or daughter assesses his parents well when they get angry. If they know that «if I keep silent now, look at the ground, do not take on a provocative posture, and behave in a humble way, I will calm them» — then [that is] not a provocative posture. But if [the matter] is mere ignoring for the sake of ignoring, as if there is nothing [going on], [and] you offer no apology, do not calm that [person], walk to another room — then that is — indeed — a provocative posture. So however your parents find [the matter] pleasant at that moment, that is how you should also please them.
Follow-up question: Imagine that they expect different postures (one moment they want you to say something, another not). How should you deal with this?
Answer: You give everything you have to calm them. If you have not made the right assessment [and] you notice that, then you change your posture to an even humbler posture. At that moment you should — especially from your heart — be sincere towards Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and towards the one who has authority over you. When you are sincere, the other will also feel that. When you are sincere and humble in your words, you try to please that [person]. Not only to keep him quiet; because that [means]: «Calm down, nothing happened.» So the teacher does not mean keeping him quiet but pleasing him. «My dear mother, what can I do to put this right?» Kiss her on her head, kiss her on her hand, and ask: what can I do to put this right?
You cannot say: «I will make the assessment that my mother has no right to be angry.» Then you are guilty; because such an assessment you cannot make. That assessment [is based] on kibr, not on sincerity and humility towards your parents [whereby] you do not go and determine whether they may shout or not, whether they may be angry or not.
Student 2
The sister wrote down all the advices for herself in an ordered way. And we have discussed 15 advices. [She looked at] what she can practise and what not. Very many steps she was already able to put into practice. And many situations [revolve] around communication, and around how you should deal with it when something happens. And there were also points such as that you should approach your partner in a beautiful way, make sure that you make him happy. The sister took a flower [bouquet] for her mother, who was happy with it. And she had resolved to tidy something up, [and] she was lying in bed, but decided — nevertheless — to tidy it up now in order to make her happy with it. These are things she practised this week.
The teacher: At the moment you thought «I will make my mother happy» — at that moment, did you think «I will do something noble towards my mother», or «I am doing what Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa asks of me and has made obligatory upon me»?
The sister indicates that she did it to make her mother happy. [He said:] Imagine that your mother was not happy, what would the sister's reaction be then? The sister finds that a difficult question. [He said:] Imagine that your mother said: «You did not do this well, you should have done it much earlier.» How do you feel then? [She said:] Then I would feel — deep inside — disappointed. [He said:] [Rather,] that is — in reality — actually not correct; because you are performing a deed for your mother for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, so the result should not matter [be important] then; because it does not diminish your deed: you have — in shaa-a Allaah — already obtained [the reward] with that deed. The reaction to it does not — in shaa-a Allaah — change anything about that.
The teacher: If I say «I will make my mother happy» with a feeling of «I will do something noble for her», then I am wrong; because then I am engaged in doing something in an arrogant way, perhaps without noticing it. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has commanded you — when your mother finds something pleasant — that it is obligatory upon you to do it. When you seek nearness [qurbah] to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and seek only the nearness to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and go and make your mother happy — then you do not feel as if you are noble towards your mother, doing something good for your mother, and you will not receive a disappointment if you should have done something better, but rather you will become happier; because your mother shows you when you can receive even more reward.
The sister says that this reminds her of a case the teacher discussed about a sister who for years did things for the sake of her family or for the sake of her own satisfaction instead of the pleasure of Allaah. You can do something for yourself by saying: «Look, I did something good.» That will enlarge his kibr. And that is why ikhlaas is a medicine for everything: for kibr, hasad (envy), everything. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is most pleased with the one who works with ikhlaas; because that [is] the Tawhied (the Oneness of Allaah) for which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa created us.
[The teacher:] Precisely at the moment when your parents say: «Well done, but you can still do such-and-such better» — you should then have a feeling that you are receiving more opportunities to multiply your hasanaat. As if someone says to you: «Here, you have products, sell them, you may take everything as long as you sell them.» Then the same person comes to you and says: «You bought the products — yes — but you could have received much more money, so next time you can make the products in a better way to earn even more from those products.» This is how you should go along with the reward of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Another sister responds to that: she indicates that for her the matter is not [about] praise. She does not need to hear that she has done something well. And how [it] came across to the sister [is] that she could never do [it] well, and that ensures — nevertheless — a lack of confidence [in oneself], for example cooking or cleaning. «My mother remains dissatisfied.» The sister wants to learn how she should deal with this.
The teacher: The fact that her mother remains dissatisfied should motivate her to do it even better, and to ask her: how can I do it better? Instead of going and saying «you remain dissatisfied» — those are the whisperings of the shaytaan. And later those whisperings are converted into «she will never be satisfied, so I will not do my best to do it better». And later [the whisperings become] «I will warn my sister in advance before she also goes and despairs; because I will then say to her: ‹My mother will never be satisfied, so you should not have the ambition for that›.» This is how the danger spreads. But when we look at [the matter] in a positive way for the sake of Allaah: «My mother wants me to do it even better, so I will do it even better. As long as I keep striving to please my mother, I have in any case pleased Allaah. And at the moment I stop keeping on pleasing my mother, Allaah will also stop being pleased. I will ask my mother: how can I do it better? I will keep striving to please my mother.» When that is your attitude, the attitude of your mother will — 100% — also be completely different, and she will be happy with you, just when she sees that you are making the effort for her for the sake of Allaah. And that applies (later) to the husband as well.
For the shaytaan then ensures irritation between the daughter and the mother, and screens the sister off from the pleasure of Allaah.
The teacher: «My striving to please her [is] my 3ibaadah.» Is that not a beautiful paradise we would then be in? That is a completely different thinking from the thinking of the shaytaan who whispers at that moment.
Sister 3
The sister is in telephone contact with her husband, because he is abroad for a long period. And he is very considerate of her. And she praises her husband. And last week the sister found that the biggest lesson [was] the culture of complaining, [and] that you do not pull old cows out of the ditch. For after the tawbah that sin no longer [exists] either.
Questions
Question: What did 3umar ibn al-KHattaab say — in translation — when the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was angry, until the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam calmed down in his anger?
Answer: «We believe in Allaah and in the Messenger, we believe in Allaah and in the Messenger.» And he also said: «We hear and we obey.»
Question: [There are] also practical points that you can prepare with your parents with regard to the partner points. Sit with them and discuss what they find pleasant, what they do not find pleasant, what irritates [bothers them] and what does not, and how you can remove the irritation. This should have happened before between the parent and the child, but — unfortunately — that does not happen. The sister indicates that they were brought up in a different way, so she also finds it difficult to act; because you have never done that.
Answer: When you see your father calm, you go and open a talk [a chat] in a father/daughter way, in a humble or light-hearted way. So then you open a conversation. And it would also be good for your mother to be present, [and] the rest of the brothers and sisters, to raise — nevertheless — such matters. And all the thresholds [barriers] that you have you should ignore. You are your father's daughter, and you can simply hold such conversations. When we were at the table with our parents, we would ask: «Father, would you like us to do such-and-such, how can we please you regarding such-and-such?» And sometimes matters were discussed [about] how one should be in one's heart.
When the father receives such conversations from his son or daughter, it is important that he does not get angry, for he will then feel much more connected with his children. And that also ensures that he will feel more responsibility towards his children. The more he gets to know them, the more responsibility the father feels. For in many families the parents do not know their children. They do not know how they think, they do not know how they feel, they do not know why they think [or] feel certain things, how they can convince them, what opportunities [they have] to motivate them — nevertheless — to do good. And that is why they do not feel the responsibility to direct [guide] them in the right way.
Many parents say: «As long as you do not come home with a swollen belly [pregnant], you may go out.» Those are parents to whom [the matter] does not matter. And [there are] also parents to whom it does — indeed — matter that [their children] do not [associate with] boys, but «you should wear the hidjaab». And yet a step higher: wearing the hidjaab when going out, [and] no contact with boys.
