Omdat hij dat werk heeft geaccepteerd met de acceptatie dat hij een grote zonde begaat — anders zou hij niet in dat werk aanwezig zijn — is zijn werk dan haraam. Of [bijvoorbeeld] dat hem gezegd wordt dat hij niet mag bidden, en hij daarmee instemt — dan zijn zijn werk en zijn inkomen haraam. En heel veel mensen denken niet zo ver. De mensen denken: «Het product waar ik mee bezig ben is halaal, ik steel niet, dus mijn werk is halaal.» Dat is een tekortschietende wijze van beoordelen.
En de sadaqah die je uitgeeft [heeft] ook een prioriteit. Ga je er op de juiste wijze mee om of niet? Deze zaken zijn heel belangrijk in de wijze van omgaan met geld. Koop je — bijvoorbeeld — op een halaal wijze? Wanneer heb je dat gekocht? Op de vrijdag (djumu3ah). Hoe laat? Om half twee. Waar heb je het gekocht? Bij een man. Die man had jou niet mogen verkopen [tijdens het vrijdaggebed]. Deze verkoop is niet toegestaan, en als je dat [voedsel] eet, dan eet je haraam. Enzovoort. Leer dus omgaan met geld. En het geld is ook iets wat veel partners irriteert [stoort] en voor veel mensen veel barrières vormt.
20) Zorg ervoor dat je de negativiteit vermijdt en haar uit je leven verwijdert.
Negativiteit leidt tot een lakse [defaitistische] houding. En zoals in veel ahaadieth gehoord en gezien is, was de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam nooit negatief. Bijvoorbeeld Anas ibn Maalik was een dienaar/bediende bij de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. Hij was nog klein, heel jong, bij de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. Hij zegt: De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam heeft mij nooit verwijten gemaakt, mij nooit gevraagd: «Waarom heb je dat gedaan?» of «waarom heb je dat niet gedaan?» Hij was altijd positief. Deze houding — de slechte houding, de defaitistische houding — wordt vaak vertaald in het gedrag [doordat] men roept dat men niets kan. «Ik kan het niet, ik heb mijn best gedaan.» Die [persoon] zegt — in werkelijkheid — «ik wil het niet doen». Daarmee troost die [persoon] zichzelf. Je hoort niet [alleen] «je best te doen», maar je hoort «het te doen». Het maximale eruit te halen. «ما أمرتُكم به فأتوا منه ما استَطَعتُم» — «Wat ik jullie heb opgedragen, doe daarvan wat jullie kunnen.» Uit dat [defaitisme] komt het verwaarlozen van de verantwoordelijkheden voort.
En wat heel belangrijk is, is dat je niet hoort op te geven. Ook al lukt [het] niet. [Maar] juist doorgaan. En ook bij het adviseren van je partner. En daarbij hoor je Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa om hulp te vragen. De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt: «استَعِن بالله ولا تَعجِز» — «Zoek hulp bij Allaah en geef niet op [wees niet machteloos].» Dat betekent: vertrouw op Allaah, vraag Allaah om je te helpen, en zorg ervoor dat je je uiterste best laat zien. Dan zeg je: «O Allaah, help mij», en ga je het opnieuw proberen. En dit houdt ook verband met het goede vermoeden over Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Volgende week zullen we spreken over de rest van de punten. En hierna komt het hoofdstuk van de communicatie in de tarbiyah tussen de echtgenoten.
Vragen
Vraag: De verkoop — geldt dat ook als [de verkoper] een niet-Muslim-man is op de vrijdag, tijdens het vrijdaggebed?
Antwoord: Ja, dan ook. Behalve wanneer een vrouw van een andere vrouw koopt. [Of] een vrouw koopt van een slaaf, of een vrouw koopt van een zieke man. [Vraag:] Stel dat je in de winkel staat boodschappen te doen, en je komt bij de kassa [de caissière] — dan hoor je dus die vrouw [de caissière] te kiezen om bij af te rekenen, klopt dat? Ja.
Vraag: Is het handen schudden van het andere geslacht een grote zonde?
Antwoord: Ja. De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt: «لأن يُطعَن في رأس أحدكم بمِخْيَطٍ من حديدٍ خيرٌ له من أن يَمَسّ امرأةً لا تَحِلّ له» — «Dat een van jullie in zijn hoofd gestoken wordt met een ijzeren naald, is beter voor hem dan dat hij een vrouw aanraakt die niet toegestaan is voor hem.» En de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zei: «اليَدان تَزنِيان، وزِناهما البَطشُ» — «De handen plegen ontucht, en hun ontucht is het grijpen [het aanraken].»
[Vraag:] Hoe bepaal je dat het een grote zonde is?
[Antwoord:] De geleerden geven aan dat de grote zonden kenmerken hebben. [Wanneer] Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa of de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam aan de zonde — erna of ervoor — een dreiging heeft verbonden (de toorn van Allaah, de vloek van Allaah, het Vuur, een specifiek vastgestelde bestraffing, hetzij in het wereldse leven of het Hiernamaals) — dan is het een grote zonde.
[Vervolgvraag:] Is in deze hadieth de naald die in het hoofd wordt gestoken dan de dreiging?
[Antwoord:] Ja, de naald hoor je als een speer te zien. [Het is een grote zonde] vanwege de hadieth van de naald, en omdat het tot zinaa (ontucht) leidt — maar niet alles wat tot zinaa leidt is een grote zonde. Het kijken naar een vrouw zonder hidjaab is een kleine zonde als [de kijker] geen begeerte naar haar heeft, [maar het zondig is] omdat hij een 3awrah ziet. En het kijken naar een vrouw zonder hidjaab mét gevoelens en met staren [aanhoudend kijken] zijn meer zonden, dat wil zeggen meerdere zonden naast elkaar. En het kijken op zichzelf is een kleine zonde. En wanneer [het] tot het aanraken komt, dan is het — volgens de hadieth — een grote zonde.
Vraag: De hadieth van de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam waarin hij zegt: «O groep... wie hun tekortkomingen [3awraat] opspoort, Allaah zal zijn tekortkomingen opsporen... [en] hem te schande maken in zijn huis» — is dat een vorm van «karma»?
Antwoord: «كما تَدِين تُدان» — «Zoals jij doet, zal met jou gedaan worden» — is een sunnah kawniyyah van Allaah (logica). En het is een juiste uitspraak als iemand die gebruikt. En [er zijn] enkele ahaadieth [waarin] hij daarvoor een bewijs heeft. Maar «karma» is een boeddhistische term. «Karma» komt uit het boeddhisme. [De betekenis] komt op hetzelfde neer, maar die term horen wij niet te gebruiken; want hij komt uit het boeddhisme en het hindoeïsme. [De betekenis] komt op hetzelfde neer. En de Nederlanders zeggen «een koekje van eigen deeg [dat wil zeggen: een vergelding van dezelfde soort als de daad]», «wie een kuil graaft voor een ander, valt er zelf in».
De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt: «من سَتَر مؤمنًا سَتَره اللهُ» — «Wie een gelovige bedekt, Allaah zal hem bedekken.» En wie voor een gelovige een moeilijkheid verlicht, Allaah zal het voor hem verlichten op de Dag des Oordeels. En [er is] een hadieth waarin «كما تَدِين تُدان» zwak is verklaard. Ibn al-Haadjdj [en] de Imaam al-Albaanie hebben hem zwak verklaard. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa zegt: ﴿وَإِذَا خَلَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ ۝١٤ ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ Interpretatie van de betekenis: «En wanneer zij zich afzonderen met hun satans, zeggen zij: ‹Voorwaar, wij zijn met jullie, wij drijven slechts de spot.› Allaah drijft de spot met hen.» (Soerat Al-Baqarah, aayah 14-15) En Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa zegt bijvoorbeeld (Soerat Al-Baqarah, aayah 40): «En kom Mijn verbond na, dan kom Ik jullie verbond na.» [En in] Soerat Al-Baqarah, aayah 152: «Gedenk Mij dus, dan gedenk Ik jullie.» «Als jullie Allaah helpen, zal Hij jullie helpen en jullie voeten stevig doen staan.» De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt: «ارحَموا من في الأرض يَرحَمكم من في السماء» — «Wees genadig voor wie op de aarde is, dan zal Degene die in de hemel is genadig voor jullie zijn.» En de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt: «احفَظِ اللهَ يَحفَظك» — «Waak over [de geboden van] Allaah, dan zal Hij over jou waken.» En [er zijn] nog heel veel ahaadieth die deze betekenis aangeven.
Vraag: Hoe kunnen wij het laatste punt over de negativiteit toepassen?
Antwoord: De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt: «استَعِن بالله ولا تَعجِز» — «Zoek hulp bij Allaah en geef niet op.» Dat is in het kort de samenvatting van hoe je het hoort te doen. Dat je niet stil blijft staan bij het slechte, [dat] je het goede opzoekt, doorgaat, en Allaah vraagt om je te helpen.
Huiswerk
[Het is] hetzelfde [huiswerk] als vorige week, maar met de nieuwe punten:
Orden je aantekeningen.
Ga bij elk advies na hoe je jezelf kunt voorbereiden als je nog niet getrouwd bent, en begin te werken aan minstens drie adviezen.
En als je getrouwd bent, zorg er dan voor dat je ze met je partner bespreekt en dat jullie aan minstens drie adviezen beginnen te werken.
De zevenendertigste les — zondag 11 november 2018
Huiswerk
[Het is] hetzelfde [huiswerk] als vorige week, maar met de nieuwe punten:
Orden je aantekeningen.
Ga bij elk advies na hoe je jezelf kunt voorbereiden als je nog niet getrouwd bent, en begin te werken aan minstens drie adviezen.
En als je getrouwd bent, zorg er dan voor dat je ze met je partner bespreekt en dat jullie aan minstens drie adviezen beginnen te werken.
Bespreking van het huiswerk (11 november 2018)
Zuster 1
Heeft [de punten] met haar man besproken. Zij willen werken aan de punten:
17) Zorg ervoor dat jullie elkaar op een spontane [natuurlijke] wijze aanmoedigen en activeren, zonder verveling te kennen in jullie relatie. Dat geldt voor alle vormen in jullie relatie: de wijze van communiceren, hoe jullie met elkaar omgaan, [en] in de routine in huis.
Wij horen meer tijd voor elkaar te hebben, en in die tijd ook samen leuke activiteiten te ondernemen om te vermijden dat onze relatie verveling kent. Wij wonen bij een gracht [waterkanaal]. Na het eten zijn we daar op een dag een stukje gaan wandelen, waarbij we ondertussen met elkaar praten.
20) Leer omgaan met geld/uitgaven waarbij je dingen koopt voor jezelf, je partner en je kinderen, en ook de wijze waarop je het uitgeeft.
Wij zijn bewuster omgegaan met onze uitgaven. Wij hebben ons bij elke uitgave afgevraagd of Allaah er tevreden mee zal zijn, en hebben meer uitgegeven aan sadaqah. En wij hebben ook de verspilling (israaf) tegengegaan: we hebben niet nóg meer borden gekocht terwijl we al goede borden hebben.
21) [20 in de oorspronkelijke volgorde] Zorg ervoor dat je de negativiteit vermijdt en haar uit je leven verwijdert.
En daarnaast kan het soms voorkomen dat ik slechte vermoedens heb, in de zin dat ik probeer mij voor te stellen wat er in mijn man omgaat, waarbij ik soms dingen aanneem die niet zo gezegd zijn. En ik ben hier al aan gaan werken met de hulp van mijn man.
De docent: Het is wellicht goed dat je bij voorbaat het goede vermoeden hebt. Je hoort jezelf af te vragen: wat zou het beste zijn wat mijn man over mij denkt? Het beste wat daaruit komt, [is] wat jij over jouw man hoort te denken. Verwijder de slechte gedachten en het onjuiste gedrag. Dan verwijder je het slechte uit jezelf, en bouw je op de feiten die je voor je ziet.
Zuster 2
Afgelopen week heeft de zuster de punten op een andere wijze aangepakt. Zij heeft gewerkt aan het punt van de ouders. En dat heeft zich [ook] voorgedaan [een situatie hiervan]. De zuster heeft het advies van de docent aangenomen. Voorheen vermeed zij de situatie en ging zij naar een andere plek. Dat deed zij nu ook, en zij dacht aan de les van de 3ilm shu-oon al-usrah, [eraan] dat zij om vergeving [excuses] hoort te vragen. Toen is zij dat gaan doen. En het was bij de moeder. [Maar de moeder] wilde het niet accepteren. De moeder van de zuster wilde het niet accepteren; want zij zei dat zij alleen haar excuses aanbiedt [omdat] zij dan met [iets] goeds bezig is, dus niet omwille van haar moeder, maar alleen voor haar eigen weegschaal.
[De moeder] zei letterlijk: «Excuses hoeven nu niet meer.» [De zuster] is gewend om naar boven te gaan en komt — meestal — niet meer terug. [De moeder] zei: «Je doet het alleen om zelf goed te zijn. Het hoeft niet.»
De docent: In principe hoor je daaraan vast te houden [te blijven proberen]. En wat niet goed is, [is] dat je vanaf het begin niet op de juiste wijze hebt gereageerd. Herinner je je nog de hadieth van de vrouw die door de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam werd aangesproken terwijl zij verdrietig huilde? De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zei: «إنما الصبرُ عند الصَّدمة الأولى» — «Het [ware] geduld is bij de eerste klap.» Wanneer je [de zaak] vanaf dat moment meemaakt, hoor je vanaf dat moment te denken: «Ik hoor mezelf te verbeteren, ik hoor mij op de goede wijze te gedragen.» Voordat je [de zaak] zover laat komen dat je moeder iets moet doen, kun je deze situatie voor jezelf voorkomen [vermijden] door te denken: «Als ik nu op die wijze reageer, zal mijn moeder dan tevreden zijn of niet?» Als je [je] op dat moment [bezighoudt] met het tevreden houden van je moeder en haar nog meer tevreden te stellen, dan ben je bezig met het voorkomen [vermijden] van zaken. Als je je daar meer mee bezighoudt, dan zal jouw iemaan toenemen, en de toename van jouw iemaan (dat hebben we behandeld bij het denkschema) zal je leiden tot een betere ingeving, waarbij je niet eerst de fout begaat en daarna jezelf verbetert, maar direct [overgaat tot] haar stil [rustig] houden, haar proberen te kalmeren, haar proberen tevreden te stellen. De preventie — als je daaraan werkt, dan zul je minder bezig zijn met het herstellen van zaken. En wat je gedaan hebt, [is] zeker goed — dat je jezelf hebt herpakt, teruggekomen bent en jezelf hebt gecorrigeerd. En we hebben vorige week behandeld dat wij alles horen te geven om degene die het gezag heeft tevreden te stellen. Je hoort haar duidelijk te maken: «Ik doe dit omwille van Allaah, maar ook om jou gelukkig te maken. Jij bent mijn moeder, jij voedt mij op en laat mij dit doen; want wanneer jij mij hierin steunt, zul jij ook veel beloning krijgen.» Dan maak je je moeder op een zachte, lieve wijze, op een moeder/dochter-wijze, duidelijk dat jouw moeder een heel groot aandeel hierin heeft. En dat je het ook voor haar doet, omwille van Allaah.
[De docent vroeg:] Hoe heb je daarna gereageerd toen zij zei dat je het voor jezelf doet?
Eerst was de zuster stil. De zuster gaf aan dat zij eerst in lachen uitbarstte. En de moeder van de zuster bleef herhalen: «Nee, excuses hoeven nu niet.» Toen zei de zuster: «Goed, dan trek ik [mijn excuses] in.» De moeder wilde dat [de zuster] haar zus ging helpen. De zuster zei: «Ik ga je niet helpen als je je zo koppig gedraagt.» Dus zij heeft die dag niet geholpen. En zij zei daarna dat zij het huiswerk op een andere dag met haar zou doen.
De docent: Als jouw moeder wilde dat je het op die dag deed, dan hoor je [de relatie] met je zus te verbeteren en het — toch — op die dag te doen. Je hoort te doen wat haar op dat moment tevredenstelt. [Maar] jij hebt gedaan wat jíj wilt, niet wat je moeder wil. Het is goed dat je de eerste stap hebt genomen, maar het is — jazeker — belangrijk dat je doorgaat [met de zaak]. Je hoort niet bij jezelf stil te blijven staan en te zeggen: «Ik heb gefaald, ik doe het niet meer.» Dat is de influistering van de shaytaan. Jij bent geslaagd; want je hebt het geprobeerd, en je zult jezelf verder gaan verbeteren. Wanneer er straks een pauze is of wanneer de les is afgelopen, ga je [de relatie] met je moeder nog verder herstellen, ook al denk je: «Zij is al rustiger geworden, zij is al tevreden.» Je hoort je nog meer in te spannen om haar tevreden te stellen. Dat [is] de volgzaamheid jegens degene die gezag over jou heeft. En dat geldt voor de zusters, maar ook wat betreft de broeders met betrekking tot de vader en de moeder. Iedereen die gezag over ons heeft — dat leer je bij je ouders. Hoe beter je bent richting de ouders, hoe beter je daarna zult zijn richting mensen buiten je ouders, zoals je echtgenoot of de mensen met kennis. En dat geldt niet op deze wijze wanneer je gaat werken. Jouw werk, [en] jouw leidinggevende op het werk, heeft (zeker bij de kaafir) alleen gezag over het werk, over het werk en over hoe het werk eruit hoort te zien. Dat [is] het enige wat zijn recht [is].
De docent: Heb je meer punten gepraktiseerd?
De zuster heeft deze keer niet elk punt volledig behandeld. En het laatste punt, «zorg ervoor dat je de negativiteit vermijdt» — daar is zij actief aan gaan werken. De zuster kreeg soms negatieve gedachten, en dan ging zij de isti3aadhah verrichten (toevlucht zoeken bij Allaah tegen de shaytaan) en een nuttige bezigheid opzoeken: boeken lezen, lezingen bijwonen, nuttige dingen doen. Zij vond dat een leuk punt.
Zuster 3
Een zuster heeft deze week een aantal punten gepraktiseerd. Het laatste punt over de negativiteit in het leven. De zuster is al heel lang bezig met het memoriseren van een soerah. En het laatste gedeelte lukte niet om te memoriseren. De zuster had daar negatieve gedachten over. [De docent zei:] Als [het] niet lukt, dan meer moeite doen om die soerah te leren.
De docent: Wie [is] de tweede belangrijkste in deze ummah na de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam (na Aboe Bakr)? 3umar. Weten jullie hoe lang het duurde voordat hij Soerat Al-Baqarah gememoriseerd had? Acht jaar. Is het niet [omdat] hij daarbij ook de tafsier (uitleg) ging leren? 3umar ibn al-KHattaab was niet de beste in het memoriseren, niet zoals veel andere metgezellen van de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. Niet alle sahaabah kenden de hele Qur'aan. En desondanks was hij — jawel — de leider van de gelovigen (amier al-mu-minien). We horen dus nooit de moed te verliezen: enerzijds [omdat] Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa ons helpt, en anderzijds: weet [dat] hoe meer je begrijpt, hoe meer je kunt memoriseren. Het memoriseren zelf houdt namelijk — voor een groot deel — verband met het begrijpen van de Qur'aan. Wanneer je de verzen kunt verbinden en het verband tussen de verzen kent, dan wordt het memoriseren ervan gemakkelijk.
Een advies: herhaal elk vers 20 keer, daarna herhaal je de halve pagina, daarna herhaal je in het gebed. Daarna, aan het einde van de week, herhaal je nogmaals. Dan blijft [het gememoriseerde] vastzitten, zolang je het elke twee, drie of elke zes maanden blijft herhalen.
En een aantal andere punten die zij deze week heeft gepraktiseerd, [is] het omgaan met het uitgeven van geld. Zij heeft deze week daarop gelet. Zij merkt dat zij veel uitgeeft aan onbenullige dingen. Vooral wanneer zij naar de winkel gaat, komt zij thuis met onnodige dingen. [Zij is] — meestal — volgens het boodschappenlijstje gaan werken en beperkt zich tot dat lijstje. Zij merkte dat zij alleen de dingen pakte die zij nodig heeft en ging afrekenen. En het was voor haar [een les] dat zij zich daar bewuster van hoort te zijn. Aan de hand van het boodschappenlijstje merkte zij dat het beter voor haar is.
De docent: Niet alleen beter voor het geld, maar ook voor de tijd. Het bespaart ook veel fitan (beproevingen/verleidingen). Hoe vaker en langer je buiten bent, hoe meer fitan [er zijn]. Kijk hoeveel voordeel je hebt behaald om Allaah tevreden te stellen. Je had je geld kunnen verkwisten, [en er was] tijdverspilling zonder bewustzijn, geldverspilling, veel fitan buiten. En al deze nadelen zien veel mensen niet — dat zij buiten zijn en onnodige dingen doen. En Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa zal ons op de Dag des Oordeels ter verantwoording roepen over elke zaak die wij doen en elke zaak die wij laten. En soms laten wij dingen [omdat] wij krap bij kas zitten [voor het geval] wij iets moois maar onnodigs zouden willen kopen. Wij horen onszelf te redden van de bestraffing van Allaah en Zijn toorn.
De zuster had — jawel — deze week een punt: het vermoeden richting de Muslims. Zij zat in een gevaarlijke situatie. Een zuster die dicht bij haar staat, was aan het twijfelen of zij de hidjaab zou afdoen of niet. De zuster wilde nog vragen hoe zij die zuster op de beste wijze kan adviseren, en welke vermaningen zij haar hoort te geven.
Zij gaf aan dat zij [het] heel moeilijk vond. Zij heeft haar niet persoonlijk [van aangezicht tot aangezicht] gesproken, maar zij vindt [het] moeilijk. [De zuster] was gewend om moderne kleding te dragen, haar haar mooi te maken. Zij vindt [het] heel moeilijk, en zij is bang dat zij hem wil afdoen. Zij is 30 jaar en zij werkt.
[De docent vroeg:] De hidjaab — is het een volledige khimaar (bedekking)? Zij wisselt tussen de 3abaayah (overkleed) en de hidjaab en tussen tunieken [korte hemden] met een broek en een hoofddoek. En tunieken met een broek en een hoofddoek zijn geen hidjaab. Soms draagt zij de hidjaab en soms niet. Hebben jullie met haar gesproken over de zuivere intentie? Ja, [wij hebben met haar gesproken] over het feit dat zij dit omwille van Allaah hoort te doen en niet omwille van haar omgeving. Haar omgeving werkt haar tegen in het dragen van de hidjaab, dus zij doet het omwille van Allaah, anders had zij hem niet gedragen. Waarschijnlijk [is het] vanwege haar werk. [De zuster] weet niet precies waar de zuster werkt. Toen zij hem begon te dragen, werkte zij — jawel.
De docent: Het dragen van de hidjaab omwille van Allaah. Wij hebben geleerd dat de zuivere intentie ook het praktiseren hoort te kennen. Als iemand zegt: «Ik wil de hidjaab dragen omwille van Allaah», dan betekent het dat zij de volledige bedekking hoort te dragen. Het dragen van een hoofddoek is niet omwille van Allaah. Dat [is] het dragen van een hoofddoek en het denken dat het omwille van Allaah is. Daar [ligt] het probleem. Het denken dat het omwille van Allaah is, en het daadwerkelijk omwille van Allaah zijn, [zijn twee verschillende dingen]. Je kunt niet omwille van Allaah iets doen wat Hem niet tevredenstelt. Als je iets omwille van Allaah wilt doen, dan hoor je ook te doen wat Hem tevredenstelt. En daarmee maak je ook jouw inkomen halaal. Wanneer je in de afweging zit «hoor ik de volledige hidjaab te dragen of een hoofddoek?» — wanneer men [het volledige] niet doet [omdat] men denkt dat het werk [er] niet [mee] geaccepteerd zal worden, dan is het geld dat je verdient haraam. En de enige afweging die gemaakt hoort te worden, [is]: «Ik zal Allaah tevredenstellen op de wijze die Hij wil, en doen wat Hij wil.»
En dit zorgt ook voor wankeling bij veel broeders of zusters. Daarom is het belangrijk dat jullie haar ook duidelijk maken dat Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa haar naar meer bedekking heeft geleid, en dat Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [haar] minder [verafschuwt] [dat wil zeggen: haar handelen minder verafschuwt] dan wanneer zij de hidjaab volledig zou afdoen, dus de hoofddoek zou afdoen. En dat Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa haar zal helpen, haar zal leiden en nog meer van haar zal houden wanneer zij haar volledige hidjaab draagt om Hem tevreden te stellen. Vermaan haar vooral op basis van de ikhlaas en de praktische kant van de hidjaab. Wanneer men de hidjaab afdoet, zal het namelijk moeilijk zijn om hem weer te dragen. [Daarmee] gooit men de gunst van Allaah weg terwijl Hij haar geleid had. Misschien is zij op het werk of door haar omgeving beïnvloed. En het verzamelen van meer kennis [is] iets wat de mens standvastig houdt.
Adviezen:
Vermaan haar door middel van de ikhlaas.
Vermaan haar door middel van de boosheid die zij laat terugkaatsen [weerkaatsen] op zichzelf [dat wil zeggen: haar boosheid op zichzelf].
Maak haar duidelijk dat zij zo snel mogelijk kennis hoort te verzamelen; daarmee kan zij haar iemaan vermeerderen, een betere begeleiding [sturing] krijgen, en wordt zij meer gestimuleerd om standvastig te zijn.
De docent: Bij de bespreking van het huiswerk halen wij veel kennis naar boven die wij in de les niet besproken hebben, en wordt veel kennis duidelijker of praktischer. Door de bespreking van het huiswerk worden wij dus meer bijgeschaafd [gevormd].
sections.title_nl: Vervolg van praktische handvatten bij het aangaan van de zawaadj
sections.content_en:
The previous lesson and this week
This week we will continue with more advices/tools with regard to strengthening the bond in the zawaadj. We stopped at «do not pull old cows out of the ditch».
We are engaged in looking at how we can improve our relationship in the zawaadj. And [there are] still some important practical advices to implement. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has prescribed for us [commanded us] not to dig up old cases; so it is not merely a [popular] proverb.
16) Make sure that you do not prejudge people [harbour bad assumptions about them] without right.
That is possible in different ways. One of the ways [is] that you lump certain groups together under one comb [generalise the judgement over them]: the men, the women. «The men are such and such, the women are such and such», [or] that you prejudge a certain ethnicity, prejudge a certain origin. Do not do that. For when you do that, it means that you harbour bad assumptions about the other and deal with him from an incorrect image, whereby you also wrong him. And it is not arbitrary [that] Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has forbidden bad thoughts, but [He has] also [forbidden] everything that leads to bad thoughts.
And another way of harbouring bad assumptions without right [is] that you have heard a lot about a certain person, rumours here and there. And sometimes that is confirmed by a certain behaviour of his that you place in [the frame] that has been presented/drawn for you. So you go and harbour bad assumptions about that [person] and deal with him from that image that has been drawn for you. For example: «That [person] is stingy, is not good, can only be negative.» Then you see from him a behaviour that is either not good, or is good but you do not see it as good, and therefore you place him in an incorrect image and you confirm the image and say to yourself: «I saw it myself, the image is correct» — whereby you harbour bad assumptions without right.
And another way [is] that you already — from the beginning — harbour bad assumptions about another. You have no trust in other people. That ensures that you harbour bad assumptions when that [person] speaks with you.
And another possibility [is] that you have associated with that [person] for years and have formed a certain image of him, [such that] you also go and listen to him in that way, listen [to him] with that image and/or look [at him] without doing that by means of the facts [truths]. You no longer see the facts. And the only thing you see before you [is] the image you have formed of that [person]. That is also a form of injustice.
And that last one — very many people think that it is something normal, [that it is] how you should deal with people — but that is not correct. Not correct at all. For when someone has shown remorse [tawbah] over a certain matter and had also repeated it several times, but has also repeated his tawbah several times — then you should — nevertheless — treat him only according to the facts, not according to his deeds that he did before. That means that you should — nevertheless — be objective at that moment, and that is [something] difficult for many people. And [it] becomes easy when one goes and trains oneself in practising ikhlaas. And the most dangerous is that when someone has done a certain thing only once and has shown remorse, that [other person] has already formed an image of the other, and then goes and deals with that other according to that image he has. And all these matters are not correct.
But it is — indeed — correct when such a person shows no remorse over his matters. Then it is important that you deal with that image according to the facts. And at the moment he shows remorse, you throw everything away and [the page] is a new page. Exactly as Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa does with His servants when they are sincere.
And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has warned against bad thoughts. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa mentions «adh-dhann» (assumption) very often in the Qur'aan, at least eight times. And they are eight times in a negative way. And «adh-dhann» means in Arabic the guessing/conjecturing about something.
And in all cases Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has coupled «adh-dhann» with desire, or mentioned it in place of desire, and as contradicting knowledge and facts. Look [for example] in Soerat An-Nisaa-e. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption.» (Soerat An-Nisaa-e, verse 157)
And also Soerat Al-An3aam for example. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa indicates here: «إن يَتّبِعون إلا الظنَّ» — «They follow only assumption» (verse 116). Then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «Indeed, your Lord knows best who strays from His way, and He knows best who are the guided ones.» If you look up «adh-dhann» in the Qur'aan, [you find] that Allaah has used it in the Qur'aan only in a negative way, contradicting knowledge, [as a] companion of the desires. And sometimes «yadhunnoen» (they assume) also [occurs] in a negative way, but sometimes also in a positive way, but then it means «they know [are certain]». For example «yadhunnoen...» — by this Allaah means those who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him. And the word «adh-dhann» [as a noun] Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has used only in a negative meaning. And «adh-dhann» [is] the root of the verb [its masdar/verbal noun].
And assumption avails nothing against the truth; the Exalted says: ﴿وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ إِلَّا ظَنًّا ۚ إِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «And most of them follow only assumption. Indeed, assumption avails nothing against the truth.» (Soerat Yoenus, verse 36)
And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has warned us against that: in Soerat Al-Hudjuraat, verse 12 Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «O you who believe, avoid much of assumption. Indeed, part of assumption is sin. And do not spy, and do not let one of you backbite another. Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it. And fear Allaah. Indeed, Allaah is Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful.»
Here Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa indicates that He forbids «adh-dhann»; because part of it is sin, or leads directly to a sin. And with part of «adh-dhann» you can leave Islaam, and that [is] the bad assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Why does Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa mention spying (tadjassus) and ghiebah (backbiting) after that? It is not only [that] «adh-dhann» can lead to ghiebah. «Adh-dhann» can lead to tadjassus, but also to ghiebah. And tadjassus and ghiebah can lead to «adh-dhann». So it is a continuous negative circle. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has forbidden [one] to have «dhann», but also [forbidden] everything that «adh-dhann» leads to, and also what leads to «adh-dhann». For when you go and spy on someone — out of mere curiosity — that leads to bad thoughts. For then you will see things you should not have seen, [or] do not need to see, or [things] that mean nothing, but which — in the end — you will nevertheless go and think about. And exactly [so] with ghiebah and buhtaan (backbiting and lying). For most of what goes on now — unfortunately — [is] ghiebah plus lying. What is said is not even true. And that is spread via everything and anything (social media, the telephone, etc.). Then one goes so far as to hate that [person]. And when he does not see that that [person] receives a punishment, he becomes even angrier. Contemplate where bad assumption leads.
What [is] the cure for «adh-dhann»?
That is very important; because with it we can then purify our thoughts, improve them, and have tranquillity in our heart. For the more bad assumptions you harbour about people, the more restlessness [there is] in the heart.
And the bad assumption about the other [is based] on one thinking — about another or about something — the bad in a negative way more than the good, without any Islamic evidence. For him [that] will be evidence: «I have 100% evidence that he does that. I heard from so-and-so that he saw him once, and he knows him well.» Those are absolutely not Islamic evidences. So do you have evidence? No.
And bad assumption happens by means of the heart, and it branches into different types. And the most dangerous type [is] the bad assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. The bad assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — for example that he assumes that his share with Allaah is far too small, and that it should — in reality — have been much more, that is, [that] Allaah supposedly gives him too little and does not treat him justly, and that Allaah should have given him more, and that he does not accept [the place] in which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has placed him. When that [person] is angry with Allaah and complains about Allaah, he leaves the religion. Why? Because at that moment he doubts Allaah and also accuses Him — on top of that — of injustice and dishonesty. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is exalted above that.
And when one does not simply accept what Allaah has chosen for him, then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will become angry with him and will not give him contentment, and Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will treat him as a sinner.
What is the minimum you should do with Allaah? That you believe that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is just, truthful, al-Hakiem (the All-Wise), the most just [of the just], the One who determines the truth, and that you accept what Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given you.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in a hadieth qudsie (sacred narration): «أنا عند ظنّ عبدي بي» — «I am as My servant assumes Me to be.» That means [that] if someone harbours bad assumptions about Allaah, Allaah will give him the bad. And if someone harbours good assumptions about Allaah, Allaah will give him the good according to his assumption about Allaah. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «من رَضِيَ فله الرِّضا، ومن سَخِط ولم يَرضَ فعليه السَّخَط» — «Whoever is content, for him is contentment [from Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa], and whoever is displeased and is not content, upon him is displeasure.» And that is why the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says in a hadieth narrated by the Imaam Muslim: «لا يَموتَنّ أحدُكم إلا وهو يُحسِن الظنَّ بالله» — «Let none of you die except while he has the good assumption about Allaah.»
And bad assumption [is based] on that. For every bad assumption about people springs from a bad assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, where there is no ikhlaas for Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
The way in which we can avoid bad assumption
With regard to bad assumption — we said that it begins with bad assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And bad assumption ensures especially that the human being becomes bad in his thinking, becomes bad in his worldly life, and also becomes bad in his Hereafter. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in Soerat Fussilat (verse 23): «And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has ruined you, so you have become among the losers.» The assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — as we said before — is an important means with which to also weigh your thoughts about people. The less you have the good assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and the less you are aware of the correct thought about Allaah, the worse your thoughts are. And the less you have the good assumption about Allaah, the less you rely on Allaah. That means that your tawakkul (reliance on Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa) is very low, and that you think that you depend on your own cleverness, your own plans, and your own defence system, instead of trusting that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa defends you and stands at your side, and that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will help you if you please Him.
Where do the bad thoughts about others come from?
After the bad thoughts and the doubting of Allaah, or [after] the lack of awareness of Allaah, [it] comes from fear. The fear that people will do something to you, the fear that you have to protect yourself from people, the fear that people will not appreciate you, the fear that if you do not attack, you become the victim. And all of that comes from the whisperings of the shaytaan. The less your connection with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, the more inclined you are towards the shaytaan, and the more power the shaytaan has over you in whispering. And the power of the shaytaan is nothing but the waswasah (whispering).
It is important, with the bad thoughts, that you first begin with your connection with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and that you begin with improving the connection with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Where does the good assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa begin?
That begins with knowing Him in the correct way by means of His Most Beautiful Names and His Exalted Attributes and by means of His Deeds. And that you also believe that all these Names, Attributes and Deeds [have] magnificent effects in your life. That they [bring about] only beneficial effects in your life. Such as knowing that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is merciful to His servants who deserve that, and that He is forgiving if they show tawbah, if they return. And that He accepts the acts of 3ibaadah, and that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is all-wise, all-knowing in His qadar (divine decree) which He decrees. There the good assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa begins.
And the good assumption about Allaah is also coupled with deeds. That [is] the difference between the good assumption about Allaah and merely wishing for yourself things you will not receive. That [is] the difference between wishing (tamannie) and hope (radjaa-e). For whoever hopes and wishes performs no deeds. And whoever looks forward to the better does so with deeds. Whoever wants Allaah to forgive him stops the sin. Whoever wants Allaah to give him barakah (blessing) goes and works/becomes active towards what he wants to receive. And that is also what the Imaam Ibn al-Qayyim says. The Imaam al-Hasan al-Basrie says: «ليس الإيمانُ بالتَّمنّي. الإيمانُ ما وَقَر في القلب وصَدّقه العمل» — «Iemaan is not [a matter of] wishing. Iemaan is what has settled in the heart and is confirmed by deeds.»
And therefore, if you look closely at the hadieth in which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa speaks about treating His servants according to how they think about Him — He says after that: «And I am with him when he remembers Me.» «And if he draws near to Me a hand's span, I draw near to him an arm's length; and if he draws near to Me an arm's length, I draw near to him a fathom [much more]; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.»
So Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa links the good assumption here to deeds. The deeds of the mind, the deeds of the heart, and the deeds of the limbs. And al-Hasan al-Basrie also says: «إن المؤمن أَحسَن الظنَّ بربِّه فأَحسَن العملَ، وإن الفاجِر أساء الظنَّ بربِّه فأساء العملَ» — «Indeed, the believer has the good assumption about his Lord and so does good deeds, and the wicked one has the bad assumption about his Lord and so does bad deeds.»
There the good assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa begins. And another matter that also belongs to the good assumption about Allaah [is] that when you perform the matter in the correct way with the correct intention, you also expect that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa accepts your matter, accepts your tawbah, answers your du3aa-e. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «ادْعُوا اللهَ وأنتم مُوقِنون بالإجابة» — «Call upon Allaah while you are certain of the answer.» And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says: «حُسنُ الظنّ بالله من حُسن العبادة» — «The good assumption about Allaah is part of the excellence of 3ibaadah.»
And what also belongs to the good assumption about Allaah is that you know that the mercy of Allaah has overcome His anger. Aboe Hurayrah says in a hadieth declared authentic [by the scholars]: Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa said: «إن رحمتي غَلَبت غضبي» — «Indeed, My mercy has overcome My anger.» And in another hadieth: «Let none of you die except while he has the good assumption about Allaah.»
And what multiplies your good assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [is] patience (sabr), and also counting the patience with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says: «عَجَبًا لأمر المؤمن، إن أمره كلَّه خيرٌ. إن أصابته سَرّاءُ شَكَر فكان خيرًا له، وإن أصابته ضَرّاءُ صَبَر فكان خيرًا له» — «Wondrous is the affair of the believer; indeed, all of his affair is good. If prosperity befalls him, he is grateful, and that is good for him; and if adversity befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him.» Why [is it] good for him? Because he counts the reward with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And what [also] matters is that you turn away from evil, from the reprehensible matters, and that you show remorse quickly.
And another important matter [is] that you also know that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa [is] the Only One in Whose hands is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He is the Only One who can change something or move something in this universe, and that without [His permission] nothing will happen. If you know that, then you also know that the more you please Him, the more He stands at your side. And if you do not please Him, then He does not stand at your side, and therefore you are compelled to please Him. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed, Allaah defends those who believe.» (Soerat Al-Hadj, verse 38) If you have heard this verse, you need nothing else. Then you do not have to run after people and harbour bad assumptions about them.
How can you — further — still remove the bad thoughts about people?
By occupying yourself with your own evils and not with the evils of people, and by being humble. How do you become humble? By occupying yourself with your own sins. And by accusing yourself instead of [accusing] people.
And another way to get rid of it [is] that you know that when you do this thing [and] harbour bad assumptions about others, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will make sure that people also harbour bad assumptions about you. For as you approach others, so you too will be approached. That is a sunnah kawniyyah that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has established (logic, 1+1=2).
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «يا مَعشَرَ من آمن بلسانه ولم يَدخُلِ الإيمانُ قلبَه، لا تَغتابوا المسلمين، ولا تَتّبِعوا عَوراتِهم. فإنه من تَتبّع عَوراتِهم، يَتتبّعِ اللهُ عَورتَه، ومن يَتتبّعِ اللهُ عَورتَه يَفضَحه في بيته» — «O company of those who believe with their tongue while iemaan has not entered their heart: do not backbite the Muslims, and do not track down their shortcomings. For whoever tracks down their shortcomings, Allaah will track down his shortcoming; and whoever's shortcoming Allaah tracks down, He will disgrace him in his own house.»
As you treat others, so you will be treated. And this is important to know.
And another matter [is] that you look only at the positive things in people. The best in people. One of the salaf (the righteous predecessors), Sufyaan ibn Husayn, mentioned someone in a bad way. Then Mu3aawiyah said to him while looking at him: Have you fought the Romans? The man said: No. He said: Have you fought the Turks, [or] the Hindus? He said: No. Then he said: Are the Romans, the Turks and the Hindus [all these people] safe from you, while your brother is not safe from you [from your tongue]? When the kaafir is engaged in fighting Islaam, they say: «Yes, we should be [people of] wisdom.» And when [the matter] concerns brothers and sisters, they know only hatred and hasad. That is a form of weakness.
And one of the important matters in the good assumption about people is that you verify the facts before you accept the rumours, and that you build upon an important definition, namely: «The Muslim is innocent of the sin until [the sin] is proven with Islamic evidences.» Not with the evidences of thinking [assumptions] or the delusions that are called evidences.
And another matter [is] that you go and seek an excuse for your Muslim brother or your Muslim sister even though the shaytaan says to you: «It is almost certain that that bad thing is true.» Then you go — nevertheless — and seek an excuse for your brother or sister, out of good assumption about the other. So that you clear yourself of the responsibility on the Day of Judgement.
Have we once covered the example of a person who enters [a place], enters a room, and then does not return the salaam (greeting of peace)? Imagine that you come across a sister and you look her in her eyes and she looks you in your eyes. You come across her in a corridor [a natural situation], you greet her with the salaam. She looks at you and says nothing. She moves on. You greet her again. She looks at you, moves on, and says nothing. Then she enters a classroom, whereby — at that moment, when she enters — the door is shut with great force. Then you see or hear that the door is being locked with a key.
What is happening at that moment? Perhaps she is angry, does not respond. So you already have in advance a delusion that she is angry. What actually [factually] happened? She did not return the salaam, she walks [on and] closes the room, slams the door. The door is shut with force. You do not know whether it is she who does that. You hear that the door is shut with force. Is [it] a fact that she is angry? No, that is an interpretation [explanation]. Everything that has not actually been seen or heard is not a fact, but many people go and translate these facts into other matters, into delusions, whereby they claim that these delusions are facts.
For example, such a sister can say: «Yes, she was angry. She did not say the salaam [back].» [Rather,] that does not mean that she is angry. She may be happy, sad, with her head occupied with something.
[Question:] A student asks: Is it not also good to make an excuse in your head [even if it were] that she is angry, in order to explain [interpret] on her behalf why she did not respond to your salaam?
The teacher: That is good, but you should do it in the best way. For example: «Most likely she did not hear me.»
What [are] the facts?
This sister has just received the news that her mother has died. At that moment she no longer sees anyone, she is thinking about her mother. She walks and does not hear the other. And because [there is] a draught [air current], the door slams shut, and because the door slams shut, she thinks: «I will lock the door.» So often [the matter is] completely different from what you thought.
And the same thing happened between Sa3d ibn Abie Waqqaas and 3uthmaan. He once walked along and greeted 3uthmaan. And Sa3d was the maternal uncle of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And he was honoured among the sahaabah. He greeted [3uthmaan], but he did not respond. Once again [he greeted him], but he did not respond. So he went to 3umar ibn al-KHattaab and said: such and such happened. 3umar did not say to him: «How bad of him, how arrogant [of him], I am surprised at you, I am surprised at him, I would not have expected that of him.» [Rather,] 3umar ibn al-KHattaab said: «Bring me 3uthmaan.» He was brought. 3umar ibn al-KHattaab said to 3uthmaan: Sa3d ibn Abie Waqqaas, the uncle of the Prophet, greeted you and you did not return his greeting. 3uthmaan said: When? I did not hear him greet me. And 3uthmaan [said]: At that moment I was [occupied in] my thoughts with an incident that had taken place with the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
What is the incident? «Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa answers whom He wills in what He wills [the du3aa-e].» Then a bedouin came, so we could no longer ask what that du3aa-e is. Then 3umar ibn al-KHattaab said: «I was there at that time too.» And Sa3d ibn Abie Waqqaas said: «I was there at that time too. I then went and waited for the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. When the bedouin departed, I went with him. [I said:] O Messenger of Allaah, you said: ‹By the One in Whose hand my soul is [the soul of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam is in His hand]›. I know a du3aa-e which, when someone says it, is answered with certainty.» [He said:] Correct, O Sa3d, it is: ‹لا إله إلا أنت، سبحانك إني كنتُ من الظالمين› — ‹There is no god [worthy of worship] except You; glorified are You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers.›»
[3uthmaan] had not heard Sa3d at all, but Allaah caused that to happen so that 3umar and 3uthmaan would know what this matter [this du3aa-e] is.
So [something like this] can happen, but one should draw the positive from it as the sahaabah did, and thereby one will also have the good assumption about the other. So this is how you see bad assumption, how bad [it is]. And harbouring bad assumptions about others without right, how bad [it is].
[Bad assumption] ruins the tarbiyah of the children. For if you treat a child all the time with talk or communication built on a prejudice, then it will — inevitably — become what you accuse it of. Instead of that, treat it without [prejudice], by means of the facts you see of it. And therefore it is important that you also treat your partner like this: treat your partner without [prejudice] in the best way. That ensures renewal in the relationship, and that you are always prepared to listen to the other, trust the other, embrace the other, without having an image whereby that image is a barrier in communicating with your partner in the best way.
Questions
Question: We just covered that you may not spy, backbite, and that that can lead to bad delusions about others. And bad assumption about another [is based] on one thinking the bad more than the good without any Islamic evidence. What is the Islamic evidence for the bad assumption about someone? By what is it — from the Islamic perspective — legitimate to harbour a bad assumption about someone?
Answer: The Islamic evidence [is] what is built on facts that have been translated in an Islamic way into sins. For example, someone says something. You know 100% that that [person] must know the opposite, the contrary. And this is a very simple example. Someone asks: was sister so-and-so present in class? You know 100% that she must know that she was present. At the moment you accuse her of lying by saying: «She knew that she was present; because she also spoke with her» — that at that moment is not evidence. Why is it not evidence? Because we should be certain that the sister actually remembers that she spoke with her, that she was present, and that she deliberately chose to say something other than what she knew. As long as you do not know that, you may not say that she is lying. That [is] what Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍۢ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ أَن تُصِيبُوا۟ قَوْمًۢا بِجَهَٰلَةٍۢ فَتُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَٰدِمِينَ ۝٦﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «O you who believe, if a wicked person comes to you with news, then verify [it], lest you strike a people out of ignorance, and then become regretful over what you have done.» (Soerat Al-Hudjuraat, verse 6) The only thing you should do is that you should ask the sister: Is it not [the case] that you asked that sister such-and-such? Then she says: «Yes», or she says: «No, I do not remember that.» Then you can say: «I do remember that — yes, it may be that you have forgotten it or [that] you no longer know, [because] perhaps you have many things in your head.»
And another example of the Islamic evidence [is] that when you see someone in front of you sinning and you say to him or her: «This is a sin», and he says: «I know it is a sin, may Allaah forgive me» — at that moment you have evidence that he knows that it is a sin and that he does it deliberately. But if you see someone sinning, you may not accuse him of sinning until you know 100% that firstly he has not forgotten it, [that] he is not doing it by mistake, or [until] you know with certainty that he knows that this is a sin. And this applies to assessing someone. So that you know with certainty that he knows that it is a sin, and that he has not forgotten it, and that he is not making a mistake.
The teacher came across a brother in Malaysia. He was travelling from Dubai to Malaysia. He wanted to take a gift for his brothers. He saw bottles and thought they were bottles of olive oil, so he bought one. Someone else, who was practising, saw him. He said: Do you know that this is not a bottle of olive oil but a bottle of wine (khamr)? Then he dropped it from his hand — out of fright — and it broke, whereby the wine came out. So when someone says at that moment: «I saw someone drinking, he had wine [in his hand]» — that does not mean that he sinned. Perhaps he does not know that it is a bottle of wine. And who knows, perhaps he forgot or made a mistake. So before we judge, we should be 100% certain. And bad assumption about people [is] a judgement upon them. Instead of doing that, you go and have the good assumption about him/her and go and advise that [person] in the best way.
All of these — and [there are] still many examples of the evidences that occur — but these are examples of the evidences. And the essential part [is] the certainty that someone is committing a sin, [that he] is not ignorant, and that you verify that. And the tabayyun [is] the examining, the verifying. And it is not [the case that] when a scholar judges a person, you go to that person and say: «Is it true what these scholars say about you?» Then you are not [proceeding correctly]; because this person will deny [the matter] in any case. When we know trustworthy scholars, and they verify matters and judge, then we accept that. [There are] certain matters that we do not need to know or should not know, but we accept [the judgement of] the people of knowledge or the scholars. For they are like judges over others, but not [judges] over one another.
[Question:] The sister: Does this then not fall under the category of blind following (taqlied)?
The teacher: Blind following [is] without evidences and without knowledge. And when the scholar judges a person or a certain group that sows fitnah (tribulation/corruption), and they are multiple scholars or [one] scholar — then it suffices that we — out of our loyalty to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and because we know that this scholar is closer to the truth than the one being judged — follow the scholar in what he says on the basis of the evidences and the matters he sets out. For you cannot make the ignorant one an equal to the scholars or the people of knowledge. That is what the ignorant always try to do in order to keep the judgement of the scholar low [inferior].
Question: Can you repeat the du3aa-e?
Answer: «لا إله إلا أنت، سبحانك إني كنتُ من الظالمين» — «There is no god [worthy of worship] except You; glorified are You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers.»
Follow-up question: How can we apply that du3aa-e?
Answer: Before you perform a specific du3aa-e, you perform this du3aa-e. With it you acknowledge the Tawhied of Allaah, and you also acknowledge your sins, your humility and your submissiveness.
17) Make sure that you encourage and energise each other in a spontaneous [natural] way, without knowing boredom in your relationship.
That applies to all forms in your relationship: the way of communicating, how you deal with each other, [and] in the routine at home. Avoid monotony [boredom] in your relationship. And monotony [is] the things you go and do [whereby] you experience boredom. Be creative. And [the activities] do not necessarily have to be educational activities; they can be sports activities, play activities, activities outside the house for the children, activities in the house.
3abdullaah ibn Mas3oed used to give his students a lesson every Thursday. And at a certain point the students asked: Why can you not give us a lesson every day? He said: I do not want you to become bored. And in this way the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also gave us the lesson. He feared that we would become bored. That means, then, that you should avoid entering an atmosphere in which you do something only as a routine [whereby] you are less energised and less motivated to do good. Break the routine sometimes. Make sure that you once do something nice, something creative. For falling into boredom ensures that a gap arises.
18) It is important that the partners continually gather knowledge.
That applies to the brother as [it applies] to the sister. They should have the minimum of knowledge. Everything they will have dealings with. That is what the Muslim should do in general, whether one is in a zawaadj or not. One should take knowledge of everything one has dealings with. Everything that [is] the knowledge of the heart, the deeds, the limbs, the obligatory deeds such as the salaah, [and] the way of the prayer of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, [and] the way of fasting. Then the general deeds such as the zawaadj, buying and selling, clothing, sale contracts, purchase contracts, etc. Everything that is connected to life and about which they should gather knowledge — that should remain continual. Then the worldly knowledge also comes. And one takes that firstly in order to develop the children with it — of course under the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — and also to help each other in married life. That is very important. That one of them has skills in organising, and the other in management and coming up with creative ideas, and the other [has] skills in coming up with solutions, and the other can do more handiwork, and the other can repair [household jobs] more. You try to complement each other by means of the skills you have received. Both the man and the woman.
For when you update [renew] your knowledge in that, you will only gain more benefit in this world and the Hereafter if you use it for the sake of Allaah. And it is important — for the man in particular — that he takes knowledge in order to exercise leadership within the family. He should be knowledgeable about the rights and duties, about his duties, and also about everything that is needed for the children. And the man should also know how he can bring up his wife; because that falls under his responsibility. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will hold him to account for that on the Day of Judgement. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says by the tongue of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam: «طَلَبُ العلم فريضةٌ على كل مسلم» — «Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.»
And one of the important matters that knowledge also brings — besides all the other matters — [is] steadfastness. For knowledge gives you iemaan, especially when you practise it. And iemaan will also help you in married life.
[18] The man and the woman should take knowledge as much as possible and be creative in tarbiyah [the knowledge of upbringing].
[Note: the number «18» is repeated in the original; what is meant is a new point about educational knowledge.] The teacher wants to emphasise this in particular; because many place their focus on the school and the mosque [in the assumption that] they will bring up the children. The man should examine in what way he can develop the educational relationship with his wife and then with his children. And the mother should know how she should have an educational relationship with her children. And the man should accompany [guide] both the wife and the children. And the tarbiyah of the child is always done in cooperation with the woman, but in that the woman should also be accompanied by her husband — although the man [is] the one ultimately responsible. And drawing up an educational plan is a responsibility upon both parents. And [the plan] should be according to Islamic knowledge. And under that we can understand everything — the basis of the relationship in tarbiyah, solving problems, dealing with differences of opinion, [and] everything we will cover in the matters of upbringing: of that both the man and the woman should have knowledge.
For when both — the man and the woman — gather knowledge about this, and then try to practise it together, they are together on [one] path instead of one of them gathering knowledge and the other not. For that ensures a gap. [Or] that one of them does — indeed — want to practise the knowledge and the other says: «No, it is not necessary.» Or what we also sometimes see [is] that one goes and practises and the other says: «No, I do not want to», or «what you people do is far too extreme». In this way the man and the woman grow apart from each other. And it is important that they grow [closer] towards each other by means of the pleasure of Allaah and by means of knowledge.
19) Learn to deal with money/expenses — whereby you buy things for yourself, for your partner and for your children — and also the way in which you spend it.
Very many young people have many debts [because] in their youthful years they dealt badly with money. Therefore it is important that we learn to deal with money. What is the halaal income? The halaal income does not mean an income [where it is only asked]: is the work halaal, [and] that you do not sell bad things, [and] that you do not steal — and then your income is halaal. That is not correct. And this has been discussed several times. For when a person's work depends on something haraam, then his income is not halaal. For example: his work depends on him accepting to shake hands with the opposite sex, otherwise he will not be accepted in that work. Then his income is haraam. Because he accepted that work with the acceptance that he commits a major sin — otherwise he would not be present in that work — his work is then haraam. Or [for example] that he is told that he is not allowed to pray, and he agrees to that — then his work and his income are haraam. And very many people do not think this far. People think: «The product I am dealing with is halaal, I do not steal, so my work is halaal.» That is a deficient way of assessing.
And the sadaqah you spend [has] a priority too. Do you deal with it in the right way or not? These matters are very important in the way of dealing with money. Do you buy — for example — in a halaal way? When did you buy that? On Friday (djumu3ah). At what hour? At half past one. Where did you buy it? From a man. That man should not [was not allowed to] sell to you [at the time of the Friday prayer]. This sale is not permissible, and if you eat that [food], you are eating haraam. And so on. So learn to deal with money. And money is also something that irritates [bothers] many partners and forms many barriers for many people.
20) Make sure that you avoid negativity and remove it from your life.
Negativity leads to a slack [defeatist] attitude. And as has been heard and seen in many ahaadieth, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was never negative. For example, Anas ibn Maalik was a servant/attendant with the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. He was still small, very young, with the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. He says: The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam never blamed me, never asked me «why did you do that?» or «why did you not do that?». He was always positive. This attitude — the bad attitude, the defeatist attitude — is often translated into behaviour [in that] one cries out that one cannot do anything. «I cannot, I did my best.» That [person] is — in reality — saying «I do not want to do it». With that, that [person] consoles himself. You should not [merely] «do your best», rather you should «do it». Bring out the maximum. «ما أمرتُكم به فأتوا منه ما استَطَعتُم» — «What I have commanded you, do of it what you are able.» From that [defeatism] comes the neglect of responsibilities.
And what is very important is that you should not give up. Even if [the matter] does not succeed. [Rather,] continuing in particular. And also when advising your partner. And in that you should ask Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa for help. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «استَعِن بالله ولا تَعجِز» — «Seek help from Allaah and do not give up [do not be helpless].» That means: rely on Allaah, ask Allaah to help you, and make sure that you show your utmost effort. Then you say: «O Allaah, help me», and you go and try again. And this is also connected to the good assumption about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Next week we will speak about the remaining points. And after this comes the chapter of communication in tarbiyah between the spouses.
Questions
Question: The sale — does that also apply if [the seller] is a non-Muslim man on Friday at the time of the Friday prayer?
Answer: Yes, then too. Except when a woman buys from another woman. [Or] a woman buys from a slave, or a woman buys from a sick man. [Question:] Imagine that you are standing in the shop doing groceries, and you come to the checkout [the cashier] — then you should choose that woman [cashier] to pay with, is that correct? Yes.
Question: Is shaking hands with the opposite sex a major sin?
Answer: Yes. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «لأن يُطعَن في رأس أحدكم بمِخْيَطٍ من حديدٍ خيرٌ له من أن يَمَسّ امرأةً لا تَحِلّ له» — «That one of you be stabbed in the head with an iron needle is better for him than that he touch a woman who is not lawful for him.» And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «اليَدان تَزنِيان، وزِناهما البَطشُ» — «The hands commit zinaa (unlawful intimacy), and their zinaa is the grasping [the touching].»
[Question:] How do you determine that it is a major sin?
[Answer:] The scholars set out that the major sins have characteristics. [When] Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa or the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam has attached to the sin — after it or before it — a threat (the anger of Allaah, the curse of Allaah, the Fire, a specific determined punishment, whether in this world or the Hereafter) — then it is a major sin.
[Follow-up question:] So in this hadieth, is the needle that is stabbed into the head the threat?
[Answer:] Yes, the needle you should see as a spear. [It is a major sin] because of the hadieth of the needle, and because it leads to zinaa — but not everything that leads to zinaa is a major sin. For looking at a woman without hidjaab is a minor sin if [the one looking] has no desire for her, [but it is sinful] because he sees an 3awrah. And looking at a woman without hidjaab with feelings and with staring [persistent looking] are more sins, that is, several sins alongside each other. And the looking in itself is a minor sin. And when [the matter] reaches touching, then it is — according to the hadieth — a major sin.
Question: The hadieth of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam in which he says: «O company... whoever tracks down their faults [3awraat], Allaah will track down his faults... [and] disgrace him in his house» — is that a form of «karma»?
Answer: «كما تَدِين تُدان» — «As you deal, so shall you be dealt with» — is a sunnah kawniyyah from Allaah (logic). And it is a correct saying if someone uses it. And [there are] some ahaadieth [in which] he has evidence for it. But «karma» is a Buddhist term. «Karma» comes from Buddhism. [The meaning] comes down to the same thing, but that term we should not use; because it comes from Buddhism and Hinduism. [The meaning] comes down to the same thing. And the Dutch say «a cookie of your own dough [that is: a repayment of the same kind as the deed]», «whoever digs a pit for another falls into it himself».
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «من سَتَر مؤمنًا سَتَره اللهُ» — «Whoever conceals a believer, Allaah will conceal him.» And whoever eases a difficulty for a believer, Allaah will ease for him on the Day of Judgement. And [there is] a hadieth in which «كما تَدِين تُدان» has been declared weak. Ibn al-Haadjdj [and] the Imaam al-Albaanie declared it weak. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿وَإِذَا خَلَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ ۝١٤ ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ Interpretation of the meaning: «And when they are alone with their satans, they say: ‹Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking.› Allaah mocks them.» (Soerat Al-Baqarah, verses 14-15) And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says for example (Soerat Al-Baqarah, verse 40): «And fulfil My covenant, [and] I will fulfil your covenant.» [And in] Soerat Al-Baqarah, verse 152: «So remember Me, [and] I will remember you.» «If you help Allaah, He will help you and make your feet firm.» The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «ارحَموا من في الأرض يَرحَمكم من في السماء» — «Show mercy to those on the earth, and the One in the heaven will show mercy to you.» And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «احفَظِ اللهَ يَحفَظك» — «Guard [the commands of] Allaah, and He will guard you.» And [there are] still very many ahaadieth that set out this meaning.
Question: How can we apply the last point about negativity?
Answer: The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «استَعِن بالله ولا تَعجِز» — «Seek help from Allaah and do not give up.» That is, in short, the summary of how you should do it. That you do not stop at the bad, [that] you seek out the good, continue, and ask Allaah to help you.
