And he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also had humour with his companions. In this way [the matter] remained good between them and they were able to deal with one another in a good manner. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam saw an old female companion (a lady). He said: «يومَ القيامة لن تَدخُلَ العجائزُ الجنّةَ» — «On the Day of Resurrection the old women will not enter the Djannah (the Paradise)». That old woman then walked away weeping. So the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «Make clear to her that people enter the Djannah as youths». He smiled and found it amusing, and he ordered that it be made clear to her that the muslimah (Muslim woman), on the Day of Resurrection, when she enters the Djannah, will be young. Such humour the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam had, and the smile is very important in the tarbiyah. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sent Anas ibn Maalik somewhere, and [Anas said to himself] that he would not do it. Anas saw some children playing along the way and was tempted to play with them. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam then went to check whether he had gone or not. When the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam saw him, he took hold of him by his nape [collar]; Anas looked back and saw the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam smiling at him. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa did not make [the two spouses] partners for one another arbitrarily. It is therefore important that we use this method that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam used.
How can the man act in an optimistic and positive manner towards the woman?
Firstly, it is important that the man knows that an important responsibility rests upon him within the family. We have often explained the hadieth (prophetic narration) in which the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says that the man in his house is the leader over his wife and his children, and that he will be questioned about his responsibility [his flock]. That means, then, that an important task has been entrusted to the man, namely the leadership and the protection of the family. And leadership means: protection, tarbiyah, embracing, that you see matters coming from very far off and then assess whether they are positive or negative; that — before a calamity strikes — you avoid the calamity and form a detour [an alternative route] in which you leave the calamity to your left [you bypass it] and are able — nonetheless — to fulfil your responsibility by protecting your children and your wife.
That means, then, that the man ought to place himself above being a party-mate [an equal] of his wife or his children. For the moment you place yourself as a party-mate [an equal] and you do not have an overview from above [a helicopter view] with which you look at how matters present themselves, develop, and how they can be improved — then you presuppose in advance that your wife and your children are your competitors, your opponents, or your equals [peers], in the sense that they can touch you personally. And when the educator is touched personally, then at that moment you can no longer carry out your task in an objective manner and no longer fulfil your responsibility. The man ought, therefore, not to equate himself with the woman as a party-mate [an equal], nor [to equate himself] with the children either; because he is their educator. That means, then, that we ought also to remove a very important matter that has been planted in us through the incorrect upbringing — the man, the woman and the children — [a matter] of which we ought also to be wary.
And that [matter] is [the claim] that everyone is equal. And the worst is that one goes — on top of that — to say that there is an Islamic foundation for it. And that comes — mostly — [because] one does not understand the texts of the Islamic legislation (the Qur'aan and the Sunnah) in the correct manner, or does not use them in the correct manner in practice. And it is very important that you become acquainted with this poison, acknowledge it, and remove it. No one is equal [to another]. And we have explained before that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa made two forms of rank [ordering]: a form here on earth, and a form with Him in the Djannah. And the form that is with Him in the Djannah depends on taqwaa (godliness/God-consciousness). Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌۭ ۝١٣﴾ [Soerat Al-Hudjuraat: 13]. Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allaah is the one with the most taqwaa. Indeed, Allaah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.» (Soerat Al-Hudjuraat, verse 13). This He says after He created us as men and women and tribes so that we come to know one another. Then He makes clear that the most noble is the one [in whom] the most taqwaa [is present]. In this way, then, we ought to deal with that [person]. And the one [in whom] there is a better 3ibaadah (worship) we ought to love more. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also made another rank that has to do with the order within society, whereby to each was entrusted his own task.
And we explained at that time also that the man received the position above the woman so that the order within the family would be preserved. And Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa did not give the man this position arbitrarily. He was given this position so that he can fulfil his responsibility. What does this mean? It means that the man ought, then, also to act in this manner, and therefore he ought not to be a party-mate [an equal] of his wife. And the mother, too, ought not to see herself as a party-mate [an equal] of her children, nor [to] equate herself with the children. For if that happens — yes — then the pessimism will grow. As in a friendship relationship: the competition grows and the envy grows. And the source of evil is envy. Look [for example] at Iblies (the satan). The origin of pride is envy; because he saw Aadam as a competitor. His envy led him to pride, and his pride led him to the refusal of obedience. At the moment that the hierarchy is preserved, one will look at the matter in a more positive manner. And that applies also from the side of the woman and from the side of the man: one goal, one path, one leader. These are logical laws [sunan] that Allaah made, a cosmic norm. If you go and see them as party-mates [equals], competitors, and you feel the whole time that you are [personally] touched when they do something wrong — then you will lose your authority.
And that does not mean that you ought to act in a haughty manner. And pride is — according to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam —: «بَطَرُ الحقّ وغَمطُ الناس» — «the rejecting [refusing to accept] of the truth and the belittling [looking down upon] of people». When a child advises you, then you ought to accept that; when a child addresses you with the truth, then you ought to accept that. When your wife addresses you with the truth, then you ought to accept that — then you are not haughty.
And belittling is [giving someone] a lower position than that in which Allaah has placed the man. When the woman goes to approach her husband at a lower position, then there is with her [a matter of] pride. That is why it is important that the man does not act in a haughty manner, that is to say [that] he accepts the truth, even if this truth comes from his wife, just as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also did with Hafsah, and Umm Salamah, and 3Aa-ishah; and that he does not belittle them, [and does] not place them beneath their level, for example that he goes to treat his wife like his children. Or that he goes to treat his wife in a manner that Allaah does not permit, [by] insulting her, going to revile her [speak ill of her], and displaying evil every time. That is not permitted and is a form of pride. Make sure that you place yourself as an educator and do not equate yourself with your wife and children, but you ought — yes — to approach them with goodness and sincerity and as Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also prescribed.
And it is part of the fitrah (natural disposition) of the woman that she wants to be led. Most women have received from their fitrah that they want to be led. When the man fulfils his role as educator, his responsibility is realized. And this applies also to the upbringing of the child. When the child does not respond after long admonition, then you ought not to cast him off by saying «that child is no longer my child»; no, you ought — nonetheless — to try to raise him in the correct manner and take him into the whole [include him]. And if you are not able to do so, then it is important that you check that someone else has the possibility for it. And it remains your responsibility as a father to raise him.
Preserve your optimism and hold on to it by acting as an educator who seeks out solutions. Utter beautiful words instead of bad words, and do not complain about people. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «إذا قال الرجلُ هَلَك الناسُ فهو أَهلَكُهم» — «When the man says: the people have perished, then he is the most ruined of them» — and in another narration «فهو أَهلَكَهم» — «then he has ruined them». «You are cursed, you are worth nothing, you will never do well» etc. With this you ensure that you destroy the people, destroy the relationship with that [person], and destroy yourself. That is not tarbiyah, but a form of weakness. If you do that, then you ensure that the one who is with you — that is, your wife — subsequently behaves [in such a way that] she gives up hope [despairs] or [that] she becomes more rebellious; because she says «no, I will show you precisely that I endure him and that I am better than him». Then [the matter] works in reverse, and you are not busy building a stable marriage. And this applies also to the relationship towards your father/mother, in order to remain positive in it. And it is important that you utter beautiful words with which you can lead people to a solution. For when you — as an educator — insult [and] provoke, then on the long term you will not be taken seriously.
Make sure that there is [with you] positive communication, as we also learned in the hadieth of 3Aa-ishah and in the hadieth of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam («غارت أمُّكم» — «Your mother became jealous» — and he went on [with his account]). When you are angry, seek your refuge with Allaah. In this manner you remind your wife of Allaah and say «a3oedhu billaahi mina-shshaytaani-rradjiem» (I seek refuge with Allaah from the accursed satan) and you perform a du3aa-e (supplication) for her (may Allaah guide you, may Allaah forgive you, may Allaah make our love increase for His sake, may Allaah provide you with the best). You place your hand on your heart and say «may Allaah forgive you, may Allaah love you», instead of that you beforehand [and] in advance go to act with anger and let matters escalate even further. And when you see that she is a little rebellious, [then] showing your muscles [strength] is not needed for anything. Make sure that you use the gentle approach; because that leads you to her heart.
As the Arabs say: «الكلمةُ الطيّبة تُخرِج الحَيّةَ من جُحرها» — «The good word draws the snake out of its hole». They mean thereby that even if it is a venomous snake, it will draw near to you through the beautiful words.
And especially when you also go to use your hands — not to use violence, but — for example — to stroke over her head or to seek closeness to your wife in another manly manner. Thereby she too will calm down, come to rest, and not make herself even angrier; because when the woman sees that her husband sincerely loves her, she will also improve herself in a sincere manner. You also calm her by embracing her despite that she is angry, whereupon she melts [softens] in your hands. Make sure that you think in a solution-oriented manner, and do not go along [be carried away] with her frustration. Many women who fall into frustration say — in reality —: «My husband, I love you, I want you to give me attention; because if you do not give me attention, I will go and demand the attention [compellingly]». She is — in reality — being coquettish and wants your attention and love.
And in principle, if the man understands his wife well, then he will only be positive and will deal with his wife with sincerity alone. And then he also has his wife in his hand, and does not need to become angry every day.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «لا يَفرَك مؤمنٌ مؤمنةً، إن كَرِه منها خُلُقًا رَضِيَ منها آخر» — «Let a believing man not hate [detest] a believing woman: if he detests a character trait of hers, then he is pleased with another [trait] of hers». Make sure, then, that that other behaviour that you love — that you take it as an opportunity to reach through to her in order to remove her bad behaviour, and make clear to her also: «No, my beloved wife, you are not like this, you are much better than this. Deep in your heart you too want the good, may Allaah love you, I know that you love Allaah; let us calm down and come to rest and then speak about it afterwards». He is sincere and knows how he can speak in a positive manner, instead of frustrating himself [and saying] «who do you think you are? You are my wife and you ought to obey me». That is true, but you do not do it in this manner.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «المرأةُ خُلِقت من ضِلَعٍ، وأَعوَجُ ما في الضِّلَع أَعلاه. فإن ذَهَبتَ تُحاوِل أن تُقيمه كَسَرتَه، وإن تَرَكتَه بَقِيَ أَعوَجَ دائمًا» — «The woman was created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its uppermost. If you go and try to straighten it, you break it, and if you leave it, it always remains crooked». The Sunnah is thus a practical matter. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam makes clear here that if he wants to set matters straight, that ought to happen in a gentle manner (you bring her back a little and then leave her [be]). And sometimes [for that] months or years are needed. And among the matters that the educator ought to know is that he ought always to expect mistakes, and he ought not to think that everything will come right of its own accord. And we will also learn how we ought to raise [children]. Make sure — as a man — that you are gentle and set matters straight step by step. And complete straightening is impossible; because she is a woman and you are a man. And the man too has shortcomings. And the man and the woman ought to complement one another. And that you do in a positive manner.
How can the woman act in an optimistic manner towards her husband?
When the woman acts as a woman, not [in a] provocative [manner], and she does not go and act as a man. Not that the women say «I will no longer cancel myself out [sacrifice myself]» etc. We have spoken several times about where this leads. The woman ought to act as a woman, with hayaa-e (proper modesty/bashfulness), humility and submissiveness. All the wonderful qualities the kuffaar (disbelievers) have — unfortunately — caused to be removed. So many women today are not women but mannish women. Women who [know] nothing but rebellion, [know] nothing but saying «no», [know] nothing but arguing. A woman 50 years ago would be ashamed to argue with a strange man, and especially with her husband. But now we argue with our husbands and with strange men, and we go and raise our voices even towards strange men. And some sisters wear the niqaab (face veil) and act as though they are engaged in da3wah. We ought to act in a humble manner.
And a very important matter (for the man and the woman) is that they acknowledge their mistakes. And it is one of the qualities that can save you in this world and the Hereafter. And acknowledging mistakes is a sign of humility, [a sign of] someone sincere who wants to improve his mistakes. And Allaah loves the acknowledgement of mistakes.
[The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam mentions] that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam brings out a man from among all the creatures, and He brings out for him 99 registers [archives], all of them filled with evil [sins]. And in each register are 99 files [irrespective of the exact wording; in the authentic hadieth: the register is as far as the eye can reach, and it is cited here as it appears in the original]. And when one of these files is opened, papers spread out from it far off as far as the sight reaches. How many are the bad deeds of this man! He is full of bad deeds. And this man will not have any good deed. So Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says to him: «Did Our scribes [recorders] wrong you? (No) Did Our scribes forget anything? (No) Do you acknowledge what you did? (Yes) Did you perform any good deed? (No)». Then Allaah says: «Today you will not be wronged». Then a card is brought out on which is written «Laa ilaaha illa-llaah» [there is no deity worthy of worship except Allaah]. «Take this with all your files». What will this card do with these files? The servant acknowledges, submissive despite that he committed mistakes. So Allaah weighs this card and weighs the 99 registers. And this card turns out to be much heavier than the 99 registers; because he was submissive.
And also another man gathers his sons before he dies. He says: if I die, then you ought to burn me and divide me into four [parts]: a part in the south, and the west, and the east, and the north. So his children do what he says. Then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa resurrects him and asks him: what made you request this from your children? He — in reality — by his deed thought that Allaah would not be able to gather him. And that is — in reality — a form of major disbelief [the greatest kufr]. So he said to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa: «Fear of You [my fear of You]». That means, then, that he too acknowledges his mistakes. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «من نُوقِش الحِسابَ عُذِّب» — «Whoever is examined closely in the reckoning is punished». So on the one hand we saw people who are not punished despite that they committed the greatest of major sins, simply because they acknowledge. And whoever contends over his reckoning will be punished. And that [is] the one who will deny («no, I did not do it, I did not intend it like that, I did it but I intended something other than that» — the one who keeps arguing and does not acknowledge). So likewise that [person] will come with such a quality on the Day of Resurrection. For whoever in this world was accustomed to such a quality will also die upon it. And in the end his mouth will be sealed, and his hands and his feet and his ears and his eyes will speak and testify against him, whereupon he says afterwards: «Away with you [woe to you], I only wanted to defend you». What was his point [his problem]? His point is that he did not acknowledge. And therefore [acknowledgement] is one of the worst qualities that one can have in this world — that one does not acknowledge one's mistake. When someone does not acknowledge his mistake (and especially the woman), then that leads to a family that will end up in nothing but problems; because the problems will only increase. And when the woman acknowledges her mistakes, then that leads to a family that removes the mistakes and is optimistic and solves the problems in a good manner.
Acknowledge your mistake, do not be rebellious, do not go and provoke, do not go and dig up the old issues. The old mistakes that have been resolved you ought not to bring up, and enter [dwell] in your husband's lived world [share in his feeling]. Do not go and dream in your own world; because then you will not be optimistic but you will only be pessimistic.
Questions
Question: What do you mean by «provocation»?
The answer: Every matter that inflames [stirs up] another, that is provocation. And mostly we make the mistakes, [but] whether it is [behaviour] that is provocative or not — the other determines whether it is provocative behaviour or not. He is provoked. And the matter is [connected] to his pleasure/consent. Many women say «it is his problem, he is the one who becomes angry over that». No, it is your problem. Do not go and determine for them whether they become angry (for example the parents). For then you have a problem, so you ought to keep them content. We do not go and determine for the other whether the other becomes angry or not. And that too is humility. For when we go and determine that for another [who has] authority over us, then that is a form of pride and haughtiness.
Question: You explained that there ought to be humour in the tarbiyah, and also between the two partners. Is there a limit in the humour also between the two partners with one another, or is that limit the pleasure of Allaah?
The answer: The limit in the humour is what falls within the pleasure of Allaah. What falls within the pleasure? That one places the other in his position. That [one] does not go and treat the other in a manner by which he is brought down [belittled]. An example: that you say to your parents «you have nothing to do [with this]», or that you say to your husband «mind your own business [do not interfere]». Those are not jokes [jesting]. That exceeds all bounds. For these are jokes that place the others beneath their position. Do not go and make with people whom you do not know jokes that place them beneath their position. And your knowing your parents, [and] your husband, does not [mean] that the limits of humour are without limits. Humour was never without limits. For when one exceeds the limit in humour, then he is engaged in [a matter] that is unjust. [And the opposite of that is] that one is just. You can make many jokes with your parents and many jokes with your husband, but the position ought to be preserved.
[For example] that the woman suddenly gives her husband a kick and then the woman says «haha, it is a joke». Many men are not able to endure that as a joke. So that indicates that your reverence for your husband is not present, and that you use the joke as a pretext. For if the position [standing] of your husband were present in your heart, you would not be able to do that yourself. And you ought to revere your husband more than your father. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam did not give the father the same position as [he gave] the husband. So the position of the man is higher than the position of the father. You ought to accustom [yourself to] the position of the father so that you give your husband a still higher position. And the limits of good behaviour and the religion remain preserved in humour.
Question: How can the woman ask for her husband's attention in a good manner?
The answer: [There are] different ways. You ought to make [the matter] simple for yourself. When the woman in her early days is in love with her husband and the man [in love] with his wife — how do they deal with one another, and how does each of them draw the other's attention? In various pleasant ways in which there is much hayaa-e [bashfulness] between them with one another, whereby [the matter] is also pleasant. It is in this manner that the two partners ought to deal with one another. «I would — in reality — pay attention to how I looked, I would then pay attention to how [my] facial expressions were». How can she seek closeness to her husband — it can be in a sexual manner, [or] in a loving manner with touches on his head, his shoulders. As a woman you can touch your husband everywhere. And it can be the other way around too. But also [it can be] by addressing him by his position as her leader, someone — for example — whom Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa made a joy in her life, a delight, someone [who is] a blessing for her. And that you go and praise your husband, and think about what he loves and give it to him without his asking for it. And the best way is humility. That she goes and practises her femininity sincerely. This is very [brief], we will speak about it much, in shaa-a Allaah.
Question: The meaning of belittling is that you give someone a lower position than that which Allaah has assigned to him. What is the Islamic ruling on a person to whom you give a higher position than that which Allaah has assigned to him? For example a disbeliever to whom you give a higher position than that which Allaah gave him.
The answer: That is a broad concept, [it may range] from [being] a good deed to leaving Islam. For if you give someone a higher position than what is his, then it can be [that this is] a good deed by which you call him to Islam. And it can also be that you venerate him with such veneration that it becomes shirk (associating partners with Allaah) or kufr (disbelief), so that thereby that [person] leaves Islam. And it can also lead to your wronging someone, wronging a Muslim. And the disbeliever it is not permitted to honour [revere] from your heart. That is not permitted. And the disbeliever is always lower than the lowest Muslim. So the greatest criminal who says «Laa ilaaha illa-llaah» is better than a disbeliever. [And] it is permitted — yes — to treat him with good treatment. [The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sent a letter] to the emperor of the Romans. He said to him: «From Muhammad sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam to the great one of the Romans». The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam never saw that he was a great person, but he is seen among the Romans as a great person. So he gave him the position that the Romans [gave him]. For a Muslim's honouring [revering] a disbeliever is beforehand a sin. That means, then, that he gives him a position — and that is [a] dangerous [matter] — [such that] he will accept from him matters that contradict Islam etc.
Question: «The people have perished [someone said], so they have perished [or: so he has ruined them]». Many people in our time say «the ummah has gone astray, humanity is such and such». Is that the same [matter]?
The answer: That is the same [matter]. It is not permitted for you to say it. It is permitted — yes — for you to say «some Muslims do that, a dangerous thought prevails among the Muslims». But that you say «the ummah has perished, the ummah is such» — [the one who says that] has himself perished within himself, so he has perished, and in another narration he has ruined them. You ought to remain objective, do not generalize.
Question: The qualities that one has in this world — does that mean that certain personalities that one has [will be such] that he will act like this with his personal qualities [in the Hereafter]?
The answer: Yes. If we look well at the hadieth of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, we see that when the two angels seat the dead person and ask him «who is your Lord?» he says «huh, huh? I do not know». The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says about this person: «I heard the people saying something and I said it [I imitated them]». So in the Hereafter you will be more truthful in your qualities. [Whereas] here you can use your tongue to whitewash [justify] yourself. For if those people are able to console themselves [calm themselves], then their consciences are far off [absent].
23) Make sure that you are aware of your mistakes.
What does «that you are aware of your mistakes» mean? It means, firstly, that you — in general — are a maker of mistakes [prone to error]. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «كلُّ بني آدمَ خَطّاؤون، وخيرُ الخَطّائين التوّابون» — «All the sons of Aadam are makers of mistakes, and the best of the makers of mistakes are those who repent». That means, then, that you ought never to whitewash [justify] yourself of mistakes.
And secondly, among what falls under that is that you know your weakness. That means, then, that you also know which weak qualities you possess, and where the shaytaan can also penetrate, that is [where] he can misuse it to steer [direct] you by it. So you go and strengthen yourself in that, you ask Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa for help so that He protects you from these points of weakness and improves you, but [also] that you know what are the roots of your points of weakness and your mistakes. Which inspiration [prompting] enticed you to those mistakes, and what it is that you saw or heard [by which] you were seduced to that mistake — so that you remove all that enticed you or led you astray to this mistake. And it can also be [that it is] an incorrect thought, or [a thought] that you think is correct while it is incorrect.
And therefore you ought to go [with that] also to people of knowledge. For when you ask people of knowledge about your mistakes, it is important that you make clear to them with what thought you made this mistake or carried out this matter, so that the person of knowledge also improves you in your thought. For many mistakes begin with an incorrect thought, and the incorrect thought leads to an incorrect belief, and the incorrect belief leads to an incorrect love, and the incorrect love leads to incorrect deeds. And therefore it is important that you are aware of your mistakes down to the roots, and that you reflect on that much. For in this manner you reach a solution faster; because if you do not reflect on that [you do not reach it]. And your knowing yourself is the best way to reach a solution.
And it is important — alongside that — that you are accustomed to blame yourself. And your blaming yourself reduces [the likelihood] that you blame another. And people often say «you did this, you did that», and the other also says «you, you», but no one speaks about himself. No one acknowledges his mistake and is aware of his mistake. And blaming yourself is a form of worship.
In a hadieth of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam that has been authenticated, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «خيرُ نسائكم الوَدودُ الوَلودُ العَؤودُ» — «The best of your women is the loving one, the fertile one, the devoted one [the caring one]». [It was said:] O Messenger of Allaah, who is the devoted one? «She is the woman who, when she has wronged or been wronged, says to her husband: this is my hand in your hand, I will not taste [sleep] until you are pleased with me».
So the woman who wrongs her husband or is wronged by her husband says: «This is my hand in your hand, I will not taste [sleep] until you are pleased with me». That means, then, that the best of women is the woman who blames herself. And if that is the best woman, then that itself indicates that that [is] the best man [too]. And the woman refuses — more than the man — to acknowledge her mistake.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam speaks — mostly — according to who possesses a quality more, but that does not mean that others are not addressed. And that quality in question is a bad quality. And sometimes a quality presents itself more with the woman or more with the man, and therefore the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sometimes speaks about the man only or about the woman only; because it presents itself with the men or the women more.
So if [the woman] displays this behaviour then she belongs to the best of behaviour. And despite that she is wronged (the man [is] the guilty one), why does the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam — nonetheless — say about her that she belongs to the best of women? The position of the man is that he is a leader and an educator. And the position of the woman in relation to the man [is that she is] his other half, and the one who is raised, and the one who also falls under his authority. So if she acts in this manner and has patience and sincerely wanted the pleasure of her husband — what is the logical consequence that happens to her family? What happens to her husband then? Does he become more inflamed or does he calm down? He calms down. Will he become angrier or calmer? He becomes calmer. And if he becomes calmer and level-headed and is a good person, what will he do? Will he acknowledge his mistake and show remorse, or [will he be] haughty and wrong her even more? For if he is a person who refuses to acknowledge and show remorse, then what has the woman gained by that in any case? In any case the pleasure of Allaah, [and] she performed her duty towards her husband, [and] she did not make the man angrier, [and] she did not make the wrong greater. The wrong occurred. You can choose to make the wrong even greater, or choose to calm it or reduce it. So if you sincerely stopped, [and] you were wronged and he did not offer an apology — is that better, or [is it better] that he becomes angrier? And if the children see that she is sincere and humble, what happens to the children then? The children will follow her example and preserve her position towards them and preserve the position of the family, they will respect her and love her more, and respect their father too and love him.
So by that she has gained her reward and belongs to the best of women, and she looked after the stability of the marriage which is also her duty. And she did not let [anyone] trample her [belittle her], and she is with Allaah — at that moment — better even than her husband; because her taqwaa at that moment is better. She did not help the plan of the shaytaan. But if she — as the kuffaar say — stands up for herself [claims her rights], goes and screams, insults, and shows who [is] the master — then everything happens that contradicts what the teacher just mentioned, and she is [then] engaged in standing up for the shaytaan and has — in reality — deceived herself.
When the man insults the woman she says: «My beloved husband, the wonderful one, my leader, I love you. May Allaah forgive me and you. Do you think that Allaah will be pleased with this? I will do everything you want. I only want you to be pleased with me. I do not want Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa to see my beloved husband and hear him in this manner». So if the man hears these words, what will he do? His heart will soften.
We ought always to think well of Allaah; because Allaah [holds] his heart in His hand. And sometimes you ought not to admonish, not [to] begin with his mistake. Say that you only want him to be pleased with you. Do not go and speak about his mistake at that moment. That means, then, that when you [admonish him] at that moment while he is angry and the shaytaan is engaged in [his work] [in that] he is not level-headed, then he will not listen to your admonition. He will listen — yes — because you calm him and place him in his position, but you ought not to do it [merely] to calm him but to sincerely mean it too. And all the cases that the teacher has been through, he has not seen in them a single case in which the man remains angry if the woman acts like this.
It is important, when we communicate, that we are positive in our communication. If you say «it will become hard, difficult», then that is not positive, and our lesson is about positivity. You ought to say «Allaah will teach me that in shaa-a Allaah». The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «استَعِن بالله ولا تَعجِز» — «Seek help with Allaah and do not fall short [become incapable]». One of the female teachers said to her female students: «Do not say ‹I cannot›. Say ‹I will do it›» — and she was a disbeliever. And regardless of that, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam [explained] how we ought to act in that. We ought to think much farther than [the length of] our nose. For if you do not go and learn this habit with your parents, then you will not learn such a habit with your husband [as though you are trying to shift a rock]. But when you do that several times, and especially with your parents [because they are the ones you revere], then [the matter] will become easy. It is perhaps [a] good [thing] that we say this tonight to our parents/spouses, and that you do it with a sincere intention for the sake of Allaah. That you say «I want you to be pleased with me. I want that in order to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa».
The awareness of your mistakes is that you improve yourself and work on that. You will one day stand before Allaah. So at that moment you hope intensely that you were able to say these words from your heart in this world. [Otherwise] then [the matter] is too late.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: ﴿أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۝٣٨﴾ [Soerat An-Nadjm: 38]. Interpretation of the meaning: «That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.» No one will bear the burden of another. Each will be recompensed for what he did. Then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «And that man shall have nothing except what he strove for. And that his striving will be seen. Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense.»
Make sure that you are aware of your mistakes, and that you place yourself in a humble manner.
We have spoken about patience. And the first step of patience is that you force yourself to perform that deed. And the second step is the repetition of that forcing, forcing yourself repeatedly. Begin by doing the first step, and the second step is the repeated forcing to utter these words. And the first step to utter these words is that you know how high the position of your husband is, and for whoever is not yet married, how high the position of your parents is. And that these words are also a 3ibaadah towards the parents. When you utter these words, you will cast off much burden from yourself. You will attain much rest.
Ask: «Are you pleased with me, mother? Are you pleased with me, father? Are you pleased with me, my husband?». That you ask this every three days. Your world during marriage is that you occupy yourself with the pleasure of your husband [which follows the pleasure of Allaah]. At that moment these people, these destroyers, the kuffaar, will be very envious of you, [then] they have hasad (envy) towards you; because they do not want you to become a good person. That Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in the Qur'aan. We ought not to think that these kuffaar want the best for us. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa makes clear in the Qur'aan that these people do not wish us a single speck of good.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says [interpretation of the meaning]: «Many of the People of the Book wished that they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief, out of envy from within themselves.» So those are People of a Book who are close to us. So how is it then with atheistic, satanic people etc.? Make sure that you are aware of your mistakes, and that you improve yourself; because you will — in the end — only be recompensed for what you do.
24) Make sure that you perform good deeds together with your partner.
When you engage in good deeds together, you invest in a good bond with one another, and moreover you invest in your relationship with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And when you both invest together in your relationship with Allaah, then Allaah will also make you love one another more for His sake. And besides that, you invest then for the sake of Allaah in a good bond with one another. And with regard to the priorities in the relationship that you ought to work on, you begin with the relationship with Allaah, then with the relationship — which depends on Allaah — with one another as partners, then with the relationship with your children.
When you perform good deeds together, love arises, a pure, sincere love, and affection for the sake of Allaah for one another; because in this manner you come to know one another more, and also come to know one another's thoughts more. And in this manner you also form a team in the correct manner.
Who can mention to me what good deeds you can perform together? Testing [reciting] the Qur'aan to one another, spending charity, sexual intercourse for the sake of Allaah, fasting, beginning together a project with which you complement one another. [There are] many marriages that arose — in reality — in this manner too, and much splendour came out of them. You see two partners who complement one another. That is beautiful. Many students of the knowledge of Islam have this. You see that these students complement one another in what they do. The man does something, and the woman does the same thing, and they go and complement one another in that. A wonderful blessing from Allaah in which both partners do matters for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. For there is no greater blessing than that you two together perform da3wah.
And a concrete example [is] — for instance — that one of you has the leadership over the project and the other the coordination of the project. That one of you has — for example — organizational, Islamic knowledge, and the other administrative knowledge. In this way they go and complement one another. For example founding an orphanage, establishing an Islamic school. Then it is important that they look at one another's skills.
25) Make sure that you involve yourself in your partner's hobby.
Often the man has no time and the woman also has no time. A father who was busy, was married to a mother who was busy, and they were granted a child that had no time for them. When you two have no time for one another, the children will also not be interested in you, and vice versa. You ought to be interested in one another's hobbies. In this way you can help one another and steer [guide] one another in the hobbies. Some men — because they are interested in their wives' hobbies — learn cooking, sewing, knitting. And other men think «what have I to do with this, I am a man». [Yet] the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam stitched his own sandal.
And regardless of that, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also played with 3Aa-ishah radiyallaahu 3anhaa. So that is a relationship you can create. Also in a playful [merry] manner.
What is a hobby?
The hobby shows what the ambition of such a person is, and what his potential is, and what the opportunities are to approach him. When you are not interested in your partner's hobby, then you also do not want to get to know him. And especially the man ought to be interested in his wife's hobby; because he ought to steer her towards the good. And as an educator, it is important that you show interest in the one you are raising so that he too shows interest in what you ask of him. In this way you also learn what and how the other is influenced, and by what he is influenced, and in this way you can steer the tarbiyah. And when the woman has the idea that the man is interested in her hobby, the woman feels her husband's love, [and] his attachment [to her], and in this manner she feels appreciated, and that makes a wonderful man.
Next week we will complete some points, and then we will begin another beautiful chapter, namely communication and tarbiyah between the two spouses.
Questions
Question: [There occurred] in this lesson some [inspiring] sayings, such as «The good word draws the snake out of its hole» and «It is never permitted for you to lose your patience until you have completed the years of Noeh». Do I have permission to share these sayings with others?
The answer: [The teacher said jokingly:] A busy man marries a busy woman and they are granted a child that had no time for them — on the one hand amusing, and on the other hand very indicative of reality. Yes, these sayings may be shared.
Question: Can you briefly address the society that gives us a different image of the successful woman? You have done that several times, but in view of today's lesson?
The answer: When you think about the society in which we live, you ought to know that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam spoke [about it]. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «سيأتي على الناس سنواتٌ خَدّاعاتٌ، يُكَذَّب فيها الصادقُ ويُصَدَّق فيها الكاذبُ، ويُؤتَمَن فيها الخائنُ ويُخَوَّن فيها الأمينُ» — «There will come over the people deceitful years, in which the truthful one is disbelieved and the liar is believed, and in which the traitor is trusted and the trustworthy one is treated as a traitor». In this time the scales have been turned. The bad [has become] good and the good [has become] bad. And the normal — which the people used to sense as good — is now turned into a taboo [forbidden]. And what [was] a taboo is turned [made] normal. Look [for example] at what we now say about the woman, about the manner in which she stands up for herself, about mutual respect, about equality. With very many Muslims [it has become the case that] very many of these matters are normal. «There is no harm in it, this is how the world is anyway». And the worst is that some Muslims see this as Islamic principles and values. And the worst [still] is that some people present for that — supposedly — (distorted) evidence from the Qur'aan and the Sunnah. In this way the shaytaan plays with the people. We ought always to remain — sincerely — performing a beautiful du3aa-e to see the truth as truth: «اللهمّ أَرِنا الحقَّ حقًّا وارزُقنا اتِّباعَه، وأَرِنا الباطلَ باطلًا وارزُقنا اجتنابَه» — «O Allaah, show us the truth as truth and grant us the following of it, and show us the falsehood as falsehood and grant us the avoidance of it».
In this time you ought to be wary and distinguish between pure Islam and Islamized thought. And that latter is when they take the thought of the kuffaar and their theories, embellish them, paste and cut them, and then say «this is Islam, this is the Islamic tarbiyah». [A] dangerous [matter], we ought to be wary of it.
Perform much the du3aa-e: «O Allaah, show us the truth as truth and grant us the following of it, and show us the falsehood as falsehood and grant us the avoidance of it».
Question: Are there still some means that you advise/recommend for remaining steadfast?
The answer: Keep in general gathering knowledge, but among the matters that you do: go and look at how the female companions were in the time of the Prophet. That you can find among the companions of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam or the women around the Prophet (some of the ahaadieth about them are weak), so you ought to inquire whether the hadieth in question is authentic or not. Read much about the wives of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. For however dreadful the society is now — [by which] you can be seduced — go back to [what was] 80, 90, 100 years ago. How was the society here? The kuffaar here had to be received in camps to learn how they ought to wash themselves, relieve themselves, how they ought to wash their hands, how they ought to learn the etiquette of eating, before they even received any assistance. And 90 years ago the Europeans thought that the woman was another creature. They were investigating whether the woman is a human, an animal, or another creature. So if you look at our wonderful history, you know how much this religion honoured the woman. And the booklet «O my sister, this is how Allaah and His Messenger want you [to be]» — the ustaadh advises everyone to acquire it and read it every six months. It is a beautiful book [about] how the muslimah ought to behave.
And it is important — as a woman — that you work as little as possible among these people [the kuffaar]. So if it is possible not to work among them, then do not do so. Thereby you will be better in the marriage for your husband and children. And the ustaadh advises everyone not to work among these people, whatever the work and however much [you gain] of money for it. It is better to be poor than to work among these people. And Allaah knows best.
The homework
Organize your notes.
Make sure that you say this sentence that we have addressed — to show your humility and your submissiveness towards the one who [has] authority over you — at least twice or three times this week to your parents if you are not married, and to your husband if you are married. Say this tonight to your parents/husband with a sincere intention that you want to please your parents/husband for the sake of Allaah. That you say: «I want you to be pleased with me. I want that in order to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa».
What we addressed last week [applies to] this week but with the new points: that you check yourself and improve yourself with regard to the new points.
The thirty-eighth lesson — Sunday 25 November 2018
The homework (11 November)
Organize your notes.
Make sure that you say this sentence that we have addressed — to show your humility and your submissiveness towards the one who [has] authority over you — at least twice or three times this week to your parents if you are not married, and to your husband if you are married. Say this tonight to your parents/husband with a sincere intention that you want to please your parents/husband for the sake of Allaah. That you say that you want them to be pleased with you, and that you want that in order to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
«I want you to be pleased with me. I want that in order to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.»
What we addressed last week [applies to] this week but with the new points: that you check yourself and improve yourself with regard to the new points.
Discussion of the homework (25 November)
Experience of student 1
The sister tried to pay attention to her behaviour at home. There was a point [namely] that you are aware of your mistakes. With the sister [it happens] sometimes that she answers her parents in an irritated [annoyed] manner. And she then offered an apology afterwards.
The ustaadh: With regard to the task «make sure that you say the sentence twice or three times a week» — what did you do with that?
The sister: I did not apply it.
The ustaadh: May I ask why?
The sister: You can always bring it up. I find [the matter] a little... not that I am ashamed, but it is not something that goes in a natural [spontaneous] manner. I do say it — yes — but not with these words. In a slightly different manner, I think. If there is — for example — a gathering or whatever with the family, then I say: «Do you see [that] things are going well? Do you need anything?». [I lean] a little more towards the side of care [caregiving]. Not that I, as a person, am in her eyes good or [whatever].
The ustaadh: We addressed [the point] that when you are not accustomed to say something — which steps you ought to take to make it a habit. What ought you to do?
The sister: You admonish yourself. You take a measure [set to work].
The ustaadh: We said that that has to do with patience, [namely] that you force yourself and that you accustom yourself / do it more to say that. [There is] a big difference between «is everything going well, do you still need help?» and «I want you to be pleased with me in order to please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa». Or that you say something more still, for example: «You are my wonderful parents, may Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa care for you, may Allaah help me to please you». That differs from saying «do you need help?». For with that [latter] you do not need to show a form of submissiveness. That you say «I will not show myself in that manner, I will — yes — say: do you need anything». [And] it can also be that [the one who says] that is a person [who is] the master over another, [that is] he has a form of arrogance. And the manner in which we communicate has a direct relation with the posture [attitude] and the behaviour that we display and radiate. Towards the one who [has] authority over us, you ought to radiate that you are beneath him or that he needs you. If you say «do you need anything?», then you ask whether he needs anything. [Whereas the reality is that] you need him. And that is the same in dealing with the poor. We need the poor, the poor do not need us. The poor do not need us. We need the poor to invest in our good deeds. They do not need us; because Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will provide for them in any case, whether that is through us or through someone else. And a person's radiance can differ.
The ustaadh: So for next week — in reality [as of] tonight — we will agree that you — nonetheless — say this phrase, or — for example — perform the supplications. That you radiate gratitude. That you say «You are my parents, you are wonderful, may Allaah reward you. I want very much to please you in order to please Allaah».
Experience of student 2
With regard to the sentence [asking] that they be pleased with her. In the case of the sister [with] her mother. She found [the matter] difficult to ask her [it]. [There is] a bit of a culture of bashfulness, but she — nonetheless — overcame [the matter]. She knows that her mother likes to tell what she went through in the old days in Morocco. So after the lesson the sister asked about her life in the old days, what she went through etc. She went through difficult times. So the sister went and made use of that [took it as a starting point]. «We — yes — [are] well.» The sister asked: «Are you pleased with our behaviour towards you and the things we do for you?». She said: «Yes». Then when the sister asked about her [herself] she asked: «Are you pleased with me?». Then she finally said sincerely: «Yes». The sister knows that her mother is sometimes annoyed with the sister. The sister agreed [with herself] [not] to sleep until around 11 o'clock. So the sister sleeps therefore until 9 at the most and then gets up. If the sister has a day off, then she can — yes — sleep until around 11 o'clock. She did that [in such a way] that she did not do it [that is: she controlled herself]. She slept once until 11 o'clock and feared that her mother's pleasure had disappeared. Has the pleasure now disappeared? [The mother] said that she is very annoyed. She can become very angry about that.
The ustaadh: When you receive a task, do not say «we do this as a task [an assignment] from the teacher». For two reasons:
So that the reaction is not built upon that.
[Because] in any case you ought not to do this matter as a task for the teacher but as an improvement for yourself. You ought to do it of your own accord. And what the ustaadh tries to do is that he tries to motivate us towards improvement, towards improvement from the Qur'aan and the Sunnah. We want to improve ourselves, re-raise ourselves, take ourselves [in hand] anew [correct ourselves].
For these two reasons it is not correct to say «the teacher asked me». For the answer ought namely not to be influenceable by that. «This is a matter that I myself believe in, am convinced of, and what I myself want is that you are truly pleased with me.» For when you go and ask [on the pretext] that the teacher says [so], then it is from your side another context and she will understand it from another context. «I as your daughter want you to be pleased with me.» Otherwise it seems as though you are being forced. We want to make this [matter] our own [internalize it].
Experience of student 3
«I — a week before we received the task — went and observed what I can do better to please my husband. I made clear to him that I see him as my king, and that I appreciate him very greatly. And that I realize that many responsibilities rest upon him as a man, and that I appreciate that greatly, such as helping him with the household chores while he does not have to do that.»
